x.Q0001:
The amber GPS light has two meanings. Steady on its own = BOTH GPS sensor units failed. Seen only when you push the annunciator for RECALL, and gone again after Master Caution reset = only ONE GPS unit has failed. That is a single failure, so the aircraft still has GPS from the other unit. The same logic applies to the ILS and GLS lights on the same panel.
Hook: "Recall only = one; always on = both."
x.Q0002:
FCOM 12.20.2 'Suction Feed': 'When main tank fuel pump pressure is low, each engine can draw fuel from its corresponding main tank through a suction feed line that bypasses the pumps.' On the schematic (12.20.5) this is the ENGINE BYPASS VALVE in each main tank. So No 1 engine keeps running on fuel from the No 1 tank, sucked by its engine-driven pump through the bypass. It does NOT flame out. At high altitude suction feed may not be able to give full thrust (air comes out of the fuel).
Hook: "Both pumps dead → engine sucks through the bypass."
x.Q0003:
FCOM 12.20.3: the centre tank scavenge jet pump (with No 1 FWD pump switch ON) moves the last centre-tank fuel into main tank No 1, and 'Fuel transfer begins when main tank No. 1 quantity is about one-half.' Once started, it continues for the rest of the flight.
Hook: "Tank 1 half empty → scavenge starts."
x.Q0004:
The green EXT TEST lights only prove that the electrical circuit to the discharge squib (the small explosive cartridge that fires the bottle) has continuity. They do NOT test the bottle contents, the fire switches or the detection loops. On the engine/APU panel, EXT TEST 1 checks engine 1 + APU squibs, position 2 checks engine 2 + APU. On the cargo panel, pushing TEST lights the green lights if the squib circuits are good.
Hook: "Green = wire to the squib is OK."
x.Q0005:
FCOM 5.20.3: ALT–NORM to ALT = DEGRADED mode: 'the ACP at that station is inoperative and the crewmember can only communicate on one radio'. The table on 5.20.4 shows which: CAPTAIN VHF-1, FIRST OFFICER VHF-2, OBSERVER VHF-1. Receiver selectors, speaker, interphone and PA don't work at that station.
Hook: "ALT = degraded: Capt VHF-1, F/O VHF-2."
x.Q0006:
The FCOM describes the flight-deck escape straps: one above and aft of each No 2 window (L2 and R2), checked on the preflight ("Capt's escape strap – Check, connected to structure"). The overwing exit straps (one above each aft overwing exit, attached to the frame and the wing for ditching) are RYR cabin equipment from the cabin/safety manuals, which is why the bank answer is FOUR straps in total.
Hook: "2 windows + 2 overwing = 4 straps."
x.Q0007:
True. NORMAL airstair operation needs both AC and DC power. STANDBY operation uses only DC power, so from the interior (FWD attendant panel) the battery switch must be ON, and the STANDBY switch must be held while you press EXTEND/RETRACT. STANDBY bypasses all safety circuits – the handrail extensions must be stowed or the stairs can be damaged.
Hook: "Standby = DC = battery ON, no safety circuits."
x.Q0008:
Both No 2 windows can be opened from inside, on the ground or in flight, and both are emergency exits for the pilots. But only the FIRST OFFICER's No 2 window can also be opened from OUTSIDE the airplane (useful for ground access/rescue).
Hook: "Outside access = right side = F/O."
x.Q0009:
True. The No 2 windows open on the ground OR in flight and are emergency exits. To open: press the trigger, turn the handle back and inboard, then slide the window back until it locks open. To close: pull the latch mechanism rod forward to unlock, press the trigger and slide forward. Don't push up on the handle.
Hook: "Trigger, back and in."
x.Q0010:
Note: some question banks call it a 'Halotron' extinguisher – same thing (Halon-type chemical extinguisher, one, behind the F/O). The flight deck has ONE chemical (Halon-type) extinguisher, behind the First Officer's seat – see FIRE EXTINGUISHER on the aft flight deck overview. If you discharge it in the flight deck, all crew must be on oxygen masks, 100% with EMERGENCY selected, because the agent and its by-products are toxic. Water/glycol extinguishers are in the cabin and are for class A (paper, fabric, wood) fires only.
Hook: "One Halon, behind the F/O – masks on before you use it."
x.Q0011:
Each Passenger Service Unit has its own chemical oxygen generator feeding FOUR masks. Attendant stations and lavatories have two masks. The masks drop automatically at 14,000 ft cabin altitude (or with the PASS OXY switch ON). Pulling one mask down fires the generator for all masks in that unit; oxygen flows for about 12 minutes and cannot be shut off.
Hook: "PSU 4, toilet 2, 12 minutes, 14,000 ft."
x.Q0012:
True. Every lavatory has a Water Supply Shutoff Valve in the cabinet under the sink with FOUR positions: SUPPLY ON (sink + toilet), FAUCET ONLY, TOILET ONLY and OFF (everything shut). So a leak in the toilet or the tap can be isolated without losing the other.
Hook: "4 positions: ON – faucet – toilet – OFF."
x.Q0013:
The keypad panel outside the door (passenger-side door post) has three access lights. RED = door locked (or the access system switch is OFF). AMBER = the correct emergency code has been entered – the flight deck hears a chime and sees AUTO UNLK. GREEN = door unlocked. If the pilots do nothing and the selector stays in AUTO, the door unlocks when the timer expires (DENY stops it, UNLKD opens it at once).
Hook: "Red locked – Amber code OK, waiting – Green open."
x.Q0014:
In the flight deck the indication is the amber AUTO UNLK light on the Flight Deck Door Lock panel (aft electronic panel), together with a chime. Before the timer expires the AUTO UNLK light flashes and the chime becomes continuous, then the door unlocks unless a pilot selects DENY. The amber light on the keypad is OUTSIDE the door – not a flight deck indication. LOCK FAIL is a different light (lock failed or system switch OFF).
Hook: "Inside = AUTO UNLK; outside = amber keypad light."
x.Q0015:
The 737-800 turning-radius page has a CAUTION: do not try to turn away from an obstacle that is within 7.4 m (24.3 ft) of the NOSE or within 5.4 m (17.8 ft) of the WING TIP. The question says 'to the front' = nose = 7.4 m. Also on the page: minimum pavement width for a 180° turn 24.3 m, wing tip radius 23.0 m.
Hook: "Nose 7.4 – wing 5.4."
x.Q0016:
The PASS OXYGEN switch has two positions. NORMAL (guarded) = the masks drop automatically if the cabin altitude climbs to 14,000 ft. ON = the system activates and the masks drop immediately, at whatever cabin altitude you are when you select it. Either way the automatic 'Emergency Descent' PA plays 3 times and repeats every 10 s for one minute, and the amber PASS OXY ON light comes on.
Hook: "Switch ON = now; guarded = 14,000 ft."
x.Q0017:
The CIRCUIT BREAKER light control is on the FORWARD OVERHEAD panel, next to the overhead PANEL light control. It adjusts the lighting of the P-6 and P-18 circuit breaker panels behind the pilots – that's the trap: the breakers are on P6/P18, but the knob that lights them is on the forward overhead panel.
Hook: "Knob up front, breakers behind."
x.Q0018:
The water quantity (POTABLE WATER) indicator is on the AFT attendant panel. Don't confuse it with the Water System Service Panel, which is below the aft entry door and only has the fill fitting and fill/overflow and drain handles. The water comes from a single tank behind the aft cargo compartment and supplies the galleys and lavatory sinks.
Hook: "Water is aft: tank aft, gauge aft."
x.Q0019:
The EMER EXIT LIGHTS switch has three positions: OFF, ARMED (guarded – the normal position) and ON. In ARMED the lights are normally off and come on automatically if power to DC bus No 1 fails or AC power is turned off. OFF prevents the system working if power fails, and gives an amber NOT ARMED light. ON lights them all now. The aft attendant panel switch can also turn them on, overriding the flight deck switch.
Hook: "Guarded ARMED: DC 1 lost or AC off → lights on."
x.Q0020:
The PBE (smoke hood) is for crew use when fighting a fire or entering smoke/fumes. It goes over the head and, once activated, gives about 15 to over 20 minutes of oxygen depending on the model. Compare: passenger PSU oxygen ≈ 12 minutes. The flight deck PBE is checked in the preflight ('PBE – Check and stow').
Hook: "Smoke hood 15–20, passenger mask 12."
x.Q0021:
False. The AFT attendant panel has an EMERGENCY EXIT LIGHTING switch (it can turn the emergency lights on, bypassing the flight deck switch), but the airstair controls are only on the FORWARD attendant panel and on the exterior panel below and aft of the forward entry door. The airstair is a forward airstair – there is nothing for it at the back.
Hook: "Lights from both ends, stairs only from the front."
x.Q0022:
Step by step from the FCOM:
1) 1.30.18 (switch description): PASS OXYGEN 'ON – activates system and drops masks.'
2) 1.40.24 (system description): 'Activating the system causes the masks to drop from the stowage compartments' → the stowage compartments are the doors of the Passenger Service Units (PSU) above the seats. That is answer A.
3) Why the others are wrong: it does NOT pressurise the masks — 'The oxygen source is activated when any mask in the unit is pulled down' (each PSU has its own chemical oxygen source, flows ~12 min). It doesn't alert the cabin crew to don masks (the automatic Emergency Descent PA plays, but that's not 'the effect' asked), and it doesn't just turn on a PSU light — the cockpit PASS OXY ON light comes on.
Hook: "Switch ON drops masks; pulling a mask starts oxygen."
x.Q0023:
ARMED is the guarded normal position. The interior and exterior emergency lights stay off and illuminate automatically if power to DC BUS No 1 fails or AC power is turned off. The emergency lights have their own batteries, so they work after a total electrical failure. 'All the time' = ON, 'prevents activation' = OFF, and 'main bus 2' is a distractor.
Hook: "ARMED watches DC bus ONE."
x.Q0024:
On the aircraft that have them (YA573–YF682, YJ827–YK898), the retractable landing lights in the lower fuselage may be extended at ANY speed – there is no speed limit for them. Switch: RETRACT (in, off), EXTEND (out, off), ON (out and on). The fixed landing lights are in the wing leading edge. Newer aircraft have LED fixed lights instead.
Hook: "Retractable lights – any speed."
x.Q0025:
FCOM 9.20.19 (most aircraft, YA573–YW097): 'When the FLAP lever is moved beyond the 5 position… LE flaps remain at the full extended position and slats extend to the full extended position.' Flaps 15 is beyond 5 → all LE devices FULL EXT → all green FULL EXT lights. (Flaps 1–5: LE flaps full ext, slats only EXT.) Note: on the short-field aircraft YW098–YW164 slats only go to full extend beyond flaps 25.
Hook: "Beyond flaps 5 → everything FULL EXT."
x.Q0026:
Before discharging a Halon (or equivalent) extinguisher in the flight deck, all flight deck crew must put on oxygen masks set to 100% with EMERGENCY selected. The agent and the by-products of the fire are toxic (dizziness, difficulty breathing, eye irritation). After a whole bottle it can take up to 7 minutes for the agent to clear – keep masks on until smoke and agent have gone.
Hook: "Halon in the cockpit = masks on, 100% EMER, ~7 min."
x.Q0027:
To CLOSE the No 2 window: (1) pull forward on the latch mechanism ROD to unlock it, (2) press the trigger and slide the window forward, (3) turn the handle forward and outboard, (4) release the trigger – the window latches. Opening is the reverse: trigger, handle back and inboard, slide back until it locks open. Don't lift the handle upwards.
Hook: "Rod – trigger – forward – out – release."
x.Q0028:
⚠️ NOT IN THE FCOM – bank answer (the FCOM sends you to Performance Dispatch for the limit). The crew oxygen pressure is read on the CREW OXYGEN indicator on the aft overhead panel (pressure at the cylinder). The FCOM preflight only says to verify that it 'meets dispatch requirements' in the Performance Dispatch manual for the 114/115 cu ft cylinder – the bank figure for the first flight of the day is 1850 psi. Learn the number from the bank/PD; learn the procedure from the FCOM.
Hook: "First flight: 1850 psi."
x.Q0029:
From the Principal Dimensions page for the 737-800 with winglets: wingspan 117 ft 5 in = 35.79 m. The same page gives the overall length 39.47 m and tail height 12.62 m. 32.18 m is a length on the -700 page – a distractor.
Hook: "Span 35.8, length 39.5."
x.Q0030:
Crew oxygen pressure is read on the CREW OXYGEN pressure indicator on the AFT OVERHEAD panel. It shows the pressure in the crew oxygen cylinder (in the forward cargo area), but you don't go to the cylinder – you check the gauge during the preflight against the dispatch figures. Each crew station has a flow indicator (yellow cross), not a pressure gauge.
Hook: "Crew O2 pressure = aft overhead gauge."
x.Q0031:
When the system activates (14,000 ft cabin or PASS OXY ON) the masks only DROP – no oxygen flows yet. The chemical oxygen source in a PSU starts when any one mask of that unit is pulled down; then all masks of THAT unit get 100% oxygen (about 12 minutes, can't be stopped). Other PSUs are not affected until someone pulls one of their masks. A green in-line flow indicator in the hose shows oxygen is flowing.
Hook: "Drop ≠ flow. Pull one = that unit flows."
x.Q0032:
A barometric pressure switch activates the passenger oxygen system automatically at 14,000 ft CABIN altitude (with the PASS OXYGEN switch in its guarded NORMAL position). The masks drop, PASS OXY ON lights and the automatic Emergency Descent PA plays. 10,000 ft is the cabin altitude warning horn – don't mix them up.
Hook: "10,000 horn – 14,000 masks."
x.Q0033:
Yes. The overwing exits open from inside OR outside with a spring-loaded handle at the top of the door. From outside: knee against the lower door, push the exterior push panel, the door opens out and up automatically. From inside: pull the handle down and inward. A 28 V DC flight lock locks them automatically during takeoff, flight and landing (doors closed + engine running + thrust/air conditions) and unlocks them on the ground.
Hook: "Overwing: in or out, spring handle, opens UP and OUT."
x.Q0034:
From the 737-800 turning radius page: do not attempt to turn away from an obstacle within 7.4 m (24.3 ft) of the NOSE or within 5.4 m (17.8 ft) of the WING TIP. Distractors swap the numbers (7.4 m of the wing tip) – the bigger number belongs to the nose.
Hook: "Big nose 7.4, small wing 5.4."
x.Q0035:
Two places: the EMER EXIT LIGHTS switch on the flight deck forward overhead panel, and the EMERGENCY EXIT LIGHTING switch on the AFT attendant panel. The aft switch turns the lights on even if the flight deck switch is OFF. The forward attendant panel has airstair and cabin lighting controls but no emergency exit light switch.
Hook: "Exit lights: front office + the back."
x.Q0036:
FCOM SP.1.4: the door must be open to the cocked position only 'When operating the airstair from the INTERIOR control panel' (safety circuits). FCOM SP.1.5 Exterior Control: you select AIRSTAIRS EXTEND first and only then 'Forward entry door – Open to cocked position' → from outside the stair extends with the door closed. So the exterior system bypasses the door-open requirement. (It doesn't bypass the handrail safety; standby mode bypasses all safety circuits.)
Hook: "Inside needs the door open; outside doesn't."
x.Q0037:
RVSM limits (Limitations chapter): ON THE GROUND at a field from sea level to 5,000 ft, the Captain and F/O altitude displays may differ by at most 50 ft, and either display vs field elevation by at most 75 ft (fields 5,001–10,000 ft: 60 ft / 75 ft). IN FLIGHT the maximum Capt–F/O difference is 200 ft. The standby altimeter does not meet RVSM accuracy.
Hook: "Ground 50/75, flight 200, standby no good."
x.Q0038:
FCOM SP.1.4: the door must be cocked open only when using the INTERIOR control panel. FCOM SP.1.5 Exterior Control: AIRSTAIRS EXTEND first, then 'Forward entry door – Open to cocked position' → with the exterior control the door can be in ANY position.
Hook: "Outside = door any position."
x.Q0039:
The EMER EXIT LIGHTS switch is a three-position switch (OFF / ARMED / ON) on the forward overhead panel, guarded in ARMED. In ARMED the lights come on automatically when power to DC bus No 1 fails or AC power is turned off. There is no AUTO position, opening an overwing exit does not switch them on, and the switch for the cabin crew is on the AFT attendant panel, not the forward one. Preflight: ARMED, guard down, NOT ARMED light extinguished.
Hook: "OFF – ARMED – ON, no AUTO."
x.Q0040:
All three are correct. Emergency exit lights come on: (1) with the flight deck switch at ON, (2) automatically with the switch ARMED when DC bus No 1 power fails or AC power is turned off, (3) with the guarded switch on the AFT attendant panel – which works even if the flight deck switch is OFF.
Hook: "Three ways: ON, ARMED-auto, aft attendant."
x.Q0041:
All of the above: the forward overhead switch at ON; the same switch ARMED with DC bus No 1 power lost or AC power off; or the guarded switch on the aft attendant panel. Learn the three positions OFF / ARMED / ON and the extra switch at the back.
Hook: "Three ways: ON, ARMED-auto, aft attendant."
x.Q0042:
True. The flight deck door has decompression panels. Two pressure sensors unlock them if pressurisation is lost, so they open automatically and equalise pressure between cabin and flight deck (protecting the structure). They also give an escape path: pulling the release pins frees a panel manually if the door is jammed.
Hook: "Pressure drops → door panels pop."
x.Q0043:
Exterior STANDBY mode (hold the POWER switch in STANDBY, then AIRSTAIRS EXTEND) uses DC power only and does NOT need the battery switch ON – the FCOM only requires BAT ON for INTERIOR standby operation. Normal mode needs AC + DC. Standby bypasses the safety circuits, and from the exterior panel the door does not need to be open.
Hook: "Battery switch only for INSIDE standby."
x.Q0044:
False. Nothing in the FCOM about recirc fans or opening windows. The requirement before discharging a Halon (or equivalent) extinguisher in the flight deck is: all flight deck crew wear oxygen masks with 100% oxygen and EMERGENCY selected. Keep them on until smoke and agent have cleared (up to about 7 minutes).
Hook: "Halon = masks, nothing else."
x.Q0045:
True. The FCOM exterior lighting pages are split by effectivity. The older aircraft (YA573–YF682, YJ827–YK898) have a taxi light on the nose gear plus retractable landing lights. The newer aircraft use a different (LED) light fit with the taxi lights in other positions, so 'some aircraft have no taxi light on the nose gear' is true.
Hook: "Check the effectivity line at the top of the page."
x.Q0046:
Crew mask selector: NORM = air/oxygen mix on demand (ratio depends on cabin altitude); 100% = pure oxygen on demand; EMERGENCY = 100% oxygen under POSITIVE PRESSURE at ALL cabin altitudes. Positive pressure keeps smoke and toxic fumes out of the mask and clears fogging. It uses oxygen faster and makes talking harder – go back to 100% or NORM when you can.
Hook: "EMER = push air out, at every altitude."
x.Q0047:
The flight crew oxygen comes from a single cylinder. Pressure is shown on the aft overhead panel indicator and may be as high as 1850 psi; a pressure-reducing regulator lowers it before it reaches the masks. Same number as the bank's first-flight figure – 1850 psi is the full cylinder.
Hook: "One bottle, 1850 psi."
x.Q0048:
On the aircraft with automatic pressure-breathing masks (YA573–YK898), the regulator starts pressure breathing above 27,000 ft: at high cabin altitude oxygen is forced into the lungs under pressure so the blood still absorbs enough. Later aircraft have diluter-demand masks. Both use one cylinder at up to 1850 psi.
Hook: "Pressure breathing above 27."
x.Q0049:
False – there aren't two different panels. The flight deck door's DECOMPRESSION PANELS do both jobs: they open automatically during a decompression (two pressure sensors unlock them) AND they are the emergency egress path. If the door is jammed, pulling the release pins frees a decompression panel so the crew can get out.
Hook: "One type of panel: pops on decompression, pull pins to escape."
x.Q0050:
PASS OXY ON (amber, aft overhead panel) = the passenger oxygen system has been activated and the masks have dropped (automatically at 14,000 ft or by the switch). It also brings up OVERHEAD on the Master Caution annunciator. It does not show quantity or pressure – the passenger system is chemical generators, there's no bottle to measure.
Hook: "PASS OXY ON = masks are down."
x.Q0051:
Wingspan of the 737-800 with winglets = 117 ft 5 in = 35.79 m (FCOM Principal Dimensions). The other options swap the digits (37.59, 39.75…) – remember 35.79, and that the overall length is 39.47 m.
Hook: "Span 35.79 – length 39.47."
x.Q0052:
From the exterior panel (below and aft of the forward entry door): in NORMAL mode just select AIRSTAIRS – EXTEND. In STANDBY mode hold the POWER switch in STANDBY and select AIRSTAIRS – EXTEND. STANDBY is the answer they want: it works on DC only, bypasses the safety circuits, and from outside doesn't need the battery switch ON.
Hook: "Outside standby: hold STANDBY + EXTEND."
x.Q0053:
737-800: minimum pavement width for a 180° turn = 79.7 ft = 24.3 m (slow continuous turn, minimum thrust, no differential braking, 75° effective steering). Funny coincidence: 24.3 ft is also the 'nose obstacle' distance (7.4 m) – don't mix feet and metres.
Hook: "180° turn needs 24.3 METRES."
x.Q0054:
Wingspan 737-800 with winglets: 35.79 m (117 ft 5 in). 39.5 m is close to the overall length (39.47 m) and 12.5 m close to the tail height – typical distractors.
Hook: "Span 35.8, length 39.5, tail 12.6."
x.Q0055:
⚠️ NOT IN THE FCOM – bank answer. Bank answer: 6.4 m for the winglet tip height. The FCOM Principal Dimensions drawing gives heights only as reference values (marked *, 'consult airport planning guide') and does not label the wingtip height clearly, so learn this figure from the bank.
Hook: "Winglet tip ≈ 6.4 m."
x.Q0056:
FCOM SP.1.4: 'When operating the airstair from the interior control panel, the forward entry door must be open to the cocked position.' That's interior only. FCOM SP.1.5 Exterior Control: you extend first and open the door afterwards → from outside the door can be in any position.
Hook: "Outside = door any position."
x.Q0057:
FCOM 2.20.1 lists the users of the bleed air (pneumatic) system, including 'Water tank pressurization'. The schematic (2.20.3) shows the WATER branch off the bleed duct. So the potable water is pressurised by engine (or APU) bleed air – not hydraulics, not standby power.
Hook: "Bleed air pushes the water."
x.Q0058:
True. On the exterior panel the POWER switch is spring-loaded to NORMAL. NORMAL operation needs BOTH AC and DC power. Only if you hold it in STANDBY does the airstair run on DC power alone (and bypass the safety circuits). So just moving AIRSTAIRS to EXTEND (normal) needs AC and DC.
Hook: "Normal = AC+DC, Standby = DC."
x.Q0059:
All flight deck crew (both pilots and any observer) must don masks with 100% oxygen AND EMERGENCY selected before Halon is discharged in the flight deck. EMER gives positive pressure so the toxic agent and smoke cannot leak into the mask – 100% alone (on demand) is not enough.
Hook: "Everyone, 100% + EMER."
x.Q0060:
Both ways: automatically, when the two pressure sensors detect a decompression (pressure difference between flight deck and cabin), and manually, by pulling the release pins if the door is jammed. The door lock selector UNLKD only unlocks the door itself, not the panels.
Hook: "Panels: auto on decompression OR pins by hand."
x.Q0061:
The decompression (emergency access/egress) panels in the flight deck door open in two ways: automatically during a rapid decompression (two pressure sensors unlock them), or manually from INSIDE the flight deck by pulling the release pins (e.g. door jammed). Loss of electrical power does not open them, there's no key for them from outside, and the UNLK/UNLKD selector unlocks the door itself, not the panels.
Hook: "Decompression or pins – nothing else."
x.Q0062:
FCOM list of bleed air users: air conditioning/pressurisation, wing and engine thermal anti-ice, engine starting, hydraulic reservoir pressurisation, and water tank pressurisation (plus the Nitrogen Generation System on later aircraft). The only option with ALL of them, including water, is the correct one – the others each miss one item. Trace them on the bleed schematic: every 'TO …' arrow is a user.
Hook: "PAWS-H: Packs, Anti-ice, Water, Starters, Hydraulics."
x.Q0063:
All three temperature selectors OFF = Fixed Cabin Temperature mode: the LEFT pack holds 24 °C (75 °F) and the RIGHT pack 18 °C (65 °F), measured at the pack sensor. Option A has the sides swapped. 'Average of all zones' is what a single pack does with TRIM AIR OFF, not this case.
Hook: "Left is warm (24), right is cool (18)."
x.Q0064:
If all zone controls AND the primary pack controls fail, the STANDBY pack controls take over: they make the packs produce air to satisfy the AVERAGE demand of the two passenger cabin zones. The trim air modulating valves close and the flight deck selector has no effect. The fixed 24/18 °C mode only happens when you turn all selectors OFF.
Hook: "Everything failed → standby averages the two cabins."
x.Q0065:
True. APU bleed: two packs on the ground, one pack in flight (less air at altitude). A single pack in HIGH can maintain pressurisation and temperature up to the maximum certified ceiling. Rule: never run more than one pack from one engine.
Hook: "APU: 2 on ground, 1 in air."
x.Q0066:
False. Bleed air comes from the 5th and 9th compressor stages. Normally the 5th stage (low pressure) is enough – takeoff, climb and most cruise – and the high stage valve stays closed. When 5th stage pressure is too low (low thrust, e.g. descent/idle) the high stage valve modulates open to use 9th stage air.
Hook: "5 normally, 9 when low thrust."
x.Q0067:
If you descend before reaching the FLT ALT (e.g. returning after a malfunction), the controller shows OFF SCHED DESCENT and automatically programs the cabin to land at the TAKEOFF field elevation – no pilot input needed. If you reset the FLT ALT, that automatic abort capability to the departure field is LOST and you must set LAND ALT yourself. Nothing dramatic like a rapid depressurisation happens.
Hook: "Touch FLT ALT = lose the auto return."
x.Q0068:
Auto pressurisation modes are triggered by the FLT ALT: CRUISE mode starts when the airplane climbs to within 0.25 psi of the selected FLT ALT; DESCENT mode starts when it descends 0.25 psi below the FLT ALT. In descent the cabin descends proportionally to slightly below LAND ALT, so it lands slightly pressurised. On taxi-in the outflow valve drives fully open.
Hook: "0.25 psi either side of FLT ALT."
x.Q0069:
True. The engine bleed air valve is both a pressure regulator AND a shutoff valve. With the BLEED switch ON it is DC activated and pressure (pneumatically) operated: it keeps system pressure correct and reduces flow if bleed temperature is high. If bleed temperature/pressure exceeds limits, the bleed trip sensors close it automatically and BLEED TRIP OFF illuminates.
Hook: "Bleed valve = PRSOV: regulates AND shuts."
x.Q0070:
In MANUAL mode a separate DC motor powered by the DC STANDBY system drives the outflow valve – and faster than in AUTO/ALTN (full travel in about 20 seconds) so the crew can depressurise quickly. Because it's fast, small switch movements give big cabin rate changes. Powering it from standby means it still works after a loss of normal power.
Hook: "MAN = standby motor, fast."
x.Q0071:
OFF SCHED DESCENT (amber) = the airplane started descending before reaching the cruise altitude set in the FLT ALT window – typically a return to the departure airport. It is not a failure: the controller automatically programs the cabin to land at the takeoff field elevation. Controller failures show as AUTO FAIL (with ALTN = single, alone = dual).
Hook: "Off schedule = descending early, not broken."
x.Q0072:
TWO pressure relief valves limit the differential pressure to a maximum of 9.1 psi (an AFM limitation). Separately, a NEGATIVE pressure relief valve stops outside pressure from exceeding cabin pressure (e.g. fast descent with cabin higher than airplane) – it does not limit 9.1 psi. The outflow valve is the normal controller, not the safety relief.
Hook: "Two valves, 9.1 psi; negative valve for the other way."
x.Q0073:
True. Both packs produce air cold enough for the zone that needs the MOST cooling. Every other zone is then warmed up to its selected temperature by adding hot trim air (bleed air) through its own trim air modulating valve. That's why the packs are 'set' by the coldest zone.
Hook: "Packs cool for the coldest, trim air warms the rest."
x.Q0074:
Each electronic controller contains the PRIMARY control of its own pack and the STANDBY control of the OTHER pack. So if the right primary pack control fails, the right pack is controlled by the standby pack control in the LEFT controller. Either failure shows PACK + MASTER CAUTION + AIR COND only on recall. If both primary and standby for the same pack fail, the lights come on steady and the pack runs uncontrolled until it trips on overtemperature.
Hook: "Primary fails → the other side's standby."
x.Q0075:
False. TRIP RESET (if the fault has cleared) resets BLEED TRIP OFF, PACK (TRIP OFF) and DUCT/ZONE overheat lights, and RE-OPENS the related valve (bleed valve, pack valve or mix/trim valve) – it does not isolate anything. WING-BODY OVERHEAT is a bleed duct leak warning and is not reset by TRIP RESET; it goes out when the overheat condition is gone.
Hook: "Reset = re-open, and never for WING-BODY."
x.Q0076:
All bleed and air-conditioning lights on the forward overhead panel report to the AIR COND system annunciator on the glareshield: DUAL BLEED, WING-BODY OVERHEAT, BLEED TRIP OFF, PACK, ZONE TEMP, AUTO FAIL, OFF SCHED DESCENT. OVHT/DET is for engine/APU fire detection, OVERHEAD is for things like EMER EXIT NOT ARMED and PASS OXY ON.
Hook: "Anything on the air panel → AIR COND."
x.Q0077:
Pressing the WING-BODY OVHT TEST switch (hold at least 5 s) tests the overheat detection circuits: both amber WING-BODY OVERHEAT lights illuminate, plus MASTER CAUTION and the AIR COND annunciator. It doesn't test the duct overheat, bleed trip or pack trip circuits.
Hook: "OVHT TEST → both WING-BODY lights."
x.Q0078:
DUAL BLEED (amber) means the valve positions would let ENGINE bleed air back-pressure the APU: APU bleed valve open AND engine 1 BLEED switch ON, or engine 2 BLEED ON with the APU bleed valve and isolation valve open. It comes on normally during engine start (APU bleed still on) – just keep thrust low until the APU bleed is OFF. It's about valve positions, not measured pressure.
Hook: "DUAL BLEED = engine could blow back into the APU."
x.Q0079:
The recirculation fans re-use filtered cabin air: air from the cabin and E&E compartment is drawn through the forward cargo compartment lining, filtered and sent back to the mix manifold. Their purpose is to REDUCE the pack load and the engine bleed air demand (less fresh bleed air needed). They are not a backup for the packs. Fans are AC-driven; in AUTO they stop when packs are in HIGH (see switch logic).
Hook: "Recirc = reuse air → less bleed."
x.Q0080:
The flight deck gets its air directly from the LEFT pack, taken off upstream of the mix manifold. The left pack's excess air, the right pack's air and the recirculated air all go into the mix manifold for the passenger cabin. If flight deck trim air is lost, the left pack is controlled to the flight deck temperature.
Hook: "Left pack = cockpit."
x.Q0081:
WING-BODY OVERHEAT = a hot BLEED AIR DUCT LEAK detected by overheat sensors along the ducts. Left light sensors: left engine strut, left inboard wing leading edge, left air-conditioning bay, keel beam and the APU bleed duct. Right light: right strut, right inboard wing leading edge, right air-conditioning bay. It doesn't close a valve itself – the QRH has you isolate the leak.
Hook: "WING-BODY = hot air leaking from a duct."
x.Q0082:
BLEED TRIP OFF (amber) = engine bleed air temperature OR pressure exceeded a limit and that engine's bleed air valve has closed automatically. Once the condition clears, push TRIP RESET to reopen the valve. Low temperature never trips it.
Hook: "Too hot or too much pressure → valve shuts → reset."
x.Q0083:
True. Pressurisation is controlled by modulating the outflow valve (and the overboard exhaust valve), but the cabin also continuously loses air through small 'leaks' such as the lavatory and galley vents, which the controller compensates for. The outflow valve is in the aft fuselage; the overboard exhaust valve dumps E&E cooling air.
Hook: "Outflow valve controls, toilets and galleys leak a bit."
x.Q0084:
5th and 9th stages of the compressor. 5th stage normally; 9th stage through the high stage valve when 5th stage pressure is too low (low thrust). The other options mix in 4th or 8th stage – wrong.
Hook: "5 and 9."
x.Q0085:
The engine bleed air valve is DC ACTIVATED (a solenoid, signalled by the BLEED switch) and PRESSURE (pneumatically) OPERATED – the bleed air itself moves the valve. That's why a bleed valve can't open with the engine stopped even if the switch is ON.
Hook: "DC tells it, air moves it."
x.Q0086:
ONE trim air pressure regulating and shutoff valve. Follow the hot bleed air (red) on the distribution schematic: it goes through that single valve – opened/closed by the TRIM AIR switch – and then splits to THREE trim air modulating valves, one per zone (flight deck, FWD cabin, AFT cabin). The packs make air cold enough for the coldest zone; each modulating valve adds hot trim air to warm its own zone.
Hook: "1 regulator → 3 modulating valves → 3 zones."
x.Q0087:
All temperature selectors OFF → fixed temperatures: LEFT pack 24 °C (75 °F), RIGHT pack 18 °C (65 °F). Option C has them reversed. Remember the left pack also feeds the flight deck, so it's the warmer one.
Hook: "Left 24 (warm), right 18 (cool)."
x.Q0088:
BLEED TRIP OFF closes the ENGINE BLEED AIR VALVE of that engine automatically. Not the isolation valve, not the high stage valve. TRIP RESET reopens it once the overtemperature/overpressure has cleared.
Hook: "BLEED TRIP = bleed valve."
x.Q0089:
In the PACK / PACK TRIP OFF non-normal checklist (QRH) you select a WARMER temperature to REDUCE THE WORKLOAD on the AFFECTED pack: a warmer setting needs less cooling, so the pack runs cooler and is less likely to trip on overtemperature. It isn't about the other pack or the outflow.
Hook: "Warmer = easier for the sick pack."
x.Q0090:
BOTH packs from the APU: on the GROUND only. In flight the APU can supply ONE pack (thinner air, less APU bleed output). The APU itself starts and runs up to the maximum certified altitude.
Hook: "APU: 2 on ground, 1 in air."
x.Q0091:
Maximum cabin differential pressure = 9.1 psi, set by the two pressure relief valves (AFM limitation). Don't confuse with the normal controller schedule: 7.45 psid (FLT ALT ≤ FL280), 7.80 (FL280–370), 8.35 (above FL370), or 8.75 psi which triggers AUTO FAIL.
Hook: "Relief 9.1 – schedule 7.45 / 7.8 / 8.35."
x.Q0092:
The outflow VALVE position indicator on the pressurisation panel shows the outflow valve position and works in ALL modes (AUTO, ALTN and MAN). In MAN you use it with the cabin altitude panel to check what your OPEN/CLOSE inputs are doing. It has nothing to do with the ram air deflector doors.
Hook: "Valve needle works in every mode."
x.Q0093:
The recirculation fan reduces the air conditioning pack load and the engine bleed air demand by reusing filtered cabin air (through the forward cargo compartment lining back to the mix manifold). It is driven by an AC motor – so 'DC motor' is wrong. It has no overheat-detection role.
Hook: "Recirc: less pack work, AC motor."
x.Q0095:
Wing anti-ice uses bleed air to heat ONLY the THREE INBOARD leading edge slats on each wing. It does not heat the leading edge flaps or the outboard slats. The control valves are AC motor-operated and it works with the slats in any position; the air is then exhausted overboard.
Hook: "Three inboard slats – nothing else."
x.Q0096:
The warm E&E bay cooling air goes two ways depending on the overboard exhaust valve: on the ground and in flight at LOW differential pressure the valve is OPEN and the air is dumped overboard; in flight at HIGHER differential pressure the valve CLOSES and the air is diffused around the lining of the FORWARD cargo compartment to heat it. (Cabin air heats the AFT cargo lining on its way to the outflow valve.)
Hook: "High up, E&E heat warms the forward hold."
x.Q0097:
The auto controller keeps the lowest cabin altitude allowed by the differential pressure schedule for the selected FLT ALT: at or below 28,000 ft → 7.45 psid; 28,000–37,000 ft → 7.80 psid; ABOVE 37,000 ft → 8.35 psid. 9.1 psi is the relief valve maximum, not the controller's target.
Hook: "28 – 37 – above: 7.45 – 7.80 – 8.35."
x.Q0098:
ISOLATION VALVE in AUTO: CLOSED when both engine BLEED switches are ON and both PACK switches are AUTO or HIGH (each side runs independently). It OPENS automatically as soon as ANY engine BLEED or PACK switch is positioned OFF, so one side can feed the other. It doesn't modulate.
Hook: "All ON = closed; anything OFF = open."
x.Q0099:
One pack (in HIGH flow) can maintain pressurisation AND acceptable temperatures throughout the airplane up to the maximum certified ceiling (41,000 ft). With TRIM AIR ON, zone temperature control works the same as with two packs; only with TRIM AIR OFF does the pack aim for the average of all zones – so D is not the general answer.
Hook: "One pack is enough – all the way to FL410."
x.Q0100:
Bleed (pneumatic) air users: air conditioning/pressurisation, wing and engine anti-ice, engine starting, hydraulic reservoir and water tank pressurisation – and the TAT probe aspiration. The APU is a SOURCE of bleed air, not a user – which kills options A, B and D.
Hook: "APU gives air, it doesn't use it."
x.Q0101:
On STANDBY pack controls the packs produce air for the AVERAGE temperature demand of the two cabin zones (FWD and AFT). The trim air modulating valves close, but pack air still flows to all zones – it's just not trimmed. The flight deck selector has no effect.
Hook: "Standby = average of the cabins."
x.Q0102:
Wing-body overheat sensors run along the bleed ducts: engine STRUTS, INBOARD wing leading edges, air-conditioning bays, KEEL BEAM and APU BLEED DUCT (the last two only on the LEFT loop). Distractors use 'slats', 'cowl lips', 'APU compartment' or 'E&E bay' – all wrong: cowl and slats are anti-ice areas, not duct overheat zones.
Hook: "Strut – inboard LE – A/C bay – keel – APU duct."
x.Q0103:
A CONT CAB (flight deck) ZONE TEMP light that STAYS ON after Master Caution reset means a flight deck duct overheat OR failure of BOTH the primary and standby flight deck temperature controls – so both statements are correct. If it only shows on RECALL and goes out on reset, only ONE of the two controls has failed. FWD/AFT CAB steady = duct overheat.
Hook: "Steady = overheat or both failed; recall = one failed."
x.Q0104:
Take no action. OFF SCHED DESCENT on an early return is the system telling you it noticed: it automatically programs the cabin to land at the takeoff field elevation. Don't touch FLT ALT (that would cancel the auto abort). LAND ALT already shows the departure field, so it doesn't need changing.
Hook: "Going back home? Pressurisation already knows."
x.Q0105:
The APU bleed duct runs along the keel area on the left side, so a leak there lights the LEFT WING-BODY OVERHEAT light (left loop: left strut, left inboard LE, left A/C bay, keel beam, APU bleed duct). The right light only covers the right strut, right inboard LE and right A/C bay. There is no 'APU BLEED' warning light.
Hook: "APU duct and keel = LEFT light."
x.Q0106:
If the pressurisation panel detects a failure after a DC power interruption, the FLT ALT indicator shows '88888' or all dashes. If cabin altitude and rate are normal, automatic pressure control is NOT affected. Other indicator failures can show non-numbers or blank – if you can't change it with the selector, monitor the system closely in climb and descent.
Hook: "Eights = panel failure, auto still works."
x.Q0107:
True (on our trim-air aircraft YF501–YW164). A zone duct overheat lights ZONE TEMP and closes that zone's trim air modulating valve. Once the duct has cooled, TRIP RESET resets BLEED TRIP OFF, PACK or ZONE TEMP lights and re-opens the related valve (bleed valve, pack valve or trim air modulating valve). On older YA573 the wording is DUCT OVERHEAT instead of ZONE TEMP.
Hook: "TRIP RESET: BLEED, PACK, ZONE."
x.Q0108:
False. The flight deck gets its air from the LEFT pack, taken off upstream of the mix manifold. The right pack's air goes into the mix manifold for the passenger cabin.
Hook: "Left pack = cockpit."
x.Q0109:
AUTO FAIL (amber) = automatic pressurisation failure. With the ALTN light ALSO on → single controller failure (the other controller has taken over automatically). AUTO FAIL ALONE → dual failure → go to MAN. Triggers include loss of DC power, controller or outflow valve fault, differential > 8.75 psi, rate ±2000 ft/min, cabin above 15,800 ft. The distractors use AC power, 13,875 ft or 10,000 ft – all wrong.
Hook: "AUTO FAIL + ALTN = one gone; alone = both gone."
x.Q0110:
AUTO FAIL triggers (if the controller isn't responding properly): differential pressure > 8.75 psi, cabin rate faster than ±2000 sea-level ft/min, or cabin altitude above 15,800 ft – plus loss of DC power and controller/valve faults. The system then automatically transfers to the other controller (ALTN). Selecting ALTN yourself doesn't cause AUTO FAIL.
Hook: "8.75 psi – 2000 fpm – 15,800 ft."
x.Q0111:
True – word for word from FCOM 2.40.3. Outflow is controlled by the outflow valve and the overboard exhaust valve; a small amount also leaves through toilet and galley vents, fixed vents and seal leakage. Most cabin air goes down through the foot-level grills, around the aft cargo lining (heating it) and out through the outflow valve.
Hook: "Outflow valve + exhaust valve + small leaks."
x.Q0112:
The controller keeps the cabin at a maximum of 8,000 ft cabin altitude even at the airplane's maximum certified ceiling of 41,000 ft. 10,000 ft is the cabin altitude warning; 12,000 is nothing in particular.
Hook: "8,000 cabin at 41,000 airplane."
x.Q0113:
True. Bleed air from the packs is pumped in more or less constantly; the cabin pressure is set by how far the OUTFLOW VALVE opens – more closed = more pressure (lower cabin altitude). The overboard exhaust valve also contributes. The controller (AUTO/ALTN) or the pilot (MAN) moves the valve.
Hook: "Air in is constant – the outflow valve decides the pressure."
x.Q0114:
False – the trap is 'from the Mix Manifold'. Left pack air goes to the flight deck directly, taken off UPSTREAM of (before) the mix manifold. Only the left pack's excess, the right pack and the recirc air go into the mix manifold for the cabin.
Hook: "Cockpit air skips the mix manifold."
x.Q0115:
Normally at high differential pressure (e.g. FL370) the overboard exhaust valve is CLOSED. It is driven OPEN if EITHER pack switch is in HIGH AND the (right) recirculation fan is OFF – that's the smoke removal configuration, giving extra ventilation to clear smoke. The QRH smoke/fumes checklist sets exactly that.
Hook: "Pack HIGH + recirc OFF = smoke mode = exhaust valve open."
x.Q0116:
Unlocked. The overwing exit flight lock (28 V DC) only locks when ALL these are true: three of the four entry/service doors closed, either engine running, and air/ground logic says airborne or thrust levers set for takeoff. During boarding with L1 and L2 open and engines off, the overwing exits stay unlocked so they can be used in an emergency.
Hook: "Doors open, engines off → overwings unlocked."
x.Q0117:
Single pack + TRIM AIR OFF: without trim air nothing can warm individual zones, so the pack aims for the AVERAGE temperature demand of all three zones. With TRIM AIR ON, single pack works like two-pack operation (coldest zone + trim). Option D describes 'trim air lost' and wrongly says left pack (it's the right pack that averages fwd/aft).
Hook: "No trim air → average everything."
x.Q0118:
Single pack with TRIM AIR OFF → the pack produces air for the AVERAGE demand of all three zones (flight deck, FWD, AFT). It still heats and cools normally. Matching the coldest zone only happens WITH trim air, because then the warmer zones can be trimmed up.
Hook: "Trim OFF = average of three."
x.Q0119:
⚠️ NOT IN THE FCOM – bank answer (the FCOM doesn't give the duration). Bank answer: 10 minutes. The emergency lights run on their own batteries (charged from DC bus 1), which is why they still work after a total power loss. The FCOM shows WHERE the emergency lights are (exit signs, aisle lights, slide and exterior lighting, photoluminescent strips) but doesn't state the duration – learn 10 minutes from the bank.
Hook: "Emergency lights: own batteries, ~10 minutes."
x.Q0120:
The auto pressurisation controllers get their air data from the ADIRUs: ambient static pressure, baro-corrected and uncorrected altitude and calibrated airspeed (BARO settings come from both pilots' selectors). They also get thrust lever position from the stall management computers and air/ground signals. They don't read the static ports directly, nor the EFIS panel or CDU – the FLT/LAND ALT come from the pressurisation panel.
Hook: "Pressurisation listens to the ADIRUs."
x.Q0121:
Do nothing on the pressurisation panel. If you descend before reaching the FLT ALT, the controller (auto abort) programs the cabin to land at the takeoff field elevation by itself. Resetting FLT ALT would cancel that capability; LAND ALT already equals the departure field.
Hook: "Return to departure = hands off the pressurisation."
x.Q0122:
A steady PACK light has two possible causes: a pack TRIP OFF (overheat in the cooling cycle → pack valve closes) or failure of BOTH primary and standby pack controls. TRIP RESET only resets the overheat trip (after it cools down) – a dual control failure can't be reset. So if the light resets, it was an overheat trip.
Hook: "Resettable PACK = overheat; not resettable = controllers."
x.Q0123:
True – FCOM 2.31.6 word for word: a zone whose selector is OFF is simply ignored by the temperature control logic (the system controls to the remaining zones). If ALL selectors are OFF you get the fixed temperatures: left pack 24 °C, right pack 18 °C.
Hook: "One OFF = ignored; all OFF = 24/18."
x.Q0124:
FCOM: when BOTH the primary and standby controls of the same pack fail, PACK + MASTER CAUTION + AIR COND come on (steady) and the pack CONTINUES TO OPERATE WITHOUT CONTROL until excessive temperature makes it trip off. Some question banks say 'inoperative' – the FCOM wording is the safe answer; the QRH PACK checklist then deals with it.
Hook: "Both controls gone → pack runs wild until it trips."
x.Q0125:
In MANUAL mode: during descent nudge the outflow valve toward CLOSE as needed, and BEFORE ENTERING THE LANDING PATTERN slowly drive it FULLY OPEN so the airplane is depressurised, then check differential pressure is ZERO. Landing pressurised could make doors hard to open and cause ear/pressure problems.
Hook: "Manual landing: valve full open, diff zero."
x.Q0126:
If you descend in MANUAL with the outflow valve still (partly) closed, cabin pressure can become higher than sea level pressure. The CABIN ALT needle then goes below zero and can wrap round to the upper end of the scale – so it looks like a HIGH cabin altitude when really the cabin is over-pressurised. FCOM note on the cabin altimeter (2.10.12). The fix: open the outflow valve.
Hook: "Needle past zero = cabin over-pressurised, not high."
x.Q0127:
Yes. Look at the engine anti-ice schematic: the cowl anti-ice air is taken from the engine BEFORE (upstream of) the engine bleed air valve, through its own cowl anti-ice valve. So closing the engine BLEED valve (switch OFF) does not stop engine anti-ice. Wing anti-ice is different – it uses the bleed air duct and needs bleed air.
Hook: "Engine anti-ice takes its own air, before the bleed valve."
x.Q0128:
After a correct emergency code (chime + AUTO UNLK), rotate the Flight Deck Door Lock selector to DENY (hold it about 1 second). That denies entry, extinguishes AUTO UNLK and blocks further keypad entry for several minutes. AUTO leaves it to the timer; UNLKD opens it. LOCK FAIL is just a light.
Hook: "DENY = no entry + keypad locked for minutes."
x.Q0129:
The ram air inlet doors are controlled automatically by the packs. On the ground or in slow flight with flaps not fully up → FULL OPEN (RAM DOOR FULL OPEN light, blue). In normal cruise → they MODULATE between open and closed as the pack needs for temperature control. Deflector doors in front stop slush ingestion on the ground.
Hook: "Ground = open, cruise = modulate."
x.Q0131:
False – two errors. In MAN mode the DC standby-powered motor moves the outflow valve FASTER than AUTO/ALTN, and full travel takes up to 20 SECONDS (not 2 minutes). That speed lets the crew depressurise quickly in an emergency, but small switch movements cause large cabin rate changes.
Hook: "MAN = fast: 20 seconds."
x.Q0132:
BLEED TRIP OFF = excessive engine bleed air TEMPERATURE or PRESSURE detected by the bleed trip sensors; the engine bleed air valve closes automatically. Pack faults show as PACK, not BLEED TRIP OFF, and there's no flow-rate trip.
Hook: "BLEED TRIP = too hot or too much pressure."
x.Q0133:
PACK light only on RECALL (goes out on reset) = failure of EITHER the primary OR the standby pack control. The pack keeps working normally on the remaining control (if primary failed, the standby control in the opposite controller takes over). Steady PACK = trip off or both controls failed.
Hook: "Recall-only PACK = one control gone, pack still OK."
x.Q0134:
Corrected after the independent audit: B. FCOM 2.31.6: 'Overheat detection is provided by temperature sensors located downstream of the packs and the mix manifold.' The trim air valve is what CLOSES on an overheat – the FCOM doesn't list a sensor downstream of it. (On the older YA573 system the FCOM just says 'downstream of the packs'.)
Hook: "Sensors: after the packs and the mix manifold."
x.Q0135:
True – FCOM 2.20.2: DUAL BLEED comes on whenever the APU bleed valve is open and the engine bleed switches/isolation valve would allow possible backpressure of the APU, 'therefore thrust must be limited to idle with the DUAL BLEED light illuminated'. In practice: after engine start, switch the APU bleed OFF before taxi thrust.
Hook: "DUAL BLEED = idle thrust only."
x.Q0136:
BLEED TRIP OFF = excessive ENGINE BLEED AIR pressure or temperature; the bleed valve closes. It can only be reset with TRIP RESET once the condition has cleared (not 'at any time'). Pack overheat and pack controller faults use the PACK light instead.
Hook: "BLEED TRIP = engine bleed too hot/high."
x.Q0137:
Ram air (outside air through the ram inlet doors) cools the pack HEAT EXCHANGERS – it never enters the cabin. On the pack schematic, bleed air goes through the heat exchanger (cooled by ram air), then the air cycle machine and water separator, then to the mix manifold. E&E cooling uses separate fans.
Hook: "Ram air cools the heat exchanger, not people."
x.Q0138:
The RIGHT WING-BODY OVERHEAT light covers only the right engine strut, right inboard wing leading edge and right air-conditioning bay. The keel beam and APU bleed duct are on the LEFT light, and the left A/C bay is obviously left. So the right engine strut is the only correct area.
Hook: "Right light = right strut, right wing, right bay."
x.Q0139:
AUTO FAIL + ALTN light together = SINGLE controller failure – control has transferred automatically to the other controller. AUTO FAIL ALONE = DUAL controller failure (go MAN). Option D swaps these. Auto slat failure is AUTO SLAT FAIL on the forward overhead, unrelated.
Hook: "With ALTN = one; alone = both."
x.Q0140:
An APU bleed duct leak is a hot-air leak in a duct → WING-BODY OVERHEAT, and the APU duct sensor is on the LEFT loop → LEFT WING-BODY OVERHEAT light only. BLEED TRIP OFF is for engine bleed temp/pressure, DUAL BLEED is about valve positions.
Hook: "APU duct leak = LEFT wing-body."
x.Q0141:
Each electronic controller holds its own pack's PRIMARY control and the OTHER pack's STANDBY control (on the pack schematic the L controller contains 'R STBY PACK CONTROL'). Right primary fails → right pack controlled by the standby control in the LEFT controller. The pack keeps working; PACK shows only on recall.
Hook: "Primary fails → standby on the other side."
x.Q0142:
CONT CAB ZONE TEMP on RECALL only = failure of EITHER the flight deck primary OR standby temperature control (the other one is still working; the light goes out on reset). Steady (without recall) = duct overheat or failure of BOTH controls. Pack overheats use the PACK light.
Hook: "Recall = one; steady = both (or overheat)."
x.Q0143:
One pack (high flow) maintains pressurisation AND acceptable temperatures up to the maximum certified ceiling, 41,000 ft. No need to descend. Average-temperature control only happens with TRIM AIR OFF, and switching zone selectors OFF has nothing to do with pressurisation capability.
Hook: "One pack = FL410, no descent needed."
x.Q0145:
In the secure (parking) flow the PACK switches go OFF, but the engine BLEED air switches are not moved – they stay ON (their normal position; a bleed valve can't open without the engine running anyway). There is no HIGH or AUTO position on a bleed switch – only OFF/ON.
Hook: "Secure: packs OFF, bleeds stay ON."
x.Q0146:
Recirculation fans reuse filtered cabin air to REDUCE THE PACK LOAD and engine bleed demand. They don't mix air in the manifold, don't pressurise the cabin, and for smoke removal they are actually switched OFF (with a pack in HIGH the overboard exhaust valve opens).
Hook: "Recirc = less work for the packs; OFF for smoke."
x.Q0147:
The high stage (9th) valve opens when 5th stage pressure is too low – i.e. LOW ENGINE THRUST, such as a descent with the engines at idle (and taxi/idle on the ground). During takeoff, climb and most cruise the 5th stage is enough and the high stage valve stays closed. A 'bleeds off' takeoff takes no bleed at all.
Hook: "Idle descent = 9th stage."
x.Q0148:
CONT CAB ZONE TEMP on recall = the PRIMARY flight deck temperature control has failed and the system has AUTOMATICALLY switched to the BACKUP control (in the left controller). Temperature control continues normally. Both failed = steady light; pack overheat = PACK light.
Hook: "Recall CONT CAB = switched to backup."
x.Q0149:
Descent mode starts when the airplane descends 0.25 psi below the selected FLT ALT – not at T/D, not at a fixed distance, and nothing to do with the autothrottle RETARD. The cabin then descends proportionally to slightly below LAND ALT.
Hook: "0.25 psi below FLT ALT."
x.Q0150:
Bleed trip sensors are positioned on both sides of the engine bleed air valve (B737 Question Bank answer). If engine bleed temperature or pressure exceeds a limit, the BLEED TRIP OFF light illuminates and that engine bleed air valve closes automatically (FCOM 2.20.1). The FCOM doesn't state the location; this is the bank's answer.
Hook: "Trip sensors sit around the bleed valve they close."
x.Q0151:
TRIP RESET resets only BLEED TRIP OFF, PACK and ZONE TEMP lights (re-opening the bleed, pack or trim air valve). It does NOT reset WING-BODY OVERHEAT (goes out when the leak/overheat stops), DUAL BLEED (valve positions) or RAM DOOR FULL OPEN (just a door position).
Hook: "Reset: BLEED – PACK – ZONE."
x.Q0152:
5th stage is the normal source. 9th stage air is supplied ONLY when the high stage valve modulates open because 5th stage air is not enough (low thrust). Option A reverses the stages, and C ('constantly from both') is wrong because the high stage valve is normally closed.
Hook: "5 normally; 9 only when 5 can't cope."
x.Q0153:
Same idea: bleed air comes from the 5th stage; 9th stage air is added only when the high stage valve modulates open because the 5th stage can't supply enough (low thrust). It is not 'whenever the bleed valve is ON' and not 'constantly from both'.
Hook: "High stage valve = only at low thrust."
x.Q0154:
No-engine-bleed takeoff (SP 2): packs supplied by the APU, engine BLEED switches OFF. If an engine fails, do NOT put the engine BLEED switches ON until reaching 1500 ft or obstacle clearance height – you need every bit of thrust from the remaining engine first.
Hook: "Engine failure on a no-bleed takeoff: bleeds stay OFF until 1500 ft."
x.Q0155:
ISOLATION VALVE in AUTO is CLOSED only when BOTH engine BLEED switches are ON AND BOTH PACK switches are AUTO or HIGH (each side self-sufficient). As soon as any bleed or pack switch goes OFF, it opens automatically so one side can supply the other.
Hook: "All ON = closed; one OFF = open."
x.Q0156:
The amber COWL ANTI-ICE light = OVERPRESSURE in the duct downstream of the cowl anti-ice valve (between valve and cowl lip). It is not an over-temperature warning. Valve position is shown by the blue COWL VALVE OPEN light (bright = in transit/disagree, dim = open).
Hook: "Amber COWL = too much pressure."
x.Q0157:
True. On the schematic the cowl anti-ice air is tapped from the engine BEFORE the engine bleed air valve. So engine anti-ice still works with the engine BLEED switch OFF or the bleed valve tripped. The cowl valve is electrically controlled and pressure actuated.
Hook: "Cowl valve first, bleed valve after."
x.Q0158:
Rain removal on the forward windows = windshield WIPERS + a permanent RAIN REPELLENT COATING. Window heat is for anti-icing and anti-fogging (and strength against bird strikes), not rain removal. Don't run the wipers on a dry windshield – it scratches.
Hook: "Rain: wipers + coating."
x.Q0159:
False – because of one word. If a cowl anti-ice valve disagrees with its switch, the COWL VALVE OPEN light stays bright blue AND an amber TAI shows on the engine display AFTER A SHORT DELAY – not immediately. Watch for 'immediately' vs 'after a short delay' in exam questions.
Hook: "Amber TAI comes after a delay."
x.Q0160:
False. The thrust-lever logic only applies ON THE GROUND: the wing anti-ice valves close if either engine's thrust is above the takeoff warning setting (or a duct gets too hot) and reopen when thrust is reduced. In flight thrust has no effect. Also: the switch trips OFF automatically at lift-off.
Hook: "Thrust closes wing anti-ice valves only on the ground."
x.Q0161:
Green window heat ON light: ILLUMINATED = heat is being applied to that window. EXTINGUISHED = switch OFF, overheat, system failure, or (normally) the window is at the correct temperature – the heat cycles on and off. Overheat is the amber OVERHEAT light.
Hook: "Green = heating; out = warm enough."
x.Q0162:
WINDOW HEAT test switch: OVHT simulates an OVERHEAT so you can check the warning: amber OVERHEAT lights on, green ON lights out, MASTER CAUTION + ANTI-ICE. The other position, PWR TEST, forces the controller to full power to check the heating works. It isn't a voltage check and isn't limited to flight.
Hook: "OVHT = fake overheat; PWR TEST = full power."
x.Q0163:
With the switch ON, a green ON light going out most likely means that window has reached the CORRECT TEMPERATURE – the controller cycles the heat. An overheat or failure would normally show other indications (amber OVERHEAT light, MASTER CAUTION). Power loss would also bring on OVERHEAT.
Hook: "Green out with switch ON = window warm enough."
x.Q0164:
NOT protected by wing anti-ice: the leading edge FLAPS (inboard of the engines) and the OUTBOARD slat on each wing. Protected: the three inboard slats. So the answer is LE flaps + outboard slat.
Hook: "Heated = 3 inboard slats; not heated = LE flaps + outboard slat."
x.Q0165:
Blue VALVE OPEN light logic: BRIGHT = valve in transit OR valve position disagrees with the switch; DIM = valve open and agrees with switch ON; OUT = valve closed with switch OFF. A valve that closes while the switch is ON is a disagreement → BRIGHT blue (stays bright).
Hook: "Bright = moving or wrong; dim = open OK."
x.Q0167:
ENG ANTI-ICE ON: opens the cowl anti-ice valve and sets the stall warning logic for icing – the stick shaker and the minimum manoeuvre speed bars move. The FMC VREF is NOT adjusted automatically (you add any icing correction yourself). Engine anti-ice logic returns to normal when switched OFF, unless WING anti-ice was used in flight.
Hook: "Shaker and bars yes, VREF no."
x.Q0168:
Loss of both engine generators (no APU) = standby power. On standby power only the CAPTAIN's pitot probe stays heated (and its CAPT PITOT light won't show a failure). A/P, A/T, autobrake and the F/O probe heat are not available on standby power.
Hook: "Standby power keeps the Captain's pitot warm, nothing else."
x.Q0169:
Amber COWL ANTI-ICE = OVERPRESSURE in the duct DOWNSTREAM of the cowl anti-ice valve (the duct from the valve to the cowl lip). Not temperature, not leaks, not low pressure.
Hook: "COWL ANTI-ICE amber = over-pressure after the valve."
x.Q0170:
With the PROBE HEAT switches ON, an amber probe light (here R ELEV PITOT) means that probe is NOT HEATED. The lights don't measure blockage or pressure differences. Elevator pitots feed the elevator feel system.
Hook: "Amber probe light = not heated."
x.Q0171:
Valve disagreement: the blue COWL VALVE OPEN light REMAINS BRIGHT (and an amber TAI shows on the CDS after a short delay). The amber COWL ANTI-ICE light is for overpressure. A green TAI means valve open and agreeing – the normal state.
Hook: "Stuck valve = stays bright blue."
x.Q0172:
ENG ANTI-ICE OFF: the cowl valves CLOSE and the stall warning logic RETURNS TO NORMAL – unless WING anti-ice was used in flight, because wing anti-ice keeps the icing logic for the rest of the flight.
Hook: "Engine anti-ice OFF resets the shaker logic – unless wing anti-ice was on."
x.Q0173:
WING ANTI-ICE ON in flight: both valves open (blue lights bright in transit, then dim) and the stick shaker / minimum manoeuvre speed bars are set for icing – and they STAY set for the REMAINDER OF THE FLIGHT even if you switch it off. That's the difference with engine anti-ice.
Hook: "Wing anti-ice once = icing logic all flight."
x.Q0174:
True. On standby power only the Captain's pitot probe is heated, and if that heat fails the CAPT PITOT light does NOT illuminate. Also, the pitot for the standby airspeed indicator is not heated on standby power.
Hook: "Standby power: Capt pitot heated, but no failure light."
x.Q0175:
ENG ANTI-ICE ON sets stall warning logic for icing: it ADJUSTS the stick shaker AND the minimum manoeuvre speed bars on the airspeed indicator. It does NOT change the FMC VREF.
Hook: "Shaker + bars move, VREF doesn't."
x.Q0176:
Heated electrically: pitot probes (Capt, F/O, aux), elevator pitots, the TAT probe and the alpha vanes. NOT heated: the STATIC PORTS (they're flush with the skin and don't ice).
Hook: "Everything that sticks out is heated; static ports aren't."
x.Q0177:
On standby power ONLY the Captain's pitot probe is heated – not the F/O's, not the TAT, not the standby airspeed pitot. (And its failure light won't work.)
Hook: "Standby power = Captain's pitot only."
x.Q0178:
The alpha (angle of attack) vanes are electrically heated, controlled by the PROBE HEAT switches together with the pitots and TAT probe (amber L/R ALPHA VANE light if not heated). They have nothing to do with window heat or engine anti-ice, and static ports aren't heated at all.
Hook: "Alpha vanes = PROBE HEAT."
x.Q0179:
TAI on the engine display: GREEN = cowl anti-ice valve OPEN and its ENG ANTI-ICE switch ON (normal). AMBER = valve not in the position the switch commands (disagreement). No TAI = valve closed, switch OFF.
Hook: "Green TAI = working; amber TAI = stuck."
x.Q0180:
Dual-autopilot autoland: FLARE arms below 1500 ft RA (must be armed by ~350 ft or both A/Ps disengage); the FLARE manoeuvre starts at about 50 ft RADIO altitude; the A/T starts RETARD at about 27 ft RA to reach idle at touchdown; A/T disengages ~2 s after touchdown; A/P is disengaged manually.
Hook: "1500 arm – 350 check – 50 flare – 27 retard."
x.Q0181:
True (the FCOM says 800 ft above FIELD ELEVATION). Takeoff sequence: A/T in N1 → THR HLD at 84 kt (servos inhibited, levers stay where they are) → at 800 ft above field elevation the A/T changes to ARM → push N1 for climb thrust.
Hook: "84 kt THR HLD – 800 ft ARM."
x.Q0182:
False. In THR HLD the autothrottle servos are INHIBITED: the pilot can move the thrust levers manually and the A/T won't drive them back. THR HLD protects against unwanted thrust changes during the takeoff roll after 84 kt.
Hook: "THR HLD = A/T hands off."
x.Q0183:
With both F/Ds ON, both pilots' F/D modes come from the MASTER FCC. If an autopilot is engaged, the master is the FCC of the first A/P engaged in CMD – regardless of which F/D was switched on first. CMD B → FCC B is master → it drives the Captain's F/D too (MA light on the F/O side). Without A/P, the first F/D switched on decides.
Hook: "A/P in CMD wins the master battle."
x.Q0184:
False – it's the AUTOTHROTTLE that disengages automatically about 2 seconds after touchdown. The AUTOPILOT must be disengaged MANUALLY after touchdown, and the roll-out is flown manually.
Hook: "A/T leaves by itself; you kick off the A/P."
x.Q0185:
False. It's the APP (approach) mode – not VOR/LOC – that enables engagement of the second autopilot. For a dual-channel approach: APP selected, BOTH VHF NAV receivers tuned to the ILS, and the second A/P in CMD before 800 ft RA. Pushing CMD for the second A/P outside APP mode just swaps autopilots.
Hook: "Second A/P needs APP, both NAVs, before 800 ft."
x.Q0186:
AFS = AFDS (autopilot flight director system) + A/T (autothrottle). The MCP and FMC are what CONTROL them, not parts of the AFS. The FMC feeds N1 limits, target N1 and command speeds.
Hook: "AFS = AFDS + A/T."
x.Q0187:
The FMC provides the N1 limits and target N1 to the autothrottle (and command speeds to A/T and AFDS). The A/T uses FMC N1 limits whether the EECs are ON or in ALTN. There is no separate 'autothrottle computer' feeding limits; the EECs control the engine, not the A/T limits.
Hook: "N1 limits come from the FMC."
x.Q0188:
The second A/P must be engaged in CMD BY 800 FT RA for a dual-channel approach – after that its engagement is inhibited. Other gates: FLARE arms below 1500 ft RA, must be armed by 350 ft RA, flare at 50 ft.
Hook: "Second A/P by 800."
x.Q0189:
The AFDS is a dual system: TWO flight control computers (FCC A and FCC B) and ONE mode control panel. Each FCC drives its own pitch/roll hydraulic servos (through separate hydraulic systems) and its own pilot's F/D bars.
Hook: "Two FCCs (A & B), one MCP."
x.Q0190:
RTO disarms itself after takeoff when both air/ground systems say 'air', but the selector stays in RTO and no light comes on. If you land with RTO still selected (never cycled through OFF): NO automatic braking, and the AUTO BRAKE DISARM light comes on 2 SECONDS after touchdown. Brake manually.
Hook: "Land in RTO → no autobrake, DISARM after 2 s."
x.Q0191:
Corrected after the independent audit: D for the Ryanair fleet. FCOM 4.20.2 (effectivity YF501–YW164): the A/P automatically disengages for 'column or wheel force override'. The 'CWS P, returns to ALT HOLD within 250 ft' behaviour (4.20.8) is marked YA573 only (one older aircraft). Older banks give C – that's the YA573/Classic logic.
Hook: "Our fleet: push the column → A/P off."
x.Q0192:
LVL CHG: the switch lights; PITCH flies the speed (FMA pitch = MCP SPD); THRUST goes to N1 for a climb or RETARD then ARM for a descent; the IAS/MACH window OPENS showing the target speed. In LVL CHG it's the elevator that holds speed, the thrust is fixed (climb N1 or idle).
Hook: "LVL CHG: pitch = speed, thrust = N1 or idle."
x.Q0193:
First TO/GA push below 2000 ft RA (dual A/P approach with FLARE armed): A/T engages in GA and advances toward the REDUCED go-around N1 giving 1000–2000 fpm; pitch TO/GA; the A/Ps STAY ENGAGED (dual A/P go-around). A SECOND push gives FULL go-around N1. Above 2000 ft RA the first push gives full N1.
Hook: "One push = reduced GA; two = full."
x.Q0194:
MCP speed condition symbols appear when the commanded speed can't be reached: flashing 'A' = UNDERSPEED limiting (the AFS is holding minimum speed, so your FMC/selected speed can't be flown); flashing '8' = OVERSPEED limiting (Vmo/Mmo, gear or flap placard).
Hook: "A = too slow (A for 'Alpha'/stall side); 8 = too fast."
x.Q0195:
You can still select a landing autobrake setting after touchdown, as long as you're above 30 kt ground speed – braking starts immediately if the thrust levers are at idle and the wheels have spun up. Normally autobrake begins when both thrust levers are at IDLE and the main wheels spin up.
Hook: "Late autobrake OK above 30 kt."
x.Q0196:
Besides pushing the N1 switch, N1 mode engages AUTOMATICALLY when you engage VNAV in a climb, or LVL CHG in a climb – except during the 2½-minute inhibit period after lift-off (to protect a reduced-thrust/ engine-out takeoff from an automatic thrust increase).
Hook: "Auto N1: VNAV climb, LVL CHG climb after 2½ min."
x.Q0197:
True: the A/T provides automatic thrust from the start of takeoff through climb, cruise, descent, approach and go-around or landing (RETARD in the flare, disengages 2 s after touchdown). It uses a separate servo on each thrust lever.
Hook: "A/T: takeoff to touchdown."
x.Q0198:
Each FCC uses its own radio altimeter. With one radio altimeter inoperative, the autopilot disengages TWO SECONDS after LOC and G/S capture – so no autopilot ILS to minimums. Also: dual-channel A/P needs two generators powering the busses.
Hook: "One RA dead → A/P off 2 s after capture."
x.Q0199:
AFS = autothrottle + autopilot flight director system (AFDS). The MCP is the control panel for them – not a separate 'mode selector system' component.
Hook: "AFS = AFDS + A/T."
x.Q0200:
An illuminated MCP switch light means the mode is selected AND can be DESELECTED by pushing it again. If the mode is active but can't be deselected (inhibited), the light goes OUT even though the mode is engaged – e.g. LOC/GS captured in APP. So the light is about deselection, not just 'engaged'. Always read the FMA for what's engaged.
Hook: "Light on = you can switch it off."
x.Q0201:
With FLARE armed (dual A/P ILS), one TO/GA push: A/Ps stay engaged and fly the go-around, A/T advances to REDUCED go-around N1 (1000–2000 fpm). Second push: full GA N1. The A/P does not disengage and the A/T doesn't go to THR HLD.
Hook: "First push reduced, second push full."
x.Q0202:
Engaging the A/P in CMD after takeoff (no other pitch mode selected): FD status changes to CMD, pitch engages in LVL CHG – shown on the pitch FMA as MCP SPD – and the speed bug goes to V2+20; roll engages in HDG SEL. Above 400 ft RA engaging the A/P terminates the takeoff mode.
Hook: "A/P after takeoff = MCP SPD + HDG SEL."
x.Q0203:
Two A/T modes let you move the thrust levers without the A/T fighting: THR HLD (servos inhibited during takeoff) and ARM (no mode engaged, servos inhibited – but minimum speed protection is still provided). In N1, GA, MCP SPD or FMC SPD the A/T drives the levers.
Hook: "Hands-free for you: THR HLD and ARM."
x.Q0204:
If FLARE isn't armed by about 350 ft RA, BOTH autopilots disengage automatically. Checking 'FLARE armed' at 500 ft gives you warning that the A/Ps will drop out at 350 ft if it isn't – so you can be ready to land manually or go around. The flare itself starts at 50 ft.
Hook: "No FLARE at 500 → expect A/P off at 350."
x.Q0205:
SPD INTV with VNAV engaged: the IAS/MACH window OPENS showing the current FMC target speed, and you can dial a new speed – VNAV stays engaged. Push SPD INTV again: window blanks and the FMC speed resumes. No constraint is deleted.
Hook: "SPD INTV = open the window, VNAV stays."
x.Q0206:
(Older YA573 air system.) A DUCT OVERHEAT light only: the related air mix valves drive FULL COLD (requires reset). If the temperature goes even higher, the pack valve closes and PACK TRIP OFF lights. Bleed trip is an engine bleed thing.
Hook: "Duct overheat → full cold; hotter → pack trips."
x.Q0207:
After lift-off the A/T stays in THR HLD until 800 ft above field elevation (the bank says 800 ft RA), then changes to ARM and you can push N1 for climb thrust. There's no 18-second rule.
Hook: "THR HLD until 800."
x.Q0208:
Antenna switching (tail → nose) happens when a LOCALIZER frequency is selected AND VOR/LOC is annunciated (armed or engaged). If the switching doesn't happen, LOC mode is inhibited. VOR frequencies stay on the tail antenna. Back-course isn't available.
Hook: "LOC freq + VOR/LOC armed → nose antenna."
x.Q0209:
If FLARE is not armed by about 350 ft RA on a dual-channel ILS, BOTH A/Ps disengage automatically. Gates to remember: second A/P by 800 ft, FLARE armed below 1500 ft and by 350 ft, stab trim nose-up at 400 ft, flare at 50 ft, RETARD at 27 ft.
Hook: "No FLARE by 350 → A/Ps off."
x.Q0210:
Main electric trim (thumb switches) and autopilot trim both drive the SAME single electric stabilizer trim motor. That's why there are two cutout switches on the control stand: MAIN ELECT and AUTOPILOT – each disconnects its input from that one motor. Manual trim wheels work through cables and override everything.
Hook: "One trim motor, two cutouts."
x.Q0211:
FLARE ARMED appears on a dual-A/P ILS after LOC and G/S capture and BELOW 1500 ft RA – at the same moment the second A/P couples to the controls and A/P go-around arms. It must be armed by 350 ft; the flare itself engages at 50 ft.
Hook: "FLARE arms below 1500."
x.Q0212:
FLARE engages (and the manoeuvre starts) at about 50 ft RADIO altitude, F/D bars retract, then RETARD at 27 ft and touchdown.
Hook: "Flare at 50, retard at 27."
x.Q0213:
Before THR HLD (84 kt) the A/T is in N1 mode and still drives the levers – the A/T may reposition the thrust levers after you move them, except in THR HLD and ARM. So in a very early RTO, if you only pull the levers back and let go without disengaging the A/T, it will push them forward again to takeoff N1. Disengage the A/T as part of the RTO.
Hook: "Early RTO: kill the A/T or it pushes back."
x.Q0214:
Advancing the thrust lever(s) after braking has started disarms the autobrake and lights AUTO BRAKE DISARM – EXCEPT during the first 3 seconds after touchdown (so a small thrust bump at touchdown doesn't kill it). Other disarm actions: speed brake lever to DOWN, manual braking. Selecting OFF disarms without the light.
Hook: "Thrust disarms autobrake – after the first 3 seconds."
x.Q0215:
Mach trim gives speed stability at high Mach (counters Mach tuck): above M.615 the FCCs, using ADIRU Mach, command the Mach trim actuator, which repositions the elevator feel & centering unit and so moves the elevators up as speed increases. MACH TRIM FAIL light if it fails.
Hook: "Mach trim above .615."
x.Q0216:
The FMC provides the N1 limits and target N1 to the A/T, shown as the thrust mode display (TO, R-TO, CLB, CRZ, G/A, CON) above the N1 gauges. '---' on the thrust mode display means the FMC isn't computing a thrust limit.
Hook: "N1 limits = FMC."
x.Q0217:
AFS = AFDS (autopilots + flight directors together) + A/T. The options that list only A/P, only F/D or 'only' two items are incomplete. 
Hook: "AFS = AFDS + A/T."
x.Q0218:
The AFS flies the HIGHEST of: minimum speed (about 1.3 Vs for the flap setting), FMC speed or selected speed. When minimum speed is the highest – i.e. your FMC/selected speed is below it and can't be flown – the flashing 'A' (underspeed limiting) appears. That's why the bank's answer is 'the highest of all'.
Hook: "AFS flies the highest; 'A' = minimum speed wins."
x.Q0219:
VNAV is a PITCH mode, so it's terminated by selecting another PITCH mode (LVL CHG, V/S, ALT HOLD…) or by glideslope capture. Roll-mode selections (HDG SEL, LNAV, LOC capture) don't affect it.
Hook: "VNAV ends with another pitch mode or G/S."
x.Q0220:
A/T disengaged = the red A/T disengage lights FLASH – no aural tone (only the autopilot has the wailer). A second push of a disengage switch cancels the lights. Steady red/amber = light test; flashing AMBER = A/T speed error (flaps not up, +10/−5 kt).
Hook: "A/T off: flashing red, silent."
x.Q0221:
Flashing 'A' = UNDERSPEED limiting: the AFS is holding minimum speed because the FMC/MCP speed is lower and can't be reached. Flashing '8' = OVERSPEED limiting (Vmo/Mmo, gear or flap limit).
Hook: "A = too slow; 8 = too fast."
x.Q0222:
SPD INTV during VNAV: the IAS/MACH window opens showing the current FMC TARGET SPEED, which you can then change. Not dashes, not 100 kt (100 kt is only what it shows on first power-up).
Hook: "SPD INTV shows the FMC target."
x.Q0223:
Second A/P in CMD by 800 ft RA, or its engagement is inhibited and you stay single-channel (no autoland). 
Hook: "Second A/P by 800."
x.Q0224:
A/T disengages by: A/T ARM switch OFF, pushing either A/T disengage switch, an A/T system fault, 2 seconds after landing touchdown, and certain thrust-lever split/override conditions. 'Immediately the left main gear is compressed' is wrong – it's 2 s after touchdown. The fullest correct list is A.
Hook: "A/T off: ARM off, button, fault, 2 s after touchdown."
x.Q0225:
First TO/GA push below 2000 ft RA with FLARE armed: A/T engages in GA (FMA 'GA', not N1) and advances to REDUCED go-around N1 (1000–2000 fpm). A/Ps remain engaged. Second push = full GA N1.
Hook: "Below 2000: GA, reduced thrust."
x.Q0226:
Aileron trim normally rotates the control wheel and shows on the scale on the column. But with the A/P engaged, the A/P overpowers the trim and holds the wheel where it needs it – so trim applied is NOT reflected on the wheel/scale, and when the A/P disconnects you can get an abrupt roll. Don't use aileron trim with the A/P engaged.
Hook: "A/P on: aileron trim is hidden – and bites at disconnect."
x.Q0227:
The A/T works with EECs ON or ALTN, but with ONE EEC ON and ONE in ALTN the two engines need different lever positions for the same N1, so the thrust levers separate. Keep both EECs in the same mode for minimum lever separation.
Hook: "Mixed EEC modes = staggered levers."
x.Q0228:
On the PFD vertical speed scale: the WHITE pointer = actual vertical speed; the MAGENTA bug = the V/S selected in the MCP window, shown only with V/S pitch mode engaged. (Magenta always = something selected/commanded.)
Hook: "Magenta = selected, white = actual."
x.Q0229:
In CWS, releasing the controls makes the A/P hold the existing attitude. If you release with 6° of bank or less, it rolls wings level and holds the heading; with more than 6° it keeps the bank. Heading hold is inhibited below 1500 ft RA with gear down, after LOC capture, or after VOR capture at ≤250 kt TAS.
Hook: "CWS: ≤6° rolls level."
x.Q0230:
After a normal (all-engine) takeoff the F/D holds 15° until climb rate is sufficient, then commands MCP speed (normally V2) + 20 kt. With an engine failure the target becomes V2 / existing speed between V2 and V2+20 / V2+20.
Hook: "All engines: V2 + 20."
x.Q0231:
The A/T stays in THR HLD until 800 ft above field (aerodrome) elevation, then changes to ARM; push N1 for climb thrust (or it reduces automatically at the thrust reduction altitude).
Hook: "THR HLD until 800 ft AAL."
x.Q0232:
