The FMC descent path is an idle-thrust path. If a restriction forces the aircraft below that path early, after the first 'at' or 'at or below' restriction the path is LEVEL until it re-intercepts the original idle descent path, then descends at idle again (picture option A).
Hook: "Below the path? Fly level until you meet it."
x.Q0233:
Automatic (A/P) go-around below 2000 ft without the TOGA-to-LNAV feature: thrust FMA = GA, roll FMA = BLANK (ground track hold), pitch FMA = TO/GA. N1 appears only for go-arounds started at/above 2000 ft.
Hook: "GA : blank : TO/GA."
x.Q0234:
On aircraft with TOGA-to-LNAV (YW059–YW164) and a missed approach in the route, LNAV is already ARMED (white) on the approach. Pressing TO/GA gives: GA : LNAV (white, armed) : TO/GA. During autoland LNAV engages above 400 ft (below that track hold); F/D-only above 50 ft.
Hook: "TOGA to LNAV: GA – LNAV(white) – TO/GA."
x.Q0235:
A/T disconnect: red A/T disengage lights FLASH, NO aural. Push a disengage switch again to extinguish them. The wailer (minimum 2 s) belongs to the AUTOPILOT disconnect.
Hook: "A/T = silent flash; A/P = wailer."
x.Q0236:
Flashing 'A' = underspeed limiting (minimum speed). Alpha floor (non-VNAV modes): if speed drops below minimum, the A/T goes to MCP SPD, the 'A' appears in the speed window and thrust advances until 5 kt above minimum speed, then the 'A' disappears. In approach (gear down, flaps ≥15, below 800 ft) the A/T flies the SMYD minimum speed.
Hook: "'A' = alpha floor/underspeed, +5 kt."
x.Q0237:
True – in THR HLD the A/T servos are inhibited and the pilot can set the thrust levers manually (e.g. for an RTO after 84 kt or a manual thrust correction).
Hook: "THR HLD = pilot's levers."
x.Q0238:
FLARE engages at 50 ft RA on a dual-channel ILS (armed below 1500 ft). 300/200/150 ft are distractors.
Hook: "Flare at 50."
x.Q0239:
An A/P go-around needs DUAL A/P (armed when FLARE armed shows). On a SINGLE A/P approach there's no autoland and no A/P go-around: pushing TO/GA below 2000 ft RA disengages the A/P and you fly a MANUAL F/D go-around.
Hook: "Single A/P + TO/GA = hand-flown F/D go-around."
x.Q0240:
Single-engine F/D go-around: F/D pitch commands 13° nose up, then as climb rate increases it commands a target speed (MCP approach speed, or depending on when the engine failed, the speed at failure/current speed). Compare: takeoff 15°, go-around two engines 15°.
Hook: "One engine GA = 13°."
x.Q0241:
At about 50 ft RA the flare manoeuvre starts, FLARE engaged is annunciated and the F/D bars retract. RETARD follows at 27 ft.
Hook: "50 ft: FLARE, bars gone."
x.Q0242:
TO/GA takeoff F/D pitch: 10° NOSE DOWN until 60 kt, then 15° NOSE UP after 60 kt (that's when the bars jump up), 15° after lift-off until climb rate is sufficient, then MCP speed + 20. 84 kt is THR HLD, not a pitch change.
Hook: "60 kt: bars to 15° up."
x.Q0243:
When you select RTO the AUTO BRAKE DISARM light flashes for 1–2 seconds – normal. If it comes on and stays on while taxiing, there's a MALFUNCTION in the autobrake system: select AUTO BRAKE OFF; if the light stays illuminated, do not take off (QRH). Don't touch the antiskid switch.
Hook: "DISARM steady before takeoff = autobrake fault, don't go."
x.Q0244:
True. Climb in LVL CHG or VNAV → A/T N1 automatically (LVL CHG has the 2½-minute inhibit after lift-off). Descent in LVL CHG/VNAV → RETARD then ARM at idle. ALT ACQ/ALT HOLD outside VNAV and G/S capture → MCP SPD.
Hook: "Climb = N1, descent = RETARD/ARM."
x.Q0246:
The flashing 'A' (underspeed limiting) and the limit speed stay until you select a speed that doesn't violate the limit – and specifically a speed at least 15 kt ABOVE the minimum speed to remove the underspeed symbol. Pushing the knob or engaging CMD B does nothing for it.
Hook: "Kill the 'A': min speed + 15."
x.Q0247:
After the restriction, ALT INTV removes the constraint, so the airplane is now BELOW the original idle path = 'early descent'. In early descent VNAV commands 1000 fpm until it intercepts the idle descent path (path B). Compare: without ALT INTV the FMC path goes LEVEL until it meets the idle path (path A).
Hook: "Below the path in VNAV DES = 1000 fpm until intercept."
x.Q0248:
Engine failure after lift-off, F/D pitch target: below V2 → V2; between V2 and V2+20 → existing speed; above V2+20 → V2+20. So 'all of the above'. Failure on the ground: V2 or lift-off speed, whichever is higher.
Hook: "V2 floor, V2+20 ceiling, otherwise keep what you have."
x.Q0249:
The FMC provides the N1 limit values to the A/T. If the FMC isn't providing them, A/T LIM appears and a degraded limit is used.
Hook: "N1 limits = FMC."
x.Q0250:
False. In ARM no A/T mode is engaged and the servos are inhibited – the pilot sets thrust (minimum speed protection still available). Holding the selected N1 limit is N1 mode.
Hook: "ARM = armed, not working."
x.Q0251:
The character is a flashing '8' (looks like a B): OVERSPEED limiting – the selected speed is above Vmo/Mmo, the gear limit or the flap limit, so the AFS flies the limit instead. It has nothing to do with autopilot B.
Hook: "8 = overspeed (looks like B)."
x.Q0252:
LNAV disconnects at: end of the active route, a ROUTE DISCONTINUITY, intercepting the approach course in VOR LOC/APP, selecting HDG SEL, or loss of capture criteria. VNAV and G/S capture are pitch events and don't affect LNAV.
Hook: "Discontinuity = LNAV drops."
x.Q0253:
All correct: LNAV terminates on loss of capture criteria, selecting HDG SEL, and VOR/LOC capture – plus end of route and route discontinuity.
Hook: "LNAV ends: end, gap, HDG, LOC, lost."
x.Q0254:
LVL CHG FMA: PITCH = MCP SPD (elevator holds speed); A/T = N1 in a climb, RETARD then ARM in a descent.
Hook: "LVL CHG: pitch speed, thrust N1/idle."
x.Q0255:
False. Minimum speed reversion is NOT available with the A/T OFF in ALT HOLD or after G/S capture, nor in VNAV PTH on a level segment – the pitch mode can't give up altitude/path to save speed, so you must watch the speed and add thrust yourself.
Hook: "A/T off + ALT HOLD/GS = no speed protection."
x.Q0256:
True. STAB TRIM AUTOPILOT cutout → CUTOUT deactivates autopilot stab trim and DISENGAGES the autopilot (the A/P can't fly without trimming). It's also a condition for engagement: the A/P can't be engaged unless that switch is at NORMAL.
Hook: "No A/P trim, no A/P."
x.Q0257:
False (corrected after the independent audit). The FCOM schematic on 11.20.7 shows a separate AUTOTHROTTLE COMPUTER, next to FCC A and FCC B (the two flight control computers of the AFDS). FCOM 4.20.1: the AFS consists of the AFDS (two FCCs) AND the autothrottle. So the A/T is not 'controlled by FCC A only'. Some old banks mark True – the FCOM doesn't support it.
Hook: "A/T has its own computer."
x.Q0258:
True. Even with CMD engaged, an axis drops into CWS when no command mode is selected for it or when you override it with control force – shown as CWS P / CWS R on the FMA. CWS R with CMD can even be used to intercept a VOR/LOC course.
Hook: "CMD can still give you CWS P/R."
x.Q0259:
True. In ALT HOLD at the MCP altitude, setting a new MCP altitude more than 100 ft away ARMS V/S (and lights the ALT HLD switch); moving the V/S thumbwheel then engages V/S. LVL CHG, V/S and VNAV climbs/descents are inhibited until a new altitude is set.
Hook: "New altitude > 100 ft → V/S armed."
x.Q0261:
True. A/P engagement (CMD or CWS) is inhibited unless (1) no force is applied to the control wheel and (2) the STAB TRIM AUTOPILOT cutout switch is at NORMAL.
Hook: "Hands off the wheel, trim cutout normal."
x.Q0262:
Both A/Ps disengage if FLARE isn't armed by about 350 ft RA. (400 ft = extra nose-up stab trim; 50 ft = flare.)
Hook: "350 or bust."
x.Q0263:
Flare starts at about 50 ft RA and finishes at touchdown. 27 ft is when the A/T starts RETARD – don't mix them.
Hook: "50 flare, 27 retard."
x.Q0264:
True – the A/T disengages automatically about 2 s after touchdown, and in that case the A/T disengage lights do NOT come on. The A/P you must disengage yourself.
Hook: "A/T off at +2 s, no lights."
x.Q0266:
FCOM 10.41.4 (ND symbols table), row 'Wind direction/speed and wind arrow', mode 'All': 'Displayed if wind magnitude is greater than 6 knots and blanked if wind magnitude becomes less than 4 knots.' → answer: displayed if wind > 6 kt.
Why not the others: it's blanked below 4 kt (not 6), and it shows in ALL modes, not only MAP or ILS.
Hook: "Wind appears above 6, disappears below 4."
x.Q0267:
True. Using either pilot's control-wheel stab trim switches disengages the A/P (main electric trim and A/P trim share one motor – you're taking over).
Hook: "Thumb-trim = A/P off."
x.Q0268:
A/T disconnect = the red A/T disengage light FLASHES, no sound. Steady = test switch. Bells and tones are other systems (fire bell, A/P wailer).
Hook: "A/T off = silent flashing red."
x.Q0269:
Single-channel or F/D-only approach: if a persistent LOC/GS beam anomaly or ground station failure is detected, the autopilot disengages and/or the F/D bars are removed – so you can't follow bad guidance. Revert to raw data / go around.
Hook: "Bad beam → A/P and bars go."
x.Q0270:
RTO at 100 kt (above 88 kt wheel speed): MAXIMUM braking is applied automatically as soon as the thrust levers are retarded to IDLE. Below 88 kt nothing happens and RTO stays armed. Speed brakes deploy from the speed brake lever logic (ARMED/RTO), not from this autobrake answer.
Hook: "RTO ≥ 88 kt + idle = max brakes."
x.Q0271:
Latest point for the second A/P CMD: 800 ft RA.
Hook: "Second A/P by 800."
x.Q0273:
A/T disengages: A/T ARM switch OFF, either A/T disengage switch pushed, an A/T system fault, 2 s after touchdown (not 'immediately'), and some lever split/override conditions. The stick shaker doesn't disconnect it.
Hook: "Switch off, button, fault, +2 s."
x.Q0274:
A/T: automatically, 2 s after touchdown. A/P: manually after touchdown; roll-out is flown by hand.
Hook: "A/T leaves, A/P you kick."
x.Q0275:
True. The G/S can be captured from above or below, at 2/5 dot – but only after the localizer is captured (LOC capture by 1/2 dot). On G/S capture the previous pitch mode drops and GA appears on the thrust mode display.
Hook: "GS: LOC first, above or below, 2/5 dot."
x.Q0276:
LNAV drops at a ROUTE DISCONTINUITY (also end of route, LOC/VOR capture, selecting HDG SEL, loss of capture). VNAV engagement and G/S capture don't affect it; it's SELECTING HDG SEL, not 'disengaging' it.
Hook: "Gap in the route = LNAV off."
x.Q0277:
After takeoff with LNAV armed and the A/P engaged before VNAV: thrust N1 (climb thrust), roll LNAV, pitch MCP SPD (LVL CHG). FMC SPD would need VNAV; THR HLD only lasts until 800 ft.
Hook: "N1 : LNAV : MCP SPD."
x.Q0278:
APP mode must be selected before the second A/P can be engaged in CMD. The second A/P is then armed and couples automatically after LOC and G/S capture and below 1500 ft RA. In VOR LOC mode, pushing the other CMD just swaps A/Ps.
Hook: "Second A/P only in APP."
x.Q0279:
APP must be selected first. Outside approach mode, pushing the second CMD switch just engages that A/P and disengages the first one. With APP selected and both NAVs on the ILS, the second A/P can be engaged (before 800 ft RA).
Hook: "Two A/Ps only in APP."
x.Q0280:
Single A/P ILS, TO/GA below 2000 ft RA: the A/P DISENGAGES (no flare armed), the F/D go-around engages (TO/GA pitch) and the A/T (armed below 2000 ft) engages GA and advances to REDUCED go-around N1. So all options happen. You hand-fly the F/D go-around.
Hook: "Single A/P + TO/GA = A/P off, F/D GA, reduced thrust."
x.Q0281:
LNAV armed on the ground engages at 50 ft RA after takeoff; VNAV armed engages at 400 ft. (In a TOGA-to-LNAV go-around during autoland, LNAV engages above 400 ft.)
Hook: "LNAV 50, VNAV 400."
x.Q0282:
False. The RECEIVER SWITCHES are on the AUDIO CONTROL PANEL (ACP), not on the Radio Tuning Panel: FCOM 5.10.5 'Receiver Switches – Rotate – adjusts volume; Push – allows reception…'. The RTP only selects and tunes frequencies.
Hook: "RTP tunes; ACP listens (and sets volume)."
x.Q0283:
False – it's the other way round. The LOWER fuselage antennas (VHF-2 and VHF-3) are susceptible to multipath interference from nearby structures or vehicles; the UPPER antenna (VHF-1) is less susceptible. So on the ground VHF-1 is usually the cleanest.
Hook: "Low antennas get the bounce."
x.Q0284:
The PILOT CALL switch is on the external power connector panel (for ground crew): pushing it sounds a SINGLE-tone chime in the FLIGHT DECK and lights the blue CALL light. Two-tone chime + pink lights is the ATTEND call to the cabin.
Hook: "Calls TO the flight deck = single chime + blue light."
x.Q0285:
Three microphones: HAND mic, headset BOOM mic and OXYGEN MASK mic (MASK–BOOM switch on the ACP chooses between mask and boom). The overhead speaker is only for listening.
Hook: "Hand, boom, mask."
x.Q0286:
True. The SERVICE INTERPHONE switch only adds or removes the EXTERNAL service jacks (ground crew around the aircraft). With it OFF the flight deck can still talk to the flight attendants.
Hook: "Service interphone OFF = outside jacks off only."
x.Q0287:
Cabin call lights: PINK = flight deck or another attendant station; BLUE = passenger seat call; AMBER = lavatory call.
Hook: "Pink crew, blue seat, amber toilet."
x.Q0288:
VOICE RECORDER switch: ON = powers the CVR before engine start (e.g. preflight briefings), then at first engine start it trips to AUTO. AUTO = powers the CVR from first engine start until 5 minutes after the last engine shutdown.
Hook: "ON until start, then AUTO; AUTO until 5 min after shutdown."
x.Q0289:
True. FCOM 5.20.4: 'The flight interphone system is an independent communication network. Its primary purpose is to provide private communication between flight deck crewmembers without intrusion from the service interphone system.' Service interphone = flight deck ↔ cabin attendants ↔ external service jacks.
Hook: "Flight interphone = pilots' private line."
x.Q0290:
ACP Filter switch: V = VOICE (NAV/ADF voice), B = BOTH, R = RANGE (the Morse station identifier). Use R to identify a navaid.
Hook: "V-B-R: Voice, Both, Range."
x.Q0291:
Blank displays and the OFF switch lit = the RTP has been switched OFF (disconnected from the radios). Push OFF again to reconnect. Nothing is broken – a common start-up trap.
Hook: "Blank RTP? Push OFF."
x.Q0292:
Corrected after the independent audit: A. FCOM 5.10.2, radio tuning panel TEST switch: 'removes automatic squelch feature… improves reception of weak signals.' Weak (distant) stations become audible → better reception range. Tuning VHF 1 and 2 to the same frequency is not an FCOM method.
Hook: "VHF TEST = squelch off = hear the weak ones."
x.Q0293:
CPDLC/ACARS use VHF-3 in DATA mode: on the RTP select VHF-3, turn the frequency selector until 'DATA' appears in the STANDBY window, then transfer it to ACTIVE. The RTP shows DATA when that radio is in data mode (FCOM 5.10.1); the step-by-step is RYR procedure.
Hook: "VHF 3 → DATA → transfer."
x.Q0294:
To hear NAV/ADF voice AND range (ident) audio, set the ACP Filter switch to B (Both).
Hook: "B = Both."
x.Q0295:
The mask microphone becomes active when the mask is taken out of its stowage box (doors open) – then select MASK on the ACP MASK–BOOM switch to transmit through it. The RESET/TEST lever with the mask out also keeps the mic and regulator active.
Hook: "Mask out = mask mic live."
x.Q0296:
RYR CVR: four channels, 120 minutes, older audio erased automatically. One channel is the area mic; the others are the pilots' and observer's ACP audio. Underwater locator beacon works 90 days. ERASE only on the ground with the parking brake set.
Hook: "4 channels, 120 min, beacon 90 days."
x.Q0297:
FCOM 5.20.3: in ALT (degraded) mode 'the crewmember can only communicate on one radio' – and the table on 5.20.4 'Radio available for transmission and reception': CAPTAIN VHF-1, FIRST OFFICER VHF-2, OBSERVER VHF-1. So the F/O transmits AND receives on VHF-2 only.
Hook: "F/O in ALT = VHF-2 only."
x.Q0298:
ATTEND call switch (forward overhead): TWO-tone chime in the passenger cabin and BOTH pink master call lights. A call to the flight deck is the single chime and blue CALL light.
Hook: "Calling the cabin = two-tone + pink."
x.Q0299:
Maximum CVR recording: 120 minutes (4 channels).
Hook: "CVR = 2 hours."
x.Q0300:
The HF SENS control on the RTP adjusts the sensitivity of the ON-SIDE HF receiver only – nothing to do with VHF or data.
Hook: "HF SENS = my side's HF."
x.Q0301:
A call from the flight deck shows PINK in the cabin (with a two-tone chime). Blue = passenger seat, amber = lavatory.
Hook: "Pink = crew calling."
x.Q0302:
White OFFSIDE TUNING light: this RTP is tuning a radio it doesn't normally control (e.g. RTP-1 tuning VHF-2), or its own radio is being tuned by another RTP. Reminder to check who tunes what.
Hook: "Offside light = cross-tuning."
x.Q0303:
Offside tuning light = cross-tuning in either direction: your radio is being tuned by another panel, or your panel is tuning someone else's radio. It doesn't mean a failure.
Hook: "Offside = someone's tuning someone else's radio."
x.Q0304:
Attendant calls the flight deck (CAPTAIN/PILOT call on the handset): SINGLE-tone chime in the flight deck and the BLUE flight deck CALL light illuminates (steady).
Hook: "To the cockpit: single chime, blue light."
x.Q0307:
On the attendant handset keypad the PILOT call is '2' (ATTENDANT 5, PA 8 – printed on the handset). So from the cabin interphone, press 2 to call the flight deck.
Hook: "2 for the pilots, 5 attendants, 8 PA."
x.Q0308:
CVR AUTO: powered from first engine start until 5 minutes after the last engine shutdown. ON powers it before start and trips to AUTO at engine start. Nothing to do with the FDR.
Hook: "AUTO = engine start → +5 min after shutdown."
x.Q0309:
Degraded ACP: at that station altitude alert, GPWS and windshear AURAL warnings are NOT heard (still heard on the other side if that ACP is normal). Also: transmitter and receiver selectors don't work, no speaker, no flight or service interphone, no PA through the ACP, no hand mic. Captain's usable radio is VHF-1.
Hook: "Degraded = no aural warnings on that side."
x.Q0310:
ALT on the ACP: that ACP is inoperative (degraded mode) but the crewmember can still communicate on ONE radio (Capt/Obs VHF-1, F/O VHF-2) using boom or mask mic. No PA, no interphone.
Hook: "ALT = ACP dead, one radio left."
x.Q0311:
STANDBY POWER switch in AUTO: the standby busses switch from normal to battery (alternate) power if power is lost from EITHER AC transfer bus 1 OR DC bus 1 – the '1' side feeds the standby system. Losing DC bus 2 alone doesn't trigger it.
Hook: "Standby watches the No. 1 side: XFR 1 or DC 1."
x.Q0312:
Normal: DC STANDBY bus ← TR1, TR2 and TR3; AC STANDBY bus ← AC transfer bus 1; battery bus ← TR3; hot battery buses ← battery/charger. With all AC lost, the battery powers DC standby and (via the static inverter) AC standby.
Hook: "DC standby has all three TRs."
x.Q0313:
After loss of all engine/APU AC power, the standby system gives 115 V AC (from the battery through the static inverter, on the AC standby bus) and 24 V DC (battery: DC standby bus, battery bus, hot battery buses). 22–30 V is just the battery's voltage range.
Hook: "Standby = 115 AC + 24 DC."
x.Q0314:
Normally the cross bus tie relay is CLOSED, so DC bus 1, DC bus 2 and DC standby are tied together and BOTH TR1 and TR2 feed DC bus 1 (and bus 2 and standby). TR3 feeds the battery bus and backs up TR1/TR2. Any two TRs can carry the whole load.
Hook: "Tie closed: TR1 + TR2 feed everything."
x.Q0315:
DC bus 1 and DC bus 2 are isolated when the cross bus tie relay opens, which happens automatically at G/S capture on an F/D or A/P ILS approach (so one failure can't take out both nav receivers/FCCs) and when the BUS TRANSFER switch is OFF. So all answers are true.
Hook: "GS capture or BUS TRANSFER OFF → DC busses split."
x.Q0316:
Generator DISCONNECT (guarded): disconnects the IDG from the engine (needs electrical power and start lever at IDLE) and the amber DRIVE light comes on (IDG low oil pressure). It can only be reconnected on the ground by maintenance. The transfer bus then gets power via the BTBs from another source.
Hook: "DISCONNECT = DRIVE light, no way back in flight."
x.Q0317:
The GROUND SERVICE switch (forward attendant panel, momentary) sends ground power directly to the AC ground service busses – utility outlets, cabin lighting and the battery charger – without powering the whole aircraft. It's overridden when both transfer busses are powered.
Hook: "Ground service = cleaners' power, not the whole aircraft."
x.Q0318:
With all AC lost, the AC standby bus is fed by the STATIC INVERTER, which converts 24 V DC from the battery into 115 V AC. TRs do the opposite (AC → DC).
Hook: "Inverter: battery DC → standby AC."
x.Q0319:
In flight with the APU as the ONLY power source: ALL galley and main busses are shed straight away (then IFE busses if still overloaded). On the ground the APU tries to carry the full load and sheds only if overloaded.
Hook: "APU alone in flight = galleys and mains off."
x.Q0320:
Red guards mark switches whose action can't be undone in flight – the IDG DISCONNECT can only be reset on the ground by maintenance. So: red guard = irreversible.
Hook: "Red guard = no undo."
x.Q0321:
ELEC light (amber): a fault exists in the DC power system OR the standby power system. It only works on the ground – a maintenance alert.
Hook: "ELEC = DC or standby fault, ground only."
x.Q0322:
Both battery chargers are fed from the AC GROUND SERVICE busses: main charger ← ground service bus 2, auxiliary charger ← ground service bus 1. (That's why the ground service switch can charge the batteries without powering the aircraft.)
Hook: "Chargers live on ground service: main 2, aux 1."
x.Q0323:
Two fully charged batteries (main + auxiliary, 24 V Ni-Cd, in parallel on standby) provide standby power for a MINIMUM of 60 minutes.
Hook: "Two batteries, at least an hour."
x.Q0324:
Single generator overload shedding order: 1) galleys + main bus on TRANSFER BUS 2, 2) galleys + main bus on transfer bus 1, 3) IFE busses. Restored automatically with two generators, or try CAB/UTIL OFF then ON.
Hook: "Shed 2, then 1, then IFE."
x.Q0325:
On the ground with engines off, the LAST source selected powers BOTH transfer busses – you can't split external power on one bus and APU on the other. Selecting APU GEN ON disconnects ground power and puts the APU on both busses.
Hook: "Last source selected takes both busses."
x.Q0326:
GRD PWR ON removes the previous sources (APU and GEN 2) and puts ground power on BOTH transfer busses. SOURCE OFF lights stay out, because a source (ground power) has been manually selected for the busses.
Hook: "GRD PWR ON = GPU everything, no SOURCE OFF."
x.Q0327:
Keeping both AC transfer busses powered is the job of the BUS TIE BREAKERS (BTBs), with BUS TRANSFER in AUTO: if one source fails, the BTBs connect that transfer bus to another source through the tie bus.
Hook: "BTBs keep the busses alive."
x.Q0328:
IRS power: LEFT IRS ← AC standby bus; RIGHT IRS ← AC transfer bus 2. Both switch automatically to DC from the SWITCHED HOT BATTERY bus if AC fails (ON DC light) – but the RIGHT IRS backup is cut after 5 minutes to save the battery. So on standby power you keep the left IRS.
Hook: "Right IRS: XFR 2, battery 5 min only."
x.Q0329:
TR UNIT light: ON THE GROUND = ANY TR failed (so you don't dispatch with one). IN FLIGHT = TR1 failed, or TR2 AND TR3 failed.
Hook: "Ground: any TR. Air: TR1, or 2 & 3."
x.Q0330:
TR1 ← transfer bus 1, TR2 ← transfer bus 2, TR3 ← transfer bus 2 normally, with transfer bus 1 as backup (BUS TRANSFER AUTO).
Hook: "TR3 lives on bus 2."
x.Q0331:
The HOT BATTERY BUS is always connected to the battery – no switch – so items that must always work (e.g. fire extinguisher squibs, cargo fire suppression) are on it. The SWITCHED hot battery bus needs the battery switch ON.
Hook: "Hot = always."
x.Q0332:
Cargo SMOKE DETECTION ← DC bus 1 and DC bus 2 (one per loop; lose one and it goes single-loop). Cargo FIRE SUPPRESSION (bottle) ← HOT battery bus, so you can always discharge.
Hook: "Detect on DC 1&2, extinguish on hot battery."
x.Q0333:
APU start power: No. 1 AC TRANSFER BUS if AC is available, otherwise the MAIN BATTERY (the starter-generator uses whichever). The battery switch must be ON – switching it OFF shuts the APU down.
Hook: "APU starts on XFR 1, or battery."
x.Q0334:
The ground service switch is on the FORWARD attendant panel.
Hook: "Ground service = front door panel."
x.Q0335:
Each AC side = transfer bus → main bus + two galley busses + ground service bus. So the galley busses are powered from the AC TRANSFER busses (and are the first to be shed).
Hook: "Galleys hang off the transfer busses."
x.Q0336:
ON DC steady = that IRS is running on backup DC from the SWITCHED HOT BATTERY bus (its AC is lost). On the ground the nose-wheel-well horn also sounds to warn ground crew. Right IRS DC backup lasts only 5 min.
Hook: "ON DC = on the battery."
x.Q0337:
False – order is transfer bus 2 first, then transfer bus 1, then IFE busses.
Hook: "2 before 1."
x.Q0338:
BAT DISCHARGE (amber) = with the battery switch ON, the battery is discharging excessively (e.g. you're on battery, or charger failed). Not overcharge, not meter position.
Hook: "BAT DISCHARGE = battery draining."
x.Q0339:
GEN OFF BUS (blue) = that IDG is not supplying its TRANSFER bus (e.g. not connected yet, engine off, or tripped). The bus itself may still be powered via the BTBs – TRANSFER BUS OFF tells you if it isn't.
Hook: "GEN OFF BUS = generator not connected."
x.Q0340:
STANDBY PWR OFF (amber) = one or more of: AC standby bus, DC standby bus, battery bus unpowered. Of the options only 'AC standby bus' is on that list.
Hook: "STBY PWR OFF: AC stby, DC stby, BAT bus."
x.Q0503:
On our aircraft (YF501–YW164) the NO SMOKING signs are ALWAYS illuminated and the switch is placarded INOP. Only the old YA573 has a working NO SMOKING switch (AUTO = on with gear down). FASTEN BELTS still has OFF/AUTO/ON.
Hook: "No smoking – always on."
x.Q0575:
The 28 V DC overwing flight lock depends on: engine speed, thrust lever position, air/ground mode, entry door status – and needs DC power (lose DC and the exits UNLOCK so they can always be opened). Lock condition: 3 of 4 entry/service doors closed + an engine running + in the air or both thrust levers advanced.
Hook: "Engines, thrust, air/ground, doors – and DC."
x.Q0816:
Current FCOM (737-800 with winglets): minimum pavement for a 180° turn = 79.7 ft = 24.3 m. This bank offers 24.1 (older figure) – pick the option closest to 24.3; 20.4 m is the 737-700.
Hook: "180° turn ≈ 24 m."
x.Q1088:
FASTEN BELTS in AUTO: ON when flaps OR gear are extended, OFF when flaps AND gear are retracted. No altitude logic. A low tone sounds in the cabin when the signs change.
Hook: "Flaps or gear out = belts on."
x.Q1093:
Logo lights sit on top of EACH horizontal stabilizer, shining on both sides of the fin (to light the logo). Wingtips carry position lights and strobes.
Hook: "Logo lights on the tailplane, pointing at the fin."
x.Q0341:
RECIRC FAN logic in flight (AUTO): LEFT fan stops if EITHER pack is in HIGH; RIGHT fan stops only if BOTH packs are in HIGH. So both packs HIGH → NEITHER fan runs. (On the ground the right fan runs even with both HIGH.) Packs in HIGH already supply max airflow, so recirc isn't needed.
Hook: "Left: either HIGH. Right: both HIGH."
x.Q0446:
After engine start the DUAL BLEED light is normal while the APU bleed is still open. The action: APU BLEED switch OFF (After Start procedure) – the light goes out and you can taxi with normal thrust. Until then keep thrust at idle.
Hook: "DUAL BLEED after start → APU bleed OFF."
x.Q0479:
Before start: APU bleed ON and engine BLEED switches ON → DUAL BLEED is lit – that's NORMAL (the APU bleed is needed for the start). Keep thrust at idle while it's on; it goes out when you switch APU bleed OFF after start.
Hook: "DUAL BLEED before start = normal."
x.Q0504:
DUAL BLEED = APU bleed valve open AND engine 1 BLEED switch ON (same side of the duct), OR engine 2 BLEED switch ON with the isolation valve OPEN. Option A has the isolation valve closed – then engine 2 can't reach the APU, so no light.
Hook: "APU + eng 1 = DUAL; eng 2 only via an open isolation valve."
x.Q0524:
PACK light only on recall and gone after reset = failure of EITHER the primary OR the standby pack control; the pack still works on the other one. Steady = trip off or both controls failed.
Hook: "Recall-only PACK = one control failed."
x.Q0543:
No-engine-bleed (unpressurised) takeoff: at NOT LESS THAN 400 ft and BEFORE 2000 ft above field elevation, put engine No 2 BLEED ON first, then APU bleed OFF, and engine 1 bleed ON once the cabin rate stabilises. (If an engine fails: wait until 1500 ft/obstacle clearance.)
Hook: "400–2000 ft: bleed 2 on first."
x.Q0572:
AUTO + both bleeds ON + both packs AUTO/HIGH → isolation valve fully CLOSED (each side independent). It opens if any bleed or pack switch goes OFF. It's AC-operated, and the APU bleed switch has no effect on it.
Hook: "Everything ON = isolation closed."
x.Q0806:
AUTO FAIL ALONE = DUAL controller failure → go to MANUAL. AUTO FAIL + ALTN = single failure, the other controller has already taken over. Nothing to do with passenger oxygen.
Hook: "AUTO FAIL alone = both gone → MAN."
x.Q1019:
Note (audit): reading the placard strictly, FL290 lies between FL260 (6,000) and FL320 (8,000); 'approximately 6000' is the only sensible option. The CABIN/FLIGHT ALTITUDE placard on the pressurisation panel tells you the cabin altitude to aim for at each flight altitude when in MANUAL. It reads FL220 → 4,000, FL260 → 6,000, FL320 → 8,000 cabin. FL290 lies between FL260 and FL320, so the target is about 6,000 ft (bank answer).
Hook: "Placard: 160/2000, 220/4000, 260/6000, 320/8000."
x.Q1058:
The ram air DEFLECTOR doors (in front of the ram inlets) extend ON THE GROUND only – commanded by the air/ground sensor – to stop slush/water ingestion before lift-off and after touchdown. The ram INLET doors are what open fully on the ground and in slow flight.
Hook: "Deflectors = ground only, against slush."
x.Q1071:
CONT CAB ZONE TEMP (steady) has TWO possible meanings: a flight deck duct overheat OR failure of both the primary and standby flight deck temperature controls. So the answer that includes both is correct.
Hook: "CONT CAB steady = overheat or both controls."
x.Q0512:
FWD WINDOW HEAT switch → window No 1 only (L1/R1, the windshield). SIDE → window No 2. Window No 3 is acrylic and not electrically heated (it gets warm air). So LEFT FWD = L1 only.
Hook: "FWD = 1, SIDE = 2, 3 = none."
x.Q0513:
On the ground with WING ANTI-ICE ON, advancing thrust above the takeoff warning setting CLOSES both valves, but the switch REMAINS ON. (It then trips OFF automatically at lift-off.)
Hook: "Takeoff thrust: valves close, switch stays."
x.Q0522:
With all switches ON, a green ON light going out most likely means that window is at the CORRECT TEMPERATURE (the heat cycles). Failure/overheat would bring other indications.
Hook: "Green out = warm enough."
x.Q0577:
Wing anti-ice is used when icing conditions exist – in flight as a DE-ICER (primary: let some ice form, then switch on) or as an ANTI-ICER (secondary), and on the ground between engine start and takeoff in icing conditions (unless protected by Type II/IV fluid). It is not 'flight only', and the SAT −40 rule is about engine anti-ice in climb/cruise.
Hook: "Wing anti-ice: de-icer first choice; also on ground in icing."
x.Q0590:
RYR: engine anti-ice ON immediately after both engines are started (part of the after-start flow) and keep it on for all ground operations in icing conditions. Use temperature + visible moisture criteria, not visual ice cues. Don't use it above 10 °C OAT.
Hook: "Icing on ground: ENG anti-ice right after start."
x.Q0600:
Static ports are not heated; pitots (incl. aux and elevator), TAT probe and alpha vanes are.
Hook: "Static ports – no heat."
x.Q0738:
WING ANTI-ICE ON in flight: valves open and the stick shaker logic is set for icing for the REMAINDER of the flight, whatever you do with the switch later. VREF is not adjusted automatically.
Hook: "Wing anti-ice: shaker icing logic all flight."
x.Q1062:
Window heat PWR TEST forces the controller to full power to give a CONFIDENCE test of the heating (ON lights should illuminate). The overheat protection is tested with the OVHT position, not PWR TEST. It's not a mandatory before-every-flight item.
Hook: "PWR TEST = confidence; OVHT = overheat test."
x.Q1076:
The alpha vanes (AOA sensors for stall warning, A/T, A/P and autoslats) are electrically heated together with the pitots and TAT probe, controlled by the PROBE HEAT switches. Window heat and wing anti-ice have nothing to do with them.
Hook: "Alpha vanes = PROBE HEAT."
x.Q1099:
FCOM 3.20.5: 'Pitot probes, the total air temperature probe and the alpha vanes are electrically heated' → the alpha vanes have their own electric (115 V AC) heating elements, controlled by the PROBE HEAT switches (see the L/R ALPHA lights on the Probe Heat panel, 3.10.3). Not window heat, not engine anti-ice, not linked to the alternate static ports.
Hook: "Alpha vanes = PROBE HEAT."
x.Q1117:
If window heat is inoperative, observe a maximum of 250 kt BELOW 10,000 ft. Reason: heated windows are stronger against bird strikes, and birds are mostly below 10,000 ft. Above 10,000 ft no extra limit.
Hook: "No window heat → 250 below 10."
x.Q0773:
With VNAV engaged the FMC commands BOTH the AFDS pitch modes (VNAV SPD / VNAV PTH) and the A/T modes (FMC SPD, N1, RETARD, ARM) to fly the vertical profile. The MCP speed window blanks.
Hook: "VNAV = FMC flies pitch and thrust."
x.Q1067:
CWS roll: release the wheel with 6° of bank OR LESS and the A/P rolls wings level and holds heading; more than 6° and it holds the bank. Inhibited below 1500 ft RA with gear down, after LOC capture, or after VOR capture at ≤250 kt TAS.
Hook: "6° or less = level."
x.Q1073:
Normal takeoff: F/D 15° until climb rate is sufficient, then MCP speed (V2) + 20 kt. (Engine failure: V2 / current / V2+20.)
Hook: "All engines = V2+20."
x.Q0495:
The FILTER switch on the ACP (item 5) filters the audio you hear from the NAV (VOR/ILS) and ADF receivers:
• V (Voice) – voice only (e.g. ATIS broadcast on a VOR)
• B (Both) – voice AND range (Morse ident) together
• R (Range) – only the station identifier (Morse code), used to identify a navaid.
So to hear voice AND range → BOTH. The VHF TEST button is on the radio tuning panel and has nothing to do with this.
Hook: "V-B-R: Voice, Both, Range (ident)."
x.Q0592:
Degraded mode = the ACP's ALT-NORM switch at ALT (or an ACP failure). The crew member at that station loses the normal selector functions and is left with ONE radio for transmit and receive:
• Captain → VHF-1
• First Officer → VHF-2
• Observer → VHF-1
So the F/O can only transmit/receive on VHF 2. Also lost in degraded mode: hand mic, PA via ACP, and the aural warnings (GPWS, alt alert, windshear) on that side.
Hook: "Each pilot keeps his own side's VHF; the observer sits behind the Captain → VHF-1."
x.Q0753:
The CVR ERASE switch (red, on the forward overhead CVR panel) erases all four channels when pushed for 2 seconds, BUT only works with the airplane ON THE GROUND AND THE PARKING BRAKE SET. Never in flight — this protects the recording for accident investigation.
Hook: "Erase = 2 sec + ground + parking brake."
x.Q0794:
Degraded-mode radio per station (table on 5.20.4): Captain VHF-1, F/O VHF-2, Observer VHF-1.
Other degraded-mode facts from 5.20.3 (often asked): MASK/BOOM switch still works; mic can be keyed with the control wheel PTT (MIC) or the ACP R/T; the HAND mic is NOT usable; altitude alert/GPWS/windshear audio NOT heard on that side; no PA through the ACP.
Hook: "1-2-1: Capt 1, FO 2, Obs 1."
x.Q1041:
Limitations (L.10.6), Non-AFM operational info: on the ground use the VHF radio connected to the TOP-of-fuselage antenna for primary ATC. On the 737 that is VHF-1 (VHF-2 uses the bottom antenna, which can be shielded by the fuselage/terminal buildings on the ground).
Hook: "On the ground, talk through the top: VHF 1."
x.Q1056:
The ACP receiver switches control the volume of the radios you monitor, but the safety aural warnings bypass them: GPWS, altitude alert, TCAS and predictive windshear are heard through speakers AND headsets at PRESET volume and CANNOT be controlled or turned off by the crew. → True.
Hook: "Warnings you can't turn down: GPWS, ALT, TCAS, PWS."
x.Q1097:
VHF TEST (item 9 on the radio tuning panel) simply turns OFF the automatic squelch. You then hear background hiss (that proves the receiver works) and it IMPROVES RECEPTION OF WEAK SIGNALS. It is not a self-test of all VHFs and there is no aural 'test complete'.
Hook: "TEST = squelch off = hear the weak ones."
x.Q1127:
Same rule as the true/false version: predictive windshear (and GPWS, altitude alert, TCAS) aural alerts come through speakers and headsets at a PRESET volume. They cannot be deselected on the ACP and their volume cannot be adjusted. The ACP receiver switches only set the volume of the radios/navaids you monitor.
Hook: "Warnings: fixed volume, no off switch."
x.Q0342:
Batteries are 24 V Ni-Cd (range 22–30 V). When AC is available, the battery charger/TRs hold the DC system at about 28 V. With NO AC power, nothing charges the battery, so the DC voltmeter on BAT shows the battery's own voltage — LESS than 28 V (around 24 V, decreasing as it discharges).
Hook: "No AC = no charger = below 28."
x.Q0343:
The SWITCHED hot battery bus is fed from the battery THROUGH the BATTERY switch (look at the schematic on 6.20.10: the battery switch sits between the battery and the switched hot bat bus). STANDBY POWER to BAT puts the AC standby, DC standby and battery bus on the battery even with the battery switch OFF — but the switched hot battery bus is NOT powered if the battery switch is OFF. (The plain hot battery bus is always powered.)
Hook: "'Switched' = needs the battery switch ON."
x.Q0344:
The two basic 737 electrical principles:
1) NO PARALLELING of AC sources — each transfer bus has ONE source at a time (IDG, APU or ground power).
2) Connecting a new source to a transfer bus AUTOMATICALLY DISCONNECTS the existing one (e.g. selecting GEN 1 ON drops the APU from bus 1).
On the schematic, the BTBs (bus transfer breakers) and GCBs make this happen.
Hook: "One bus, one source — newcomer kicks out the old one."
x.Q0346:
CAB/UTIL OFF (item 13, AC/DC metering panel) is a load-shed switch: it removes power from galley and cabin systems — all 115V AC galley busses, the recirculation fans (L & R), drain mast heaters, potable water heaters, lav/water systems, etc. It does NOT remove emergency lights, overhead panel lights or a pack. (Remember: L recirc fan OFF also affects pack high-flow logic.)
Hook: "CAB/UTIL = cabin comfort stuff: galleys + recirc fans."
x.Q0347:
True. 737 rules: (1) no paralleling of AC sources — only one source on a transfer bus; (2) a newly connected source automatically disconnects the existing one. This is why you can switch from APU to engine generators with no break-before-make action from the crew.
Hook: "One bus, one source — newcomer kicks out the old one."
x.Q0348:
TR UNIT light (amber), AC/DC metering panel:
• On the ground → ANY TR failed.
• In flight → TR1 failed, OR TR2 AND TR3 both failed.
Why? In flight TR1 alone matters for the DC bus 1/standby side; TR2 and TR3 back each other up for bus 2, so a single TR2 or TR3 failure is not annunciated in flight.
Hook: "Flight: 1, or 2+3."
x.Q0349:
APU GEN OFF BUS light (blue) = APU running (at speed) and NOT powering a bus — i.e. it is available to be selected. It goes out when you select an APU GEN switch ON and it takes a transfer bus. Blue = information/available, like GRD POWER AVAILABLE.
Hook: "Blue = ready, not connected."
x.Q0350:
The DC cross bus tie relay normally connects DC bus 1, DC bus 2 and the DC standby bus. It OPENS (isolating DC 1 from DC 2):
1) automatically at glideslope capture on a FD/AP ILS approach (so one failure can't take out both nav receivers/FCCs), and
2) when the BUS TRANSFER switch is positioned OFF.
No manual action needed on approach. It's not tied to AC voltmeter readings and it's TR3 (not the relay) that backs up TR1/TR2.
Hook: "Cross-tie opens at G/S capture or BUS TRANSFER OFF."
x.Q0351:
False. The static inverter makes AC (24 V DC → 115 V AC) so it only feeds the AC STANDBY bus. The DC standby bus, battery bus, hot battery bus and switched hot battery bus get DC DIRECTLY from the batteries — no conversion needed.
Hook: "Inverter only for AC; DC goes direct."
x.Q0352:
ELEC light (amber) means a fault in the DC or standby power system, BUT it operates ONLY ON THE GROUND (inhibited in flight). It is a maintenance-type light — if it comes on before departure, call maintenance. So in flight it will not illuminate.
Hook: "ELEC = DC/standby fault, ground only."
x.Q0353:
GRD POWER AVAILABLE (blue) = ground power is CONNECTED and meets power quality standards. It stays on even after you select GRD PWR ON — it only goes out when the AC ground power cart is DISCONNECTED (or quality is lost). The ground service switch and the pneumatic cart have nothing to do with it.
Hook: "Available light = plug is in."
x.Q0354:
IRS power:
• LEFT IRS: normal = AC STANDBY bus; backup = DC from the SWITCHED HOT BATTERY bus (no time limit).
• RIGHT IRS: normal = AC TRANSFER BUS 2; backup = switched hot battery bus, cut off after 5 MINUTES if AC isn't restored.
On DC the ON DC light comes on and the ground-call horn sounds in the nose wheel well.
Hook: "Left = standby (it survives); Right = transfer 2 (5 min on battery)."
x.Q0355:
Battery chargers are powered from the AC GROUND SERVICE busses (that's why the ground service switch can charge the battery without powering the whole airplane):
• MAIN battery charger ← AC ground service bus 2
• AUX battery charger ← AC ground service bus 1
After charging, the main charger works as a TR, feeding the hot/switched hot battery busses and the battery bus if TR3 fails.
Hook: "Main is 2, Aux is 1 — crossed."
x.Q0357:
Exam answer (Ryanair Q-Bank): FALSE.
Why: the light that tells you an IDG has disconnected because of HIGH OIL TEMPERATURE is the amber DRIVE light (FCOM 6.20.6: DRIVE = IDG low oil pressure caused by … 'IDG automatic disconnect due to high oil temperature'). SOURCE OFF is not an IDG-overheat light – it is about whether the transfer bus still has the source you SELECTED (6.10.7).
Honest note: read literally, the FCOM SOURCE OFF definition includes 'the manually selected source has been disconnected', so in the real aircraft SOURCE OFF can also illuminate after an IDG trips (with GEN OFF BUS), even though the BTBs keep the bus powered (no TRANSFER BUS OFF). For the RYR exam, answer False.
Hook: "IDG overheat → DRIVE light."
x.Q0358:
False. The static inverter converts 24 V DC from the battery into 115 V AC to feed the AC STANDBY bus when normal power is lost. It does not regulate DC to 24 V. Its supply is controlled by the STANDBY POWER switch and BATTERY switch.
Hook: "Inverter: DC in, AC out."
x.Q0359:
TR = Transformer Rectifier: TRANSFORMS 115 V AC down and RECTIFIES it to 28 V DC. Three of them: TR1 (from AC transfer bus 1), TR2 (transfer bus 2), TR3 (transfer bus 2, backup transfer bus 1). Any two TRs can carry the whole DC load.
Hook: "Transformer + Rectifier = AC 115 in, DC 28 out."
x.Q0360:
After GRD PWR ON (engines and APU off):
• GRD POWER AVAILABLE – stays ON (cart still connected)
• SOURCE OFF – OUT (a source is now selected)
• TRANSFER BUS OFF – OUT (busses powered)
• GEN OFF BUS – stay ON (IDGs are not supplying)
• APU GEN OFF BUS – OUT (APU not running, so this light can't be on).
The Electrical Power Up supplementary procedure (SP.6.1) lists exactly these checks.
Hook: "Ground power on: blue available stays, ambers go out, GEN blues stay."
x.Q0362:
Normal power sources for the standby system:
• AC standby bus ← AC transfer bus 1
• DC standby bus ← TR1, TR2 and TR3
• BATTERY BUS ← TR3 (main battery charger backs up if TR3 fails)
• Hot battery bus and switched hot battery bus ← battery/battery charger.
On loss of normal power they all go to the battery.
Hook: "Battery bus is TR3's job."
x.Q0363:
The IRSs are the classic load on the SWITCHED hot battery bus — it is their DC backup (L IRS indefinitely, R IRS 5 min). The bus is live whenever the battery switch is ON. Engine/APU fire extinguishing is on the HOT battery bus (always live, so you can fire a bottle with the battery switch OFF). Note: the FCOM doesn't literally say IRS is the 'only' load — but it's the expected answer.
Hook: "Switched hot = IRS backup; Hot = fire bottles."
x.Q0364:
DC busses run at 28 V DC (TR output). AC is 115 V (400 Hz). Batteries are 24 V nominal (22–30 V).
Hook: "AC 115, DC 28, battery 24."
x.Q0366:
The GRD POWER AVAILABLE light does need ground power that meets airplane power QUALITY standards — but the statement says 200 Hz. Aircraft AC is 115 V, 400 Hz, 3-phase. Because of the wrong frequency → FALSE. Read the numbers in these true/false questions carefully.
Hook: "737 AC: 115 V / 400 Hz."
x.Q0367:
On battery only (BAT ON, STANDBY POWER AUTO) the standby busses feed only the CAPTAIN's instruments: outboard display (PFD) and inboard display (compact engine / ND depending on effectivity), plus standby instruments (ISFD, RMI). They keep working until the battery is depleted (min 60 min with both batteries). The First Officer's displays are dark (see 6.20.18 – all shaded).
Hook: "Battery power = Captain's flying, F/O's watching."
x.Q0368:
STANDBY POWER switch positions:
• AUTO (guarded) – normal; automatic switch to battery if AC transfer bus 1 or DC bus 1 is lost.
• OFF (centre) – AC standby bus, static inverter and DC standby bus are NOT powered → amber STANDBY PWR OFF light ON.
• BAT – forces the standby busses onto the battery.
So OFF = no automatic switching and the light illuminates. The inverter makes AC, never 28 V DC.
Hook: "OFF switch → OFF light."
x.Q0369:
Main battery charger ← AC GROUND SERVICE bus 2; aux battery charger ← AC ground service bus 1. Putting the chargers on the ground service busses lets the ground crew charge the batteries using only the ground service switch (forward attendant panel), without powering the whole airplane.
Hook: "Main is 2, Aux is 1."
x.Q0371:
The STANDBY power system = AC standby bus, static inverter, DC standby bus, battery bus, hot battery bus, switched hot battery bus, main and aux batteries. TR1 is part of the NORMAL DC system, energized from AC transfer bus 1 — it is a normal source FOR the standby system, not powered by it.
Hook: "TRs feed the standby system; the inverter belongs to it."
x.Q0372:
The CAB/UTIL switch powers cabin/galley/utility loads: all galley busses, the L & R recirculation fans, door area heaters, drain mast heaters, lav water heaters, etc. With it OFF, the recirc fans don't run. Lighting, temperature control and packs are NOT on CAB/UTIL.
Hook: "CAB/UTIL = galleys + recirc fans + cabin utilities."
x.Q0373:
The FCOM doesn't state the 'why', but the system shows it: AC (IDGs, 115 V 400 Hz 3-phase) generates and distributes the large loads efficiently; DC (28 V via TRs) can be STORED in batteries, which give backup power to the standby system when AC is lost. That's answer B.
Hook: "AC moves big power; DC can be bottled in a battery."
x.Q0374:
BAT switch OFF:
• With NORMAL power on the busses → removes power from the BATTERY BUS and SWITCHED HOT BATTERY BUS only (standby busses stay on AC/TRs).
• When the battery is the ONLY source → also removes DC standby bus, static inverter and AC standby bus.
The HOT battery bus is never switched.
Hook: "BAT OFF kills battery bus + switched hot; standby too only if battery is all you've got."
x.Q0375:
BUS TRANSFER AUTO (guarded): the BTBs (bus transfer breakers, BTB1/BTB2 on the schematic) operate automatically to keep both AC transfer busses powered from ANY operating generator or external power, and the DC cross tie relay automatically gives normal or isolated operation. The 'isolate' answers describe the OFF position.
Hook: "AUTO = BTBs keep both busses alive."
x.Q0376:
With STANDBY POWER in AUTO, losing all generators (IDGs and APU) automatically puts the standby loads on the batteries BOTH IN THE AIR AND ON THE GROUND: AC standby via the static inverter, DC standby and battery bus directly from the battery.
Hook: "AUTO works anywhere — air or ground."
x.Q0377:
Automatic generator on-line feature: if you take off with the APU powering both transfer busses (e.g. packs-off/APU takeoff), and the APU is then shut down or fails, the engine generators AUTOMATICALLY connect to their transfer busses. It happens only ONCE per flight and only in this situation. No altitude trigger, nothing disconnects at lift-off.
Hook: "APU takeoff → APU off → gens jump on (once)."
x.Q0378:
Main + aux battery (both 24 V Ni-Cd), fully charged, give standby power for a MINIMUM OF 60 MINUTES after loss of all generators. The aux battery only works in parallel with the main when the battery is powering the standby system.
Hook: "Two batteries = one hour."
x.Q0380:
APU GEN OFF BUS (blue) = APU RUNNING but NOT powering the transfer busses. Once you move an APU GEN switch ON and the APU takes a bus, the light goes out. If the APU isn't running, the light is off.
Hook: "Blue = ready, not connected."
x.Q0381:
When a generator drops off line, its transfer bus is momentarily unpowered until the BTBs transfer it to the other source. AFS failures (4.20.3): power interruption or loss may disengage the AFDS and/or A/T → the AUTOPILOT MAY DISCONNECT. Re-engage after power is restored. Also: dual-channel A/P needs two generators powering the busses. (SOURCE OFF would illuminate, not extinguish.)
Hook: "Power blink → A/P drops."
x.Q0382:
Single-generator load shedding order: galleys + main bus on transfer bus 2 first → then galleys + main bus on transfer bus 1 → then IFE busses. When two generators are back, restoration is automatic; if it doesn't happen, RECYCLE THE CAB/UTIL switch (OFF, then ON).
Hook: "Shed 2, then 1, then IFE — fix with CAB/UTIL off-on."
x.Q0383:
APU as only source:
• IN FLIGHT → ALL galley busses and main busses are automatically shed (then both IFE busses if still overloaded).
• ON THE GROUND → the APU tries to carry the full load; only if overload is sensed does it shed galleys and main busses.
So D. Answer C is wrong because on the ground shedding isn't automatic by default.
Hook: "APU in the air = no galleys."
x.Q0384:
STANDBY PWR OFF (amber) = one or more of AC standby, DC standby or battery bus UNPOWERED. In BAT the battery powers all three (AC standby through the inverter, DC standby and battery bus directly) → light OUT = battery is supplying the standby system and standby power is available.
Hook: "Light out = standby alive."
x.Q0385:
Join two facts:
1) TR UNIT light in flight = TR1 failed (or TR2 + TR3).
2) At glideslope capture (FD/AP ILS) the cross bus tie relay OPENS, splitting DC bus 1 from DC bus 2.
If TR1 has failed, DC bus 1 was being fed only through the cross tie — when it opens at G/S capture, DC bus 1 loses power during the approach. Hence: don't use APP mode with TR UNIT light in flight (follow the NNC).
Hook: "TR1 dead + G/S capture = DC 1 dead."
x.Q0386:
BUS TRANSFER OFF = full isolation of side 1 from side 2:
• BTBs OPEN → AC transfer bus 1 isolated from transfer bus 2
• DC cross bus tie relay OPENS → DC bus 1 isolated from DC bus 2
(and TR3 can't take its backup feed from transfer bus 1). Everything OPENS.
Hook: "OFF = everything opens, two separate airplanes."
x.Q0387:
DRIVE light (amber) = IDG LOW OIL PRESSURE, caused by:
• IDG failure
• engine shutdown
• IDG automatic disconnect due to HIGH OIL TEMPERATURE
• IDG disconnected with the DISCONNECT switch.
Trap: answer B says high oil PRESSURE — wrong word. Disconnect can't be reset in the air (maintenance on the ground only).
Hook: "DRIVE = low pressure; auto-disconnect = high temperature."
x.Q0388:
GRD POWER AVAILABLE (blue) = ground power CONNECTED and MEETS airplane power QUALITY standards. It doesn't mean any bus is powered — you still have to select GRD PWR ON.
Hook: "Available = plugged in + good quality, not yet on."
x.Q0389:
In flight with the APU as the only source: ALL galley busses (A, B, C and D) and the main busses are automatically shed; IFE busses too if still overloaded.
Hook: "APU in the air = no galleys at all."
x.Q0390:
Solve by elimination with the FCOM:
• A wrong – on standby power the CAPTAIN's pitot is still heated (3.20.5).
• B wrong – VHF-1 is on standby power (basic equipment list).
• D wrong – it's the RIGHT IRS that loses its DC backup after 5 min; the left keeps going.
→ C: the flap position indicator (AC powered) freezes at its last position. The FCOM doesn't describe this directly, but it's the only answer left.
Hook: "All AC lost: Capt pitot still hot, VHF-1 alive, L IRS alive."
x.Q0391:
On standby (battery) power only the Captain's pitot probe is heated → SOME ice protection is left, the rest (window heat, F/O pitot, alpha vanes, TAT, wing/engine anti-ice valves needing AC/DC loads) is lost. The weather radar isn't on the standby busses (not in the basic equipment pages 6.20.17/18) → unavailable.
Hook: "Battery only: Capt pitot heat yes, radar no."
x.Q0392:
GEN OFF BUS (blue) = that IDG isn't supplying its transfer bus. The bus transfers to the other generator via the BTBs, causing a momentary power interruption — and AFS failures (4.20.3) say a power interruption may disengage the AFDS/A/T. So an engaged A/P on that side MAY DISCONNECT; re-engage once power is back.
Hook: "Gen drops → blink → A/P may drop."
x.Q0393:
The RYR FCOM gives no explicit 'normal DC indication', but its battery range 22–30 V is exactly 26 ± 4 V — the classic Boeing figure. (TR output is nominally 28 V, but the bank's 28 ± 4 option is not the accepted answer.)
Hook: "22–30 → 26 ± 4."
x.Q0394:
TR UNIT light: ON THE GROUND – ANY TR failed (so maintenance can catch it before flight). In flight – TR1, or TR2 and TR3.
Hook: "Ground: any. Flight: 1, or 2+3."
x.Q0395:
ELEC light (amber, ground only) = a fault exists in the DC power system or STANDBY power system. TR failures have their own TR UNIT light; battery discharge has BAT DISCHARGE.
Hook: "ELEC = DC/standby fault, ground only."
x.Q0396:
AC STANDBY BUS: normal = AC TRANSFER BUS 1. Only after loss of ALL AC power (or transfer bus 1 / DC bus 1 lost, AUTO) does it go to the battery via the static inverter. Losing one IDG isn't enough — the BTBs keep transfer bus 1 powered from the other generator.
Hook: "Standby follows side 1."
x.Q0398:
False. An IDG that disconnects for high oil temperature gives the amber DRIVE light (low oil pressure in the IDG), the blue GEN OFF BUS light, AND SOURCE OFF (selected source gone). So SOURCE OFF is NOT the only indication.
Hook: "IDG overheat = DRIVE + GEN OFF BUS + SOURCE OFF."
x.Q0399:
In flight TR UNIT illuminates for TR1 failure (alone), or for BOTH TR2 and TR3. A single TR2 or TR3 failure → no light in flight.
Hook: "Flight: 1, or 2+3."
x.Q0400:
Static inverter = DC → AC: 24 V DC from the battery → 115 V AC for the AC standby bus when normal power is lost. (A transformer changes AC voltage; a TR changes AC to DC.)
Hook: "Inverter inverts DC into AC."
x.Q0401:
Low oil pressure in an IDG is EXACTLY what the amber DRIVE light senses → No 2 DRIVE light illuminates. (Other effects — GEN OFF BUS, BTBs transferring — only follow if the generator actually drops off; standby power does not take over for a single IDG.)
Hook: "IDG low oil pressure = DRIVE light."
x.Q0402:
With no AC, the battery powers: battery bus, DC standby bus, HOT battery bus and SWITCHED HOT battery bus. The hot battery bus is wired straight to the battery; the switched one goes through the BATTERY switch (on whenever it's ON). Among the options only the switched hot battery bus fits ('standby bus' is too vague — the AC standby needs the inverter).
Hook: "Hot = always; Switched hot = battery switch ON."
x.Q0403:
GRD PWR ON (or either APU GEN switch ON) powers BOTH AC transfer busses. Whichever source is selected LAST powers both. You cannot have ground power on one bus and APU on the other (but you CAN have an engine gen on one bus and GPU/APU on the other).
Hook: "GPU or APU = both busses; last one selected wins."
x.Q0404:
On standby power: ONLY the CAPTAIN's pitot probe is heated, and the CAPT PITOT light will NOT illuminate if it fails. The standby (ISFD) pitot is NOT heated. F/O pitot, alpha vanes and TAT probe are not heated either.
Hook: "Standby power: Capt pitot hot, light dead, standby pitot cold."
x.Q0405:
ELEC light (amber, on the AC/DC metering panel) = fault in the DC power system or STANDBY power system. It works ONLY ON THE GROUND. AC faults have their own lights (TRANSFER BUS OFF, SOURCE OFF, DRIVE…).
Hook: "ELEC = DC/standby fault, ground only."
x.Q0406:
In flight TR UNIT = TR1 failed (alone), or TR2 AND TR3 failed. TR1+TR2 is not the definition; 'any TR' is the ground logic.
Hook: "Flight: 1, or 2+3."
x.Q0408:
Aux battery charger ← AC GROUND SERVICE bus 1; main battery charger ← AC ground service bus 2.
Hook: "Main is 2, Aux is 1 — crossed."
x.Q0410:
DRIVE light = IDG LOW OIL PRESSURE (from IDG failure, engine shutdown, high-temp auto disconnect, or manual disconnect). Not overload, not low temperature, not a breaker.
Hook: "DRIVE = low pressure."
x.Q0411:
Automatic generator on-line: after a takeoff on APU power, if the APU is shut down or fails, the engine gens connect automatically — once per flight. No altitude trigger.
Hook: "APU takeoff → APU off → gens jump on (once)."
x.Q0412:
Follow the schematic: each IDG → GCB → its transfer bus; each transfer bus ↔ BTB ↔ tie bus. When IDG fails in AUTO: its GCB opens, then BOTH BTBs close, so the remaining IDG feeds its own bus directly and the other bus through the tie bus. Result: one IDG powers both transfer busses automatically; no crew action, and the standby system is not involved.
Hook: "One IDG lost → both BTBs close → one IDG feeds both."
x.Q0458:
Battery voltage range is 22–30 V; during the primary charge cycle the charger pushes the battery to the top of that range — up to about 30 V. Afterward the main charger reverts to constant-voltage TR mode.
Hook: "Battery tops out at 30."
x.Q0569:
Same automatic generator on-line feature: take off with the APU on both busses, then APU shutdown/failure → engine generators connect automatically (once per flight). Nothing disconnects at lift-off and there is no 1500 ft trigger.
Hook: "APU takeoff → APU off → gens jump on (once)."
x.Q1047:
WHY the cross bus tie relay opens at glideslope capture: to isolate DC bus 1 from DC bus 2 so that a single failure can't affect BOTH navigation receivers and BOTH flight control computers during the approach (redundancy for autoland/dual channel).
Hook: "G/S capture → split DC → one failure can't kill both sides."
x.Q1094:
The DRIVE light senses one thing: LOW OIL PRESSURE in the IDG. IDG failure, engine shutdown and high-temp auto-disconnect are the reasons the pressure drops — indirect causes. 'Directly caused by' → low oil pressure.
Hook: "The light reads pressure; the rest are reasons."
x.Q0414:
APU fuel feed: with AC fuel pumps running → from the LEFT side of the fuel manifold (so any running pump that feeds the left side, incl. center tank pumps / crossfeed). With no AC pumps → suction fed from MAIN TANK No 1. That's why, for an APU start without AC, a main tank 1 pump isn't needed.
Hook: "APU drinks from the left."
x.Q0415:
EEC switch lights:
• ON only → normal mode.
• ON + ALTN → EEC AUTOMATICALLY switched to SOFT alternate (lost required signals, uses last valid conditions, no thrust change).
• ALTN only (ON blanked) → ALTN selected MANUALLY (hard alternate).
Hook: "Both lights = the EEC did it itself."
x.Q0416:
APU start cycle can take up to 120 s. If the start fails OR the APU GEN OFF BUS light hasn't illuminated by the end of the start cycle → system failure → amber APU FAULT light. (MAINT = maintenance item; OVERSPEED = overspeed shutdown / failed overspeed self-test.)
Hook: "No blue light in time → FAULT."
x.Q0417:
Start lever IDLE: (1) energizes ignition via the EEC, (2) opens the SPAR fuel shutoff valve (wing leading edge, outboard of pylon), (3) opens the ENGINE-mounted fuel shutoff valve via the EEC. CUTOFF closes both valves and de-energizes ignition. The fire switch also closes both.
Hook: "Lever up = two valves open + sparks."
x.Q0418:
True. Automatic reversion to soft alternate illuminates the amber ALTN in the EEC switch. 'EEC ALTN MODE' is one of the items on the ENG system annunciator (15.20.4), so MASTER CAUTION + ENG come on.
Hook: "Amber ALTN → MASTER CAUTION + ENG."
x.Q0419:
The red EGT START LIMIT line on the EGT dial is displayed until the engine reaches STABILIZED IDLE (~59% N2), for ground starts and some in-flight starts. Other start numbers: fuel at 25% N2 (max motoring), starter cutout ~56% N2.
Hook: "25 fuel → 56 cutout → 59 idle (redline gone)."
x.Q0420:
ENGINE START switch:
• GRD – starter + ignition on selected igniter(s)
• OFF – auto-relight logic (both igniters on rapid N2 decay etc.)
• CONT – SELECTED igniter(s) continuously (both in flight if N2 below idle)
• FLT – BOTH igniters regardless of the IGN select switch (for in-flight start, turbulence, heavy rain).
Hook: "FLT = full ignition, both plugs."
x.Q0421:
False. Two separate air paths: APU ENGINE (combustion) air enters through the automatic AIR INLET DOOR on the right side of the fuselage; COOLING air enters through a separate cooling air inlet ABOVE THE EXHAUST outlet, circulates the compartment and oil cooler, and leaves via the exhaust.
Hook: "Engine air on the side door, cooling air above the exhaust."
x.Q0422:
False. Oil quantity is a secondary engine indication on the DU. A physical check is done at the engine oil tank on the engine (sight glass / dipstick on the engine), not in the main gear wheel well. (The FCOM doesn't describe the physical check; the bank answer is False.)
Hook: "Oil is on the engine, not in the wheel well."
x.Q0423:
Start sequence: GRD → start valve opens → N2 rotates → at 25% N2 or MAX MOTORING (whichever applies) → start lever to IDLE (fuel + ignition) → ~56% N2 starter cutout (switch back to OFF) → ~59% stabilized idle. All the start speeds are N2, not N1.
Hook: "25 fuel, 56 cutout — always N2."
x.Q0424:
Reverser deploy logic: EITHER radio altimeter < 10 ft OR air/ground sensor in ground mode, AND (mechanically) forward thrust levers at idle. So yes, it can deploy just before touchdown with one RA below 10 ft.
Hook: "Either RA under 10 or ground mode."
x.Q0425:
False. During in-flight starts the EGT start limit redline CAN be shown, depending on EEC start logic. If only the EGT redline is shown → that is the in-flight start limit; if both are shown → the start-limit redline is the limit.
Hook: "In-flight start: redline may appear — EEC decides."
x.Q0426:
Abnormal start protection (hot start, stall, EGT exceedance, wet start → auto cutoff) works on GROUND STARTS ONLY. In flight there is NO automatic protection — the crew monitors and moves the lever to CUTOFF if needed.
Hook: "EEC babysits ground starts only."
x.Q0427:
Soft alternate → thrust lever to IDLE → HARD alternate. Lights unchanged: ALTN still illuminated AND ON still visible. Only a MANUAL ALTN selection blanks the ON. In hard alternate there's no EEC limiting — full forward lever may overboost.
Hook: "Idle turns soft into hard; lights stay the same."
x.Q0428:
False. Order in flight with the APU alone: FIRST all galley busses AND main busses; THEN, if still over the limit, the IFE busses. The statement wrongly pairs galleys with IFE.
Hook: "Galleys + mains first, IFE last."
x.Q0429:
The APU's electronic control unit runs on battery power. Battery switch OFF → ECU loses power → APU shuts down automatically, ON THE GROUND OR IN THE AIR. APU operation requires: APU fire switch IN, APU ground control handle IN, battery switch ON.
Hook: "No battery, no APU — anywhere."
x.Q0430:
The APU panel has 4 lights. The three AMBER ones mean the ECU made a PROTECTIVE SHUTDOWN: FAULT, OVERSPEED, LOW OIL PRESSURE. The 4th, the BLUE MAINT light, only says a maintenance problem exists — the APU keeps running.
Hook: "FOL shut down (Fault, Overspeed, Low oil) — MAINT doesn't."
x.Q0431:
Wet start = no EGT rise after the start lever goes to IDLE (fuel in, no light-off). On a GROUND start the EEC turns off ignition and fuel 15 SECONDS after the START LEVER (not the thrust lever) is moved to IDLE. In flight: no protection.
Hook: "Wet start: 15 seconds, then EEC cuts it."
x.Q0432:
False — the statement says 'bleed air only'. The APU starts and operates up to the airplane MAXIMUM CERTIFIED ALTITUDE and supplies BOTH bleed air and AC electrical power (its generator). (Bleed is limited at higher altitudes — check the APU limitations — but it is never 'bleed only'.)
Hook: "APU = air + electrics, all the way up."
x.Q0433:
False. The APU air inlet door is on the RIGHT side of the fuselage (tail area), not the left.
Hook: "APU breathes from the right."
x.Q0434:
APU switch OFF → immediately trips the APU gen, closes the APU bleed valve, GEN OFF BUS light out → actual shutdown after a 60-SECOND cooling delay. If the fuel valve fails to close, FAULT after ~30 s. Immediate shutdown = pull the APU fire switch. Remember the other APU times: 120 s max start cycle, 2 min warm-up before bleed use.
Hook: "APU off = 60 s cool-down."
x.Q0435:
At STARTER CUTOUT (~56% N2) the holding solenoid releases: start switch snaps back to OFF, engine bleed valve returns to selected position, START VALVE closes → START VALVE OPEN alert goes out.
Hook: "56 = starter quits."
x.Q0436:
Normal sequence: when you command STOW, the REVERSER light (aft overhead) comes on and goes out ~10 s later when the isolation valve closes. On for more than ~12 s → malfunction → MASTER CAUTION + ENG.
Hook: "Stow → 10 s light is normal; 12 s+ is a fault."
x.Q0437:
A/T LIM (white, upper DU, replaces the thrust mode) = the FMC is NOT providing N1 limit values to the A/T; the A/T uses a degraded N1 limit from the related EEC.
Hook: "A/T LIM = FMC stopped giving limits."
x.Q0438:
FCOM 4.10.4: with the N1 SET outer knob in AUTO the A/T won't exceed the displayed N1 limit, 'however, A/T can exceed an N1 value manually set with the N1 SET outer knob in the manual BOTH, 1, or 2 position. Setting the thrust reference manually is intended to provide guidance when manually controlling thrust.' → BOTH only moves the reference N1 bugs/readouts; it has NO effect on A/T operation (no disengage, no new max-thrust limit for the A/T).
Hook: "N1 SET BOTH moves bugs, not the A/T."
x.Q0439:
Impending scavenge oil filter bypass → amber OIL FILTER BYPASS alert on the UPPER DU (blinks with boxes for 10 s, then steady). It does NOT trigger MASTER CAUTION. The FILTER BYPASS light on the FUEL panel is the FUEL filter.
Hook: "Oil filter → upper DU; fuel filter → fuel panel."
x.Q0440:
REV above the N1 dial: AMBER = sleeves have moved from stowed (in transit); GREEN = fully DEPLOYED. The REVERSER light on the aft overhead is about the stow/fault logic, not deployment.
Hook: "Amber moving, green there."
x.Q0441:
When GRD opens the start valve, an amber START VALVE OPEN alert appears on the UPPER DU (steady = commanded; blinking = uncommanded opening). There's no blue START VALVE light on the NG.
Hook: "Start valve open → upper DU."
x.Q0442:
Oil circuit: tank → oil pump → bearings/gearboxes → SCAVENGE pumps → SCAVENGE FILTER → main engine oil cooler (fuel-cooled) → back to the tank. So the filter is in the RETURN line before reaching the tank. The pressure/temp sensors are downstream of the supply pump.
Hook: "Filter on the way home."
x.Q0443:
Each engine has two igniters: LEFT igniter ← associated AC TRANSFER bus; RIGHT igniter ← AC STANDBY bus. So with all generators lost, only the RIGHT igniters work (battery/inverter) — that's why IGN R matters for in-flight relights on standby power.
Hook: "Right igniter = Reliable (standby)."
x.Q0444:
N1, N2, OIL QUANTITY and VIBRATION come DIRECTLY from engine sensors (shown even when the EEC is unpowered). Everything else (EGT, fuel flow, oil pressure, oil temp) is sensed via the EEC. Of the options, oil quantity is the one NOT via the EEC.
Hook: "Without EEC: N1, N2, Qty, Vib."
x.Q0447:
False. The oil pressure AMBER band varies with N2 above 65% N2 and is NOT DISPLAYED BELOW 65% N2. At stabilized idle (~59% N2) there is no amber band to be in — you'd see LOW OIL PRESSURE alert and the red line.
Hook: "Amber oil band only above 65% N2."
x.Q0449:
Auto-relight: when the EEC detects a flameout — uncommanded rapid DECREASE IN N2, or N2 BELOW IDLE — it fires BOTH igniters (even with start switch OFF). It's always N2 for the start/relight logic.
Hook: "N2 falls → both plugs fire."
x.Q0450:
EEC idles: ground min idle, flight min idle, APPROACH idle. Approach idle in flight if ANY of:
• engine (cowl) anti-ice ON either engine
• below 19,000 ft MSL AND main gear down & locked
• below 19,000 ft MSL AND flaps ≥ 15.
Why: higher N1/N2 → faster spool-up for a go-around. Kept until after touchdown. Answer C (flaps landing config or anti-ice ON) is the matching option.
Hook: "Approach idle: anti-ice, or below FL190 with gear or flaps 15."
x.Q0451:
APU cooling air enters through a COOLING AIR INLET ABOVE THE APU EXHAUST outlet, circulates the compartment, cools the oil cooler and leaves through the exhaust. The air inlet door is for the APU's engine air.
Hook: "Cooling air sits right above the exhaust."
x.Q0452:
Normal start (AC available): positioning the ENGINE START switch to GRD powers the EEC and all engine parameters appear. Only on a BATTERY start (no AC) does the EEC wait until its own alternator spins it up at 15% N2.
Hook: "GRD = EEC wakes up."
x.Q0453:
Soft alternate (ON + ALTN lights) stays until HARD alternate is entered by: (1) retarding that THRUST LEVER TO IDLE, or (2) manually pushing the EEC switch to ALTN (aft overhead).
Hook: "Idle or push → hard."
x.Q0454:
Yes — a BATTERY START is possible: the start switch uses BATTERY power to open the start valve; you only need an AIR source (ground cart, APU bleed, other engine). The EEC powers up from its own alternator at 15% N2. Battery switch must be ON (start switch circuit needs it).
Hook: "No AC? Air + battery is enough."
x.Q0456:
Battery start (no AC): only N1, N2 and oil quantity are shown at first. The EEC is energized by its own alternator once N2 exceeds 15%, then all parameters appear.
Hook: "Battery start: EEC alive at 15."
x.Q0457:
EGT start-limit exceedance → EEC turns off ignition and fuel (box and dial red) — but only during GROUND STARTS. Abnormal start protection does not function in flight.
Hook: "EEC babysits ground starts only."
x.Q0459:
Engine fuel path: tank pumps → spar valve → 1st stage pump → TWO fuel/oil heat exchangers (IDG oil cooler AND main engine oil cooler) heat the fuel → fuel filter → 2nd stage pump → HMU (metered by EEC). The fuel cools the oil and the oil warms the fuel (prevents ice in the filter).
Hook: "Fuel cools both oils — IDG and engine."
x.Q0460:
CFM56-7: N1 rotor = fan + LP compressor + LP turbine; N2 rotor = HP compressor + HP turbine (mechanically independent). The N2 rotor DRIVES THE GEARBOXES (IDG, hydraulic pump, fuel & oil pumps) and the air starter turns the N2 rotor. That's why all start/relight figures are N2.
Hook: "N2 drives the accessories."
x.Q0461:
Loss of EITHER DEU → loss of signal to BOTH EECs → both ALTN lights illuminate and BOTH EECs go to (soft) alternate. Reason: so the two engines never run on a single source of data (asymmetric control).
Hook: "One DEU lost → both EECs ALTN."
x.Q0462:
Fuel is heated by TWO heat exchangers: the IDG oil cooler and the main engine oil cooler, both after the 1st-stage fuel pump and before the fuel filter.
Hook: "Fuel cools both oils — IDG and engine."
x.Q0463:
Hard alternate is entered FROM SOFT alternate by retarding the thrust lever to idle, or by pushing the EEC switch (manual ALTN). From normal mode, retarding to idle does nothing. In hard alternate, thrust ≥ normal for the same lever position and there's no EEC limiting → avoid full forward except terrain emergencies.
Hook: "Soft → idle or push → hard."
x.Q0464:
Engine oil is cooled by the MAIN ENGINE OIL COOLER using ENGINE FUEL (fuel/oil heat exchanger) on the way back to the tank. No air cooler.
Hook: "Fuel cools the oil."
x.Q0466:
Each CFM56-7 has TWO igniter plugs (left and right). The IGNITION SELECT switch (IGN L / BOTH / IGN R) chooses which igniter(s) are used on BOTH engines. Left ← AC transfer bus; right ← AC standby bus.
Hook: "Two plugs per engine; the selector picks for both engines."
x.Q0467:
In-flight start methods: WINDMILL (enough airspeed) or CROSSBLEED (air from the other engine). When airspeed is too low for a windmill start, a magenta X-BLD (XB on the compact display) appears ABOVE THE N2 dial — makes sense: the starter drives N2.
Hook: "X-BLD sits on N2 — the starter's rotor."
x.Q0473:
Auto-restow: if a sleeve isn't fully stowed or moves uncommanded toward deploy, the circuit OPENS the isolation valve (hydraulic pressure available) and commands the CONTROL VALVE to STOW. Once activated, the isolation valve STAYS OPEN and the control valve is HELD in stow until reverse is commanded again or maintenance acts. The REVERSER light comes on.
Hook: "Restow: keep the pressure on (isolation open), push to stow."
x.Q0477:
Mechanical interlocks: reverse thrust lever can be raised only when the related FORWARD lever is at IDLE; and the forward lever can't be advanced while the reverse lever is deployed. The reverse lever is also blocked at reverse idle until the reverser is >60% deployed.
Hook: "Forward at idle before you pull reverse."
x.Q0478:
The ACCESSORY GEARBOX is driven by the N2 (HP) rotor. It drives the IDG, engine hydraulic pump, fuel pumps and oil pump; the air starter is attached to it.
Hook: "N2 drives the accessories."
x.Q0480:
The APU generator can power BOTH AC transfer busses ON THE GROUND OR IN FLIGHT. As the only source it covers all ground conditions and most flight conditions (in flight galleys/main busses are shed).
Hook: "APU feeds both busses — anywhere."
x.Q0481:
APU altitude limits (Limitations, EASA):
• bleed + electrical together: max 10,000 ft
• bleed only (pneumatic): max 17,000 ft
• electrical only: max 41,000 ft.
Hook: "10 both, 17 air, 41 electric."
x.Q0482:
APU bleed AND electrical simultaneously: max 10,000 ft. (Bleed only 17,000 ft, electrical only 41,000 ft.)
Hook: "10 both, 17 air, 41 electric."
x.Q0483:
The APU starts and operates up to the airplane MAXIMUM CERTIFIED ALTITUDE (41,000 ft) and can supply electrical load alone up to 41,000 ft.
Hook: "10 both, 17 air, 41 electric."
x.Q0484:
True. Abnormal start protection (hot, stall, EGT exceedance, wet) is GROUND STARTS ONLY; there is none in flight.
Hook: "EEC babysits ground starts only."
x.Q0485:
APU MAINT light (BLUE) = an APU maintenance problem exists, but the APU MAY BE OPERATED. Disarmed with the APU switch OFF. The amber FAULT / OVERSPEED / LOW OIL PRESSURE lights are the ones linked to automatic shutdown.
Hook: "Blue MAINT = tell engineers, keep running."
x.Q0488:
Approach idle in flight if: engine anti-ice ON (either), OR below 19,000 ft with gear down, OR below 19,000 ft with flaps ≥ 15. Purpose: faster spool-up for a go-around. Start switch positions and thrust lever angle don't matter.
Hook: "Approach idle: anti-ice, or below FL190 with gear or flaps 15."
x.Q0489:
The EEC protects against N1 AND N2 redline OVERSPEED in BOTH normal and alternate modes. It does NOT protect the EGT redline — the crew must watch EGT. (In hard alternate there's no thrust LIMITING, but overspeed protection remains.)
Hook: "EEC guards N1/N2 always; EGT is your job."
x.Q0494:
Reverser can deploy when EITHER RA < 10 ft OR the air/ground sensor is in GROUND mode (with forward levers at idle). Not at 30 ft, not freely in flight. Intentional reverse in flight is prohibited (Limitations).
Hook: "Either RA under 10 or ground mode."
x.Q0496:
Abnormal start protection = GROUND ONLY, covering: impending HOT start, engine STALL, EGT start-limit EXCEEDANCE, and WET start. None in flight.
Hook: "Ground only: Hot, Stall, EGT, Wet."
x.Q0497:
Starter disengaged (cutout ~56% N2): the ENGINE START switch springs back to OFF automatically and the START VALVE OPEN alert extinguishes (start valve closed). The engine bleed valve returns to its selected position.
Hook: "Switch pops to OFF + valve alert out = starter off."
x.Q0498:
A red box around a digital readout (N1, N2, EGT) after shutdown on the ground = an EXCEEDANCE occurred during the flight. It reminds the crew to write it up in the tech log.
Hook: "Red box after shutdown = you exceeded something in flight."
x.Q0500:
Start lever to IDLE at 25% N2 or MAX MOTORING (if 25% can't be reached, max motoring = N2 stops increasing by more than 1% in ~5 s, minimum 20% N2 per the procedures). Always N2, never N1.
Hook: "25 fuel, 56 cutout — always N2."
x.Q0501:
EEC modes: NORMAL, SOFT ALTERNATE (automatic, last valid conditions, no thrust jump) and HARD ALTERNATE (alternate thrust schedule; entered by idle or manual ALTN). 'ON' is just the switch indication, not a mode.
Hook: "Normal → Soft → Hard."
x.Q0502:
NO start protection in flight. The crew monitors EGT/N2 and cuts off manually. (N1/N2 overspeed protection is a normal EEC function, not 'start protection'.)
Hook: "In flight you are the protection."
x.Q0505:
OIL FILTER BYPASS alert comes on BEFORE the oil actually bypasses — it warns the scavenge filter is becoming CLOGGED (impending bypass). That's 'partially blocked' (answer C), not 'already bypassing'.
Hook: "Alert first, bypass later."
x.Q0506:
Reverse sequence: lift to reverse idle (detent 1) → sleeves move (REV AMBER) → interlock holds the lever until the sleeves approach FULL DEPLOY (>60%) → REV GREEN → lever can go to detent 2 (normal reverse) or beyond (max). Stowing: past detent 1 downwards commands stow.
Hook: "Wait for green, then pull."
x.Q0507:
With EEC unpowered: N1, N2, OIL QUANTITY and VIBRATION come directly from engine sensors. Oil temp, oil pressure, fuel flow, EGT need the EEC.
Hook: "Without EEC: N1, N2, Qty, Vib."
x.Q0508:
Oil return path: scavenge pumps → scavenge filter → MAIN ENGINE OIL COOLER (cooled by fuel) → oil tank. So the cooler is in the RETURN line before the tank (look at the schematic 7.20.8).
Hook: "Filter and cooler both on the way home."
x.Q0509:
LEFT igniter ← its ASSOCIATED AC transfer bus → engine 1 = AC TRANSFER BUS 1 (engine 2 = transfer bus 2). RIGHT igniter ← AC standby bus.
Hook: "Left = own side transfer bus; Right = standby."
x.Q0511:
The bleed-air starter drives the HP ROTOR (N2) through the accessory gearbox. The fan (N1) just follows aerodynamically.
Hook: "Starter spins N2."
x.Q0514:
The fuel passes the two fuel/oil heat exchangers BEFORE the fuel filter. Purpose (not spelled out in FCOM but obvious from the order): warm fuel so ICE CRYSTALS (from water in cold fuel) don't block the filter.
Hook: "Warm it before you filter it — no ice in the filter."
x.Q0515:
After APU switch OFF: 60 s cooling, then shutdown; as APU speed decreases the FUEL VALVE and AIR INLET DOOR close. The door actuator needs DC (battery) power — switch the battery off too early and the door stays open. Keep the battery ON until the inlet door has closed (~2 min after APU OFF in SOPs).
Hook: "Wait for the door before the battery."
x.Q0516:
