Start switch OFF still gives auto-ignition (both igniters, start lever IDLE) when: rapid uncommanded N2 decrease, N2 between 57% and 50%, or in flight N2 between idle and 5%. It's N2 again.
Hook: "Even in OFF, N2 sagging below 57 lights both plugs."
x.Q0518:
APU switch OFF = 60 s delay, not immediate. Battery switch OFF → ECU loses power → APU stops at once (bank answer B). The FCOM's own 'immediate shutdown' method is PULLING the APU fire switch (option A says ROTATE, which fires the bottle — wrong wording).
Hook: "Immediate APU stop: pull fire switch / battery OFF — not the APU switch."
x.Q0521:
APU fuel: AC pumps ON → from the LEFT side of the fuel manifold; AC pumps OFF → SUCTION fed from MAIN TANK No 1 (the left main tank sits right under that manifold side).
Hook: "APU drinks from the left — tank 1 when nothing pumps."
x.Q0525:
Flameout detection (auto-relight) = uncommanded rapid decrease in N2, OR N2 below idle. Both igniters then fire. No N1 or EGT in the logic.
Hook: "N2 falls → both plugs fire."
x.Q0526:
Approach idle is held until AFTER TOUCHDOWN, when the EEC switches to GROUND MINIMUM IDLE. No speed value (60/84 kt) is involved.
Hook: "Approach idle until wheels on, then ground idle."
x.Q0527:
Approach idle if ANY one of: (1) cowl anti-ice ON either engine, (2) below 19,000 ft AND main gear down, (3) below 19,000 ft AND flaps ≥ 15. Option A is wrong because it requires gear AND flaps together; option C forgets the gear/flap condition. Option D (anti-ice ON) alone is enough.
Hook: "Any ONE: anti-ice, or <FL190 with gear, or <FL190 with flaps 15."
x.Q0528:
APU operation needs ALL three: (1) APU fire switch on the flight deck fire panel IN, (2) APU fire control handle on the APU GROUND control panel (nose wheel well) IN, (3) BATTERY switch ON. Start power comes from AC transfer bus 1 or the main battery.
Hook: "Two fire handles in + battery on."
x.Q0529:
Fail-safe: if the EEC loses the flap or main-gear position signal, it schedules approach idle anyway once BELOW 19,000 ft MSL — so you always have fast spool-up for a go-around.
Hook: "No signals? Approach idle below FL190 anyway."
x.Q0530:
Battery start: only N1, N2 and oil quantity are shown; the EEC isn't powered until N2 > 15% (its own alternator), then everything appears.
Hook: "Battery start: EEC alive at 15."
x.Q0531:
Normal start with AC: until the start switch goes to GRD, the EEC is unpowered → only N1, N2, OIL QUANTITY and VIBRATION are shown (direct sensors). GRD powers the EEC → all parameters appear. (Compare battery start: N1, N2, oil qty until 15% N2.)
Hook: "Before GRD: N1, N2, Qty, Vib."
x.Q0534:
Impending hot start or stall (ground start) → white box around the EGT readout FLASHES. It resets when the start lever goes to CUTOFF or the engine reaches IDLE N2. Newer EEC software also auto-cuts fuel/ignition.
Hook: "Flashing box resets at CUTOFF or idle."
x.Q0535:
Flashing white EGT box (impending hot start/stall) resets when the start lever is moved to CUTOFF or the engine reaches IDLE N2.
Hook: "Flashing box resets at CUTOFF or idle."
x.Q0536:
True — the FCOM says it word for word (APU Fuel Supply, 7.30.1): during APU operation, fuel is automatically heated to prevent icing.
Hook: "APU warms its own fuel."
x.Q0537:
True. During the APU start cycle the APU EGT may jump between 0 and 1100°C before the normal rise and LOW OIL PRESSURE may cycle — no adverse effect; you don't need to monitor EGT during the start (the ECU protects it).
Hook: "APU start: crazy EGT is normal."
x.Q0538:
Wet start (no EGT rise) on the ground → EEC cuts ignition and fuel 15 SECONDS after the start lever to IDLE.
Hook: "Wet start: 15 seconds."
x.Q0539:
RYR NP (aborted engine start criteria): NO EGT increase within 15 SECONDS of raising the start lever to IDLE → abort. It matches the EEC wet-start logic (15 s). Other abort criteria: no oil pressure by stabilized idle, no/slow N1–N2 increase after EGT indication.
Hook: "Light-off within 15 s or abort."
x.Q0541:
False. LEFT igniter ← associated AC TRANSFER bus (not DC standby). RIGHT igniter ← AC STANDBY bus. Igniters are AC-powered.
Hook: "Left = own transfer bus; Right = AC standby."
x.Q0542:
⚠️ The FCOM only defines the amber band as a 'caution range'; 'do not take off' is the bank/airmanship answer. The oil pressure amber band is a CAUTION range (it varies with N2 above 65%). At takeoff thrust oil pressure should be well in the white/normal range; amber pressure at high thrust means an abnormal oil system → do NOT take off (bank answer). The FCOM itself only defines the colours.
Hook: "Amber oil at takeoff power = stay on the ground."
x.Q0544:
The amber ALTN caption in the related EEC switch (aft overhead) = that EEC is in ALTERNATE mode (automatic → ON still visible; manual → ON blanked).
Hook: "Amber ALTN on the switch = alternate."
x.Q0546:
Wet start shutdown: 15 s after START LEVER to IDLE, GROUND STARTS ONLY (not from the start valve opening, nothing in flight).
Hook: "Wet start: 15 seconds, ground only."
x.Q0548:
Aborted engine start (QRH/NP): START LEVER → CUTOFF first (stops fuel and ignition), keep the START switch in GRD and MOTOR for the full 60 s to cool the engine and clear unburned fuel, then start switch OFF. Fire switch only if there's a fire.
Hook: "Cutoff, motor 60, then OFF."
x.Q0549:
FL270 is above both the bleed+electric limit (10,000 ft) and bleed-only limit (17,000 ft), but below the electrical limit (41,000 ft) → APU supplies AC ELECTRICAL power ONLY.
Hook: "10 both, 17 air, 41 electric."
x.Q0550:
Combine two facts: (1) APU takes fuel from the LEFT SIDE OF THE MANIFOLD; (2) center tank pumps produce HIGHER pressure than main pumps, so with all pumps running the manifold is fed by the CENTER tank. → APU burns center tank fuel (assuming fuel in the center).
Hook: "All pumps on = center pumps push hardest = APU drinks center fuel."
x.Q0551:
Yes. Auto-restow holds the control valve in stow 'UNTIL THE THRUST REVERSER IS COMMANDED TO DEPLOY' — so selecting reverse normally overrides it and the reverser deploys as usual.
Hook: "Restow holds until you ask for reverse."
x.Q0552:
The EEC reads the reverse lever position (detent 2 = normal reverse) and automatically sets the reverse thrust (N1) — exactly like forward thrust. The HMU just meters fuel as the EEC commands.
Hook: "Lever asks, EEC sets — forward or reverse."
x.Q0554:
Connect two FCOM facts:
1) 4.20.8: the A/T should run with 'both EECs ON or both in ALTN, as this produces minimum thrust lever separation' → with only EEC 1 in ALTN, engine 1 makes a different thrust for the same lever angle, so the A/T must split the levers to match N1.
2) 4.20.10: the A/T disengages if 'thrust levers become separated more than 10 degrees', followed by the A/T Arm switch releasing to OFF and FLASHING RED A/T disengage lights (the A/T P/RST light).
So with one EEC in ALTN you may see A/T P/RST.
Hook: "Mixed EEC modes → split levers → A/T P/RST."
x.Q0555:
Current RYR FCOM: lost flap or main-gear signal → approach idle schedule begins below 19,000 ft MSL. (Older material said 15,000 ft — the bank answer marked here is 19,000.)
Hook: "No signals? Approach idle below FL190."
x.Q0557:
APU numbers to know: start cycle up to 120 s; WAIT 2 MINUTES (120 s) before using APU bleed; on OFF, 60 s cooling (also run 1 min with no bleed load before shutdown); FAULT 30 s if the fuel valve doesn't close.
Hook: "APU: 2 min warm before bleed, 1 min cool before off."
x.Q0558:
⚠️ The Ryanair 737NG FCOM describes no DC APU fuel pump (with AC pumps off the APU is suction fed from tank 1) – this bank question probably comes from the 737 Classic. Bank answer kept. With no AC fuel pump running, the APU uses its own DC fuel pump. It runs until an AC FUEL PUMP PRESSURIZES THE MANIFOLD. That's why the NP says: with AC power, switch an AC fuel pump ON for APU operation — it extends the life of the APU fuel control unit.
Hook: "DC pump works until an AC pump takes over."
x.Q0560:
Return path: scavenge pumps → SCAVENGE FILTER → MAIN ENGINE OIL COOLER (fuel-cooled) → tank. The IDG oil cooler belongs to the IDG's own oil, not engine oil.
Hook: "Filter, cool, home."
x.Q0561:
Starter cutout ≈ 56% N2. (25% = fuel on, 50% = sustainable idle / ENG FAIL threshold, 59% = stabilized idle.)
Hook: "25 fuel, 56 cutout, 59 idle."
x.Q0562:
Starter cutout ≈ 56% N2.
Hook: "25 fuel, 56 cutout, 59 idle."
x.Q0565:
APU OVERSPEED (amber) has TWO meanings: (1) RPM limit exceeded → automatic shutdown, OR (2) the overspeed shutdown protection FAILED ITS SELF-TEST during a normal shutdown. Like FAULT and LOW OIL PRESSURE, it goes out 5 min after APU OFF and is disarmed with the switch OFF.
Hook: "OVERSPEED = overspeed happened, or the overspeed guard failed its test."
x.Q0566:
False. The APU STARTER-GENERATOR uses AC from transfer bus 1 if available; with NO AC it uses BATTERY power. So AC is not required.
Hook: "APU starts on AC or on the battery."
x.Q0567:
APU start cycle may take up to 120 SECONDS. If the APU doesn't reach speed in the starter's time limit, the cycle terminates; FAULT if the GEN OFF BUS light isn't on by the end.
Hook: "APU: 120 s start, 2 min warm-up, 60 s cool-down."
x.Q0571:
Distinguish the two:
• IMPENDING hot start / stall → white box FLASHES (newer software also cuts fuel).
• EGT EXCEEDS the start limit → box AND dial turn RED and the EEC cuts ignition and fuel.
Both are GROUND-start protections only.
Hook: "White flashing = about to; red = it happened."
x.Q0573:
DEU loss → both EECs lose signals → AUTOMATIC reversion is always to SOFT alternate first, using the LAST VALID flight conditions so thrust doesn't jump. HARD alternate only comes when you retard to idle or select ALTN manually. (A is wrong: hard alternate uses the alternate thrust schedule, not last valid conditions.)
Hook: "Automatic = soft first."
x.Q0578:
False. APU start power comes ONLY from AC transfer bus 1 (ground power) or the MAIN BATTERY, and the ECU needs the battery anyway. Flat batteries + no ground power = no APU start.
Hook: "No battery, no GPU → no APU."
x.Q0579:
APU start cycle: up to 120 seconds.
Hook: "APU: 120 s start."
x.Q0580:
The ECU shuts the APU down for anything that could damage it. Indications: OVERSPEED (overspeed), LOW OIL PRESSURE (low oil pressure), or FAULT (every other malfunction — e.g. high oil temperature, fuel control unit failure, EGT exceedance, failed start). So all three listed causes (high oil temp, overspeed, FCU failure) give an auto shutdown → C.
Hook: "Anything that could hurt it → APU shuts itself down."
x.Q0582:
High APU oil temperature can damage the APU → ECU protective shutdown (FAULT light). A stuck-open inlet door or low fuel temperature are not shutdown causes.
Hook: "Hot oil → APU stops itself."
x.Q0583:
Red box around N1 (or N2/EGT) readout on the ground after shutdown = an IN-FLIGHT EXCEEDANCE occurred → tech log entry.
Hook: "Red box after shutdown = you exceeded something in flight."
x.Q0584:
OIL FILTER BYPASS = impending bypass of the scavenge filter (contamination). QRH: retard the thrust lever; if the alert EXTINGUISHES, continue at the REDUCED thrust setting; if it stays on, shut the engine down. (QRH logic, not in FCOM text.)
Hook: "Throttle back; alert out → keep it at reduced thrust."
x.Q0585:
Soft alternate is entered AUTOMATICALLY when the EEC loses the REQUIRED SIGNALS to run in normal mode (e.g. DEU loss / air data). Not EGT exceedance, not N1 drop.
Hook: "Lost data → soft alternate."
x.Q0586:
The one thing ALWAYS required is DC: battery switch ON (ECU power) — and with no AC the starter-generator runs on battery DC too. AC from transfer bus 1 is used if available but isn't essential. No bleed air or hydraulics are needed (the APU is started electrically).
Hook: "APU needs DC; AC is a bonus."
x.Q0587:
When stowed: the hydraulic ISOLATION VALVE closes (no pressure to the actuators) and the ELECTRO-MECHANICAL LOCK engages; there's also a hydraulically operated locking actuator on each sleeve. These prevent uncommanded deployment. Look at the 'REVERSE THRUST (STOWED)' half of the diagram on 7.20.15.
Hook: "Stowed = valve shut + lock in."
x.Q0588:
OIL FILTER BYPASS alert illuminates PRIOR TO the oil bypassing the scavenge filter — an early warning of contamination.
Hook: "Alert first, bypass later."
x.Q0591:
False. On a battery-only APU start, the metering panel (AC selector at APU GEN) shows CPS FREQ BLANK and AC VOLTS 0 during the start — it doesn't look normal. Only after the start completes and the blue APU GEN OFF BUS light comes on do real frequency and volts appear. The blue light is your cue.
Hook: "Battery APU start: meters blank till the blue light."
x.Q0593:
Only C is right: bleed + electrical simultaneously up to 10,000 ft. Bleed only to 17,000 ft (not 10,000); electrical only to 41,000 ft. In flight the APU can supply only ONE pack.
Hook: "10 both, 17 air, 41 electric."
x.Q0594:
Fuel flow is measured AFTER the ENGINE FUEL SHUTOFF VALVE (the last valve before the combustor; on the schematic the FUEL FLOW TRANSMITTER sits right after it). Displayed on the DU and sent to the FMS. Path: spar valve → 1st stage pump → heat exchangers → filter → 2nd stage pump → HMU → engine valve → flow transmitter → nozzles.
Hook: "Flow is counted after the last valve."
x.Q0595:
The 737NG (-700/-800) uses CFM56-7 engines (typical -800 rating CFM56-7B27; actual rating per performance data). CFM56-3 is the Classic 737 (-300/400/500); JT8D/JT9 are older/other types.
Hook: "NG = -7; Classic = -3."
x.Q0596:
ENG FAIL (amber, on the EGT dial) = engine below sustainable idle (<50% N2) with start lever in IDLE. It stays until: the engine recovers, the start lever goes to CUTOFF, or the ENGINE FIRE SWITCH IS PULLED. Discharging the bottle or EEC ALTN don't clear it.
Hook: "ENG FAIL clears by recovery, CUTOFF, or pulling the fire switch."
x.Q0597:
REV AMBER = thrust reverser has MOVED FROM THE STOWED position (in transit, or not stowed). REV GREEN = fully deployed.
Hook: "Amber moving, green there."
x.Q0598:
REV GREEN = thrust reverser DEPLOYED (then the reverse lever can go past the interlock to detent 2).
Hook: "Amber moving, green there."
x.Q0601:
APU feeds from the LEFT manifold; with all pumps ON the higher-pressure CENTER pumps feed the manifold → APU uses CENTER tank fuel.
Hook: "All pumps on = center pumps push hardest."
x.Q0602:
AC pumps OFF → APU fuel is SUCTION FED from MAIN TANK No 1.
Hook: "No pumps → suction from tank 1."
x.Q0638:
True. APU ground control panel (RIGHT main wheel well): placard says '1. PULL HANDLE DOWN, 2. DISCHARGE BOTTLE'. The BOTTLE DISCHARGE switch is ARMED ONLY IF the APU fire control handle has been pulled — just like the flight deck fire switch must be pulled before it can be rotated. Pulling the handle also shuts down the APU; it must be UP (in) for APU operation (exterior walkaround check).
Hook: "Pull, then discharge."
x.Q0789:
Note: the FCOM lists the -800 'typical' rating as CFM56-7B27; Ryanair's actual rating (Performance Dispatch) is 26K – hence '26K'. A derate/assumed temperature only means the lever sits FURTHER BACK. In normal mode the EEC gives full rated thrust at a lever position short of the stop and MAXIMUM RATED thrust at the forward stop — so pushing both levers fully forward gives the engine's full rating (26K for RYR), regardless of the FMC derate.
Hook: "Firewall = full rating, whatever the FMC says."
x.Q0912:
No 1 reverser = system A. If A fails, the No 1 reverser can use the STANDBY hydraulic system — which must be running (activated automatically, e.g. by loss of A/B pressure logic, or selected via the ALTERNATE FLAPS / FLT CONTROL STBY RUD switch). It deploys/retracts SLOWER with some asymmetry. The PTU only powers the autoslats/LE devices, not reversers.
Hook: "A dead → reverser 1 on standby (slow)."
x.Q0949:
Engine 1 reverser ← SYSTEM A; engine 2 reverser ← SYSTEM B; standby system as backup for either.
Hook: "1-A, 2-B."
x.Q0955:
No 1 engine reverser = SYSTEM A (No 2 = B). Standby is only the alternate.
Hook: "1-A, 2-B."
x.Q1098:
The 737-800 is powered by two CFM56-7 engines (dual-rotor, axial-flow turbofans).
Hook: "NG = -7."
x.Q0356:
Engine fire DETECTION ← BATTERY bus; engine fire EXTINGUISHING ← HOT BATTERY bus. The hot battery bus is wired directly to the battery with no switch — so you can always fire a bottle, even with the battery switch OFF.
Hook: "Bottles on the hot bus — always armed."
x.Q0465:
Engines: TWO bottles (L and R), shared — either or both can be discharged into EITHER engine (rotate the fire switch left or right). APU: ONE bottle. Total for engines + APU = 3. (Cargo has its own single bottle on RYR aircraft; lavatories have their own small automatic extinguishers.)
Hook: "2 shared engine bottles + 1 APU = 3."
x.Q0469:
FAULT light (amber, fire panel):
• OVHT DET in NORMAL → BOTH detector loops of an engine have failed (a single loop failure is automatically deselected with NO indication).
• OVHT DET in A or B → the SELECTED loop has failed.
It does NOT trigger MASTER CAUTION / OVHT/DET.
Hook: "In NORMAL, FAULT = both loops dead."
x.Q0471:
Engine OVERHEAT: both MASTER CAUTION + OVHT/DET annunciator + related ENG OVERHEAT light (amber). No bell.
Engine FIRE: bell + both master FIRE WARN + related fire switch (red) + start lever red (where fitted) + all the overheat indications.
Hook: "Overheat = amber caution; fire = red + bell."
x.Q0474:
TEST switch to FAULT/INOP = tests the FAULT DETECTION CIRCUITS for both engines and the APU → MASTER CAUTION, OVHT/DET, FAULT and APU DET INOP light up. OVHT/FIRE position tests the actual detector loops (engines, APU, wheel well). EXT TEST tests squib continuity. Cargo has its own test.
Hook: "FAULT/INOP tests the monitors; OVHT/FIRE tests the loops."
x.Q0475:
Pulling the APU fire switch UP does NOT discharge anything. It: shuts the APU down (fuel valve closed — backup to the auto shutdown), closes the APU BLEED valve and AIR INLET DOOR, trips the APU GENERATOR, ARMS the bottle squib and lets the switch ROTATE. Rotating (either way) discharges the APU bottle.
Hook: "Pull = isolate + arm; rotate = fire the bottle."
x.Q0517:
APU switch OFF has a 60 s cooling delay. For an IMMEDIATE stop: PULL the APU fire switch — it closes the APU fuel shutoff valve at once (FCOM 7.30.3 says exactly this).
Hook: "Immediate APU stop = pull the fire switch."
x.Q0540:
Each engine has two loops (A and B), each sensing overheat and fire. In NORMAL both must sense the condition → alert (prevents false warnings). If one loop fails, it's automatically deselected (no indication) and the other works alone.
Hook: "Normal = A AND B must agree."
x.Q0553:
APU DET INOP (amber) = the APU detector loop has failed → MASTER CAUTION and OVHT/DET annunciator illuminate. (Contrast: the engine FAULT light does NOT trigger them.) NP: if APU DET INOP doesn't illuminate in the FAULT test, don't operate the APU.
Hook: "APU DET INOP → master caution; engine FAULT → none."
x.Q0604:
Silence the fire bell: push EITHER master FIRE WARN light OR the BELL CUTOUT switch on the overheat/fire panel. Both extinguish the master FIRE WARN lights, silence the bell (and the APU wheel-well horn on the ground) and reset the system for further warnings. The fire switch stays lit as long as the fire exists.
Hook: "Bell off: FIRE WARN light or BELL CUTOUT."
x.Q0605:
False. Fire switches are mechanically locked when there's no fire signal (illumination unlocks them), BUT they can also be unlocked MANUALLY by pushing the FIRE SWITCH OVERRIDE (button under the handle). The FCOM: 'The switches may also be unlocked manually.' Needed e.g. for severe damage/separation with no fire warning.
Hook: "Locked unless lit — or override button."
x.Q0606:
After pushing the cargo DISCH switch, the DISCH light comes on when the bottle has discharged (system fully activated) — it may take UP TO 30 SECONDS. (Single bottle on RYR: 75 min suppression = 60 min flight + 15 min approach/landing/unloading.)
Hook: "Cargo DISCH light: wait up to 30 s."
x.Q0607:
False as worded. The APU ground control panel is in the RIGHT MAIN WHEEL WELL (checked on the walkaround: APU FIRE CONTROL handle UP), not next to the APU in the tail. It has a fire warning light, horn cutout, fire control handle and bottle discharge switch.
Hook: "APU ground panel lives in the right wheel well."
x.Q0608:
Extinguishing exists for: ENGINES, APU, CARGO (suppression) and LAVATORIES. The main gear WHEEL WELL has detection ONLY — the remedy for a wheel well fire is to extend the gear (QRH).
Hook: "Wheel well: you can see it, you can't spray it."
x.Q0609:
RYR (YF501–YW164): ONE cargo fire bottle (air-conditioning mix bay) that can be discharged into EITHER hold — push FWD or AFT ARMED to select, then DISCH. 75 min of suppression.
Hook: "One cargo bottle, two doors."
x.Q0610:
⚠️ Nozzle/placard colours are NOT in the FCOM – bank answer; the FCOM only says there's no flight deck indication. Lavatory extinguisher (under the sink) is automatic and gives NO flight deck indication. Discharge can only be checked locally: the discharge nozzle tips change colour (black → grey/silver) and the temperature indicator placard turns black. (Local detail is not in the FCOM — bank answer.)
Hook: "Lav bottle: no flight-deck light — look at the nozzles."
x.Q0611:
If an engine fire switch doesn't illuminate during OVHT/FIRE test (both loops must agree in NORMAL), find the bad loop by repeating the OVHT/FIRE test with OVHT DET at A, then at B. Whichever position fails = failed loop. Then leave the switch on the good loop.
Hook: "Test A, test B, keep the good one."
x.Q0612:
Cargo fire TEST tests BOTH: the FWD and AFT detector loops (warning lights) AND the bottle discharge SQUIB circuit continuity (green EXT lights); DISCH light also illuminates. No tie-in to MASTER CAUTION.
Hook: "Cargo test = loops + squibs."
x.Q0613:
False. Cargo holds have smoke detection + fire SUPPRESSION, but the wheel well has fire DETECTION only — no suppression/extinguishing at all.
Hook: "Wheel well: detect only."
x.Q0614:
True. Only the ENGINES have overheat detection (ENG OVERHEAT light) as well as fire (illuminated fire switch). APU: fire switch only. Cargo: FWD/AFT fire warning lights (smoke detection). Wheel well: WHEEL WELL fire light.
Hook: "Overheat lights exist for engines only."
x.Q0615:
True. Engines = overheat + fire warnings. APU, cargo and wheel well = fire (or smoke) warnings only.
Hook: "Overheat lights exist for engines only."
x.Q0616:
Same logic: to find which loop failed, re-run the OVHT/FIRE test with OVHT DET at A, then at B. In A or B the system is single-loop, so the failed loop shows up (no fire indication / FAULT).
Hook: "Test A, test B, keep the good one."
x.Q0617:
Engine fire switch UP: closes FUEL (engine + spar valves), HYDRAULIC shutoff and ENGINE BLEED valves; DISABLES the thrust reverser; trips the GENERATOR; deactivates the EDP LOW PRESSURE light; ARMS ONE SQUIB ON EACH of the two bottles; lets the switch ROTATE (left = L bottle, right = R bottle). It doesn't close the PACK inlet directly (pack valve closes because bleed is lost), and nothing discharges until you rotate.
Hook: "Pull: fuel, hyd, bleed, rev, gen off — arm both bottles."
x.Q0618:
Lavatory fire: the extinguisher under the sink fires AUTOMATICALLY (heat-activated). Nothing on the flight deck: no OVHT/DET, no MASTER CAUTION. Smoke detector alarms are local to the cabin.
Hook: "Lav fire: automatic and silent to the cockpit."
x.Q0619:
Cargo DISCH light: up to 30 SECONDS after pushing DISCH.
Hook: "Cargo DISCH light: wait up to 30 s."
x.Q0620:
⚠️ NOT IN THE FCOM – bank answer (no time given in the FCOM). The amber BOTTLE DISCHARGED light comes on when the bottle has discharged (or pressure is low). The FCOM gives no time; engine/APU bottles discharge within seconds → 'less than 5 seconds' (bank). Compare: CARGO DISCH light may take up to 30 s.
Hook: "Engine bottle: seconds; cargo bottle: up to 30 s."
x.Q0621:
L/R BOTTLE DISCHARGED illuminates within a FEW SECONDS of rotating the fire switch (bottle empty or low pressure). No exact figure in FCOM. Don't confuse with the cargo DISCH light (up to 30 s).
Hook: "Engine bottle: seconds; cargo bottle: up to 30 s."
x.Q0623:
True for RYR aircraft (YF501–YW164): a SINGLE cargo fire bottle, 75 min suppression. Only the effectivity YA573 has two bottles (195 min).
Hook: "RYR cargo: one bottle, 75 minutes."
x.Q0624:
True. The two-bottle option (first full discharge + second metered slow discharge, 195 min = 180 + 15) is only on effectivity YA573. The RYR fleet YF501–YW164 has ONE bottle: 75 min = 60 min to land + 15 min.
Hook: "RYR: 60 + 15 = 75."
x.Q0625:
OVHT DET in NORMAL: loops A and B both active; a FIRE alert needs BOTH loops to sense FIRE. (A loop sensing fire and the other only overheat isn't enough for a fire warning.)
Hook: "Normal = A AND B must agree."
x.Q0626:
RYR single cargo bottle: 75 MINUTES of suppression = 60 min of flight to reach an airport + 15 min for missed approach/landing/unloading. (195 min = 180 + 15 is only for the two-bottle YA573 option.) It SUPPRESSES rather than extinguishes — the warning may come back.
Hook: "60 to land + 15 = 75."
x.Q0627:
APU (and engine) BOTTLE DISCHARGED light = bottle discharged OR its PRESSURE IS LOW (leak). That's why a lit light on preflight means a no-go item.
Hook: "DISCHARGED = empty or leaking."
x.Q0628:
⚠️ Nozzle colour is NOT in the FCOM – bank answer; the FCOM only says there's no flight deck indication. No flight deck indication of a lavatory bottle discharge. Locally, the extinguisher DISCHARGE NOZZLES change colour (black → grey). Local detail is not in FCOM.
Hook: "Lav bottle: look at the nozzles."
x.Q0629:
The lav extinguisher nozzles turn GREY (from black) when discharged; no flight deck or attendant-panel light, no gauge reading used.
Hook: "Lav bottle: grey nozzles = fired."
x.Q0631:
⚠️ NOT IN THE FCOM – bank answer (the FCOM gives no detector numbers). The FCOM only says each cargo compartment has SMOKE detectors in a DUAL-LOOP configuration — it gives no numbers. The bank answer is AFT 6 / FWD 4 (the aft hold is longer). Learn the bank number but know it's not in the FCOM.
Hook: "Aft is bigger → 6; forward → 4."
x.Q0632:
Yes. After the initial cargo fire, the FWD/AFT light can go out, stay on or come back. If it re-illuminates, both master FIRE WARN lights AND the bell come back too. The bottle suppresses rather than extinguishes, so smoke may re-trigger it.
Hook: "Cargo light returns → full warning returns."
x.Q0633:
APU DET INOP (amber) = APU detector loop failed → MASTER CAUTION + OVHT/DET annunciator. (The engine FAULT light does NOT trigger them — its note says 'do not illuminate'.)
Hook: "APU DET INOP → master caution; engine FAULT → none."
x.Q0634:
True. APU fire: bell + master FIRE WARN on the flight deck (air and ground), and on the GROUND ONLY the APU fire warning HORN sounds and the red light FLASHES on the APU ground control panel (right main wheel well) to alert ground crew. HORN CUTOUT silences it (light goes steady).
Hook: "APU fire on the ground: horn in the wheel well."
x.Q0635:
Cargo fire detection is by SMOKE ONLY (dual-loop smoke detectors, powered by DC bus 1 and 2). Compare: engines and APU use heat-sensing loops; wheel well uses a heat loop.
Hook: "Cargo smells smoke; engines feel heat."
x.Q0639:
RYR has ONE cargo bottle with TWO discharge squibs (one routes to FWD, one to AFT). The two green EXT lights in the cargo TEST = both squib circuits of that ONE bottle passed the continuity test. They don't measure pressure.
Hook: "Two green = two squibs, one bottle."
x.Q0642:
CARGO FIRE checklist step 1: push the affected FWD or AFT cargo fire ARM switch → white ARMED illuminates, that squib is armed (selects which hold), but NOTHING discharges. Step 2: push DISCH → bottle discharges (DISCH light up to 30 s).
Hook: "ARM picks the hold; DISCH fires the bottle."
x.Q0643:
APU DET INOP = APU fire detection inoperative. Rule: do NOT operate the APU (also if the light FAILS to illuminate during the FAULT/INOP test — the detection monitoring is suspect). A fire you can't detect is not acceptable.
Hook: "Can't detect APU fire → don't run the APU."
x.Q0644:
Cargo detection: dual loop; normally BOTH loops must detect SMOKE to give an alert. With a detector failure you can select single loop (DET SELECT A or B); a power failure in one loop converts automatically.
Hook: "Cargo: both loops smell smoke."
x.Q0645:
Silencing the bell (FIRE WARN light or BELL CUTOUT) lets the crew TALK while doing memory items/checklist, and RESETS the system so a NEW warning (e.g. another engine, re-ignition) will sound again. It doesn't mean the fire is out — the fire switch stays lit.
Hook: "Silence to talk; reset to hear the next one."
x.Q0646:
Engine loops sense OVERHEAT at a lower temperature and FIRE at a higher one. As an engine fire grows, it passes the overheat threshold first → ENG OVERHEAT + MASTER CAUTION + OVHT/DET (and they stay on during the fire). The APU has fire detection ONLY (no overheat), so an APU fire gives FIRE WARN but no master caution.
Hook: "Engine: overheat before fire. APU: fire only."
x.Q0647:
Yes. Extinguishing is on the HOT battery bus (live with BAT switch OFF). But detection (battery bus) is dead, so the switch won't illuminate/unlock by itself → use the FIRE SWITCH OVERRIDE to unlock it, pull, rotate.
Hook: "BAT off: bottles live, detection dead → override and pull."
x.Q0648:
Normal. The cargo DISCH light can take UP TO 30 SECONDS to illuminate after you push DISCH. Wait before assuming a failure.
Hook: "Cargo DISCH light: wait up to 30 s."
x.Q0840:
Pulling the engine fire switch closes BOTH the ENGINE fuel shutoff valve AND the SPAR fuel shutoff valve (exactly like the start lever to CUTOFF). It never discharges automatically — you must ROTATE. (Power: spar valve DC motor from hot battery bus; engine valve solenoid from battery bus.)
Hook: "Pull = both fuel valves shut; rotate = bottle."
x.Q1043:
Engine fire indications: FIRE WARNING BELL + both master FIRE WARN + engine fire switch red (+ start lever red where fitted) + all the overheat indications (MASTER CAUTION, OVHT/DET, ENG OVERHEAT). The missing one is the BELL.
Hook: "Fire = red lights + BELL."
x.Q0345:
Normally, moving the control column AGAINST the trim direction opens column-actuated cutout switches that stop electric trim. The STAB TRIM OVERRIDE switch (guarded, aft electronic panel) BYPASSES those column cutout switches so the control wheel trim switches work again. It's not the MAIN ELECT/AUTOPILOT cutout switches on the pedestal.
Hook: "Override = ignore the column cutouts."
x.Q0472:
Elevator jam: the override mechanism lets the two control COLUMNS be PHYSICALLY SEPARATED. Force against the jam breaks out EITHER column; the one that moves freely controls the elevator. Elevator travel is reduced but enough for flare; forces are HIGHER than manual reversion.
Hook: "Jam → push hard → columns split → free one flies."
x.Q0490:
Flight spoilers assist roll: they rise on the wing with UP aileron (the down-going wing) once the control wheel is turned more than ~10°; they stay faired on the other wing.
Hook: "10° of wheel → spoilers help."
x.Q0492:
Ground spoilers: 4 total, TWO per wing, all powered by SYSTEM A. They extend only on the ground. (Flight spoilers: 4 per wing.)
Hook: "Ground spoilers: 2 per wing, all on A."
x.Q0493:
Leading edge devices per wing: FOUR SLATS (outboard) + TWO KRUEGER LE FLAPS (inboard). On the LE DEVICES annunciator: flaps 1–4 and slats 1–8 for both wings.
Hook: "Per wing: 4 slats + 2 Kruegers."
x.Q0563:
LE FLAPS TRANSIT (amber): any LE device in transit, not in programmed position, uncommanded motion, or during alternate extension until LE fully extended and flaps 10. It is INHIBITED during AUTOSLAT operation in flight (so a stall-protection slat movement doesn't distract you).
Hook: "Autoslat moves silently — TRANSIT inhibited."
x.Q0574:
FOUR flight spoilers per wing (8 total), split between systems A and B in symmetric pairs, so one hydraulic failure keeps symmetric spoilers. Plus 2 ground spoilers per wing.
Hook: "4 flight + 2 ground per wing."
x.Q0649:
Don't extend flaps above 20,000 ft — at high altitude the same IAS means higher Mach → excessive structural loads. (Also a limitation: max flap extension altitude 20,000 ft.)
Hook: "Flaps: below FL200."
x.Q0650:
Stall identification = 3 systems: YAW DAMPER (reduced rudder commands at high AOA), ELEVATOR FEEL SHIFT module and SPEED TRIM (nose-down trim). EFS raises SYSTEM A pressure to the elevator feel & centering unit → column force about DOUBLES, making it hard to pull further into the stall. Inhibited on the ground, below 100 ft RA, or A/P engaged.
Hook: "EFS = heavy column (system A)."
x.Q0651:
Auto speedbrake on landing: lever ARMED, RA < 10 ft, strut compression, thrust levers at IDLE, wheel spin-up > 60 kt. ANY strut compression enables the FLIGHT spoilers; only the RIGHT MAIN strut compression enables the GROUND spoilers (via the ground spoiler interlock valve).
Hook: "Ground spoilers wait for the RIGHT main."
x.Q0652:
FCOM 9.10.11 uses "OR": the light comes on for EITHER condition (not both at the same time). The correct option is the one that lists both possible meanings. SPEED BRAKE DO NOT ARM (amber) has two meanings: (1) abnormal condition or test input in the auto speedbrake system; (2) after landing, wheel speed below 60 kt and the speedbrake lever NOT yet DOWN (reminder to stow). Deactivated with the lever DOWN.
Hook: "DO NOT ARM = fault, or 'stow the lever' below 60 kt."
x.Q0653:
Lever left DOWN (forgot to arm) on landing/RTO: the auto speedbrake still works when wheels spin up > 60 kt, both thrust levers at IDLE, AND the REVERSE THRUST levers are raised. Then the SPEED BRAKE lever moves UP automatically and all spoilers deploy. Advancing a thrust lever afterwards retracts them.
Hook: "Forgot to arm? Pull reverse — spoilers follow."
x.Q0655:
STBY RUD ON (amber) = standby rudder system commanded ON to pressurize the standby rudder PCU — MANUALLY (either FLT CONTROL switch to STBY RUD) OR AUTOMATICALLY (standby auto-on logic at takeoff/landing, or the Force Fight Monitor). It triggers MASTER CAUTION + FLT CONT.
Hook: "STBY RUD ON = standby rudder pressurized, however it got there."
x.Q0656:
If wheel spin-up isn't detected, the system uses the air/ground sensing: ANY strut compression (ground mode) → FLIGHT spoilers deploy. The GROUND spoilers additionally need the RIGHT main strut compressed (mechanical linkage opens the ground spoiler interlock valve).
Hook: "Any strut → flight spoilers; right main → ground spoilers."
x.Q0657:
True (YW098–YW164, short field performance): flap lever 1 to 25 → LE flaps FULL extended, slats only to EXTEND. Beyond 25 (30/40) → slats to FULL EXTEND. Older aircraft (YA573–YW097) switch at flaps 5 instead.
Hook: "SFP: slats full only beyond 25."
x.Q0658:
ALTERNATE FLAPS master: OFF (guarded) normal; ARM → closes TE flap bypass valve, activates standby pump, arms the ALTERNATE FLAPS position switch. There's no ON or STBY position.
Hook: "ARM = bypass shut, standby pump on, position switch live."
x.Q0659:
The LE (Krueger) flaps inboard of the engines have only two positions: retracted or FULL EXTENDED. At FLAP 1 they go straight to full extended. Only the slats have the intermediate EXTEND position.
Hook: "Kruegers: in or full out."
x.Q0660:
ARM: arms the position switch, activates the standby pump, closes the TE flap bypass valve. Nothing extends until you hold the ALTERNATE FLAPS position switch DOWN. (Standby rudder pressurisation is done by FLT CONTROL STBY RUD.)
Hook: "ARM prepares; DOWN extends."
x.Q0661:
Autoslat: with TE flaps 1–5 (1–25 on YW098+), slats sit at EXTEND; approaching the stall the slats drive to FULL EXTEND before stick shaker, then return when AOA reduces. Powered by SYSTEM B (backup: system A via the PTU) — not system A, not an electrical bus.
Hook: "Near stall → slats full out (system B)."
x.Q0662:
False ('for ALL aircraft from flap 10'). Flap load relief is armed at flaps 30 and 40 on YA573–YW097; only YW098–YW164 have it at 10, 15, 25, 30 and 40. Not available during alternate extension.
Hook: "Load relief: 30/40 (older), 10–40 (newer)."
x.Q0663:
True. On TE asymmetry, skew or uncommanded motion the FSEU closes the TE BYPASS valve → hydraulic flap drive stops. The flaps can still be moved by the ELECTRIC alternate flap motor — but with NO asymmetry/skew protection.
Hook: "FSEU stops hydraulics; electric motor still works (unprotected)."
x.Q0664:
FSEU LE uncommanded motion protection: with no command, if TWO LE flaps or TWO OR MORE slats move on one wing → FSEU shuts down LE control and lights LE FLAPS TRANSIT. (Skew detection exists for TE flaps, not LE.)
Hook: "Two LE devices move uncommanded → FSEU freezes the LE."
x.Q0665:
Flap load relief protects the TE flaps from EXCESSIVE AIR LOADS: if the CAPTAIN's IAS (left ADIRU) is too high for the selected setting, the FSEU retracts to the next lower setting and re-extends when speed drops (e.g. 40→30 above 163 kt, back below 158). The FLAP lever doesn't move; the indicator shows it.
Hook: "Too fast for the flaps → they back off one notch."
x.Q0666:
Yaw damper (main or standby): DUTCH ROLL prevention, GUST damping and TURN coordination. Its inputs do NOT move the rudder pedals (rudder TRIM does). The pilot can override with pedals or trim.
Hook: "Dutch roll, gusts, turns — pedals stay still."
x.Q0667:
The pilot can override EITHER yaw damper (main or standby) using the RUDDER PEDALS OR RUDDER TRIM.
Hook: "Pedals or trim beat the yaw damper."
x.Q0668:
4 flight spoilers per wing → 8 flight spoilers total (roll + speedbrake). Plus 4 ground spoilers → 12 spoilers in all.
Hook: "8 flight + 4 ground = 12."
x.Q0669:
FOUR flight spoilers on each wing.
Hook: "4 flight + 2 ground per wing."
x.Q0671:
Aileron transfer mechanism: the CAPTAIN's wheel is tied to the AILERONS, the F/O's wheel to the SPOILERS. If the aileron system/Captain's wheel jams, force on the F/O's wheel breaks out and gives roll control via the FLIGHT SPOILERS. If the spoilers jam, the Captain's wheel keeps the ailerons.
Hook: "Captain = ailerons, F/O = spoilers."
x.Q0672:
Ground spoilers deploy when the RIGHT MAIN gear strut compresses (opens the ground spoiler interlock valve).
Hook: "Ground spoilers wait for the RIGHT main."
x.Q0673:
True. YW098–YW164: slats move from EXTEND to FULL EXTEND only beyond flaps 25.
Hook: "SFP: slats full only beyond 25."
x.Q0674:
PRIMARY controls (ailerons, elevators, rudder): systems A AND B (either can do all). Backup: STANDBY hydraulics for the RUDDER; MANUAL reversion for ailerons and elevators. SECONDARY (flaps/slats): system B, with electric TE flaps / PTU / standby for LE as backups.
Hook: "Primary A+B → standby rudder, manual rest. Secondary = B."
x.Q0676:
Flap load relief armed at flaps 30 and 40 (YA573–YW097; bank answer). YW098+ add 10, 15, 25. Not with alternate flaps.
Hook: "Load relief: 30/40."
x.Q0677:
Flap load relief is an FSEU function, armed at flaps 30 and 40 (bank answer; YW098+ also 10/15/25).
Hook: "Load relief: 30/40."
x.Q0678:
True. FSEU closes the TE bypass valve (hydraulic drive stopped); the electric alternate flap motor can still move the TE flaps.
Hook: "FSEU stops hydraulics; electric motor still works."
x.Q0679:
True. After the FSEU closes the bypass valve, ALTERNATE FLAPS (electric) can still move the TE flaps — without asymmetry/skew protection.
Hook: "FSEU stops hydraulics; ALTN FLAPS still works."
x.Q0680:
Yaw damper: dutch roll prevention + gust damping + turn coordination; rudder pedals are NOT displaced.
Hook: "Dutch roll, gusts, turns — pedals stay still."
x.Q0681:
True — FSEU closes the TE bypass valve on asymmetry/skew/uncommanded motion; ALTERNATE FLAPS (electric) still moves the flaps.
Hook: "FSEU stops hydraulics; ALTN FLAPS still works."
x.Q0682:
YAW DAMPER switch trips OFF (amber YAW DAMPER light, can't reset) when: SMYD senses a yaw damper fault, the yaw damper doesn't respond, or the B FLT CONTROL switch is OFF or STBY RUD (main yaw damper uses system B). Exception: in manual reversion with BOTH FLT CONTROL switches at STBY RUD, it can be reset ON → standby yaw damper.
Hook: "Main yaw damper lives on B."
x.Q0683:
In flight: speed brakes in a turn (and especially at an intermediate position) GREATLY increase roll rate — be careful. Beyond the FLIGHT DETENT → buffeting, PROHIBITED in flight. SPEEDBRAKES EXTENDED light warns if they're out with flaps > 10 or below 800 ft RA.
Hook: "Flight detent max; careful in turns."
x.Q0684:
FLT CONTROL LOW PRESSURE (amber, one for A and one for B) = LOW pressure from THAT hydraulic system to the ailerons, elevator and rudder. It goes out when that FLT CONTROL switch is set to STBY RUD and the standby rudder shutoff valve opens.
Hook: "One light per system: A or B pressure to the primary controls is low."
x.Q0687:
Normally pulling/pushing the column AGAINST the trim direction stops electric trim (column cutout switches). STAB TRIM OVERRIDE bypasses those switches → electric trim works REGARDLESS of column position. It doesn't remove power or A/P trim (that's the CUTOUT switches).
Hook: "Override = trim even against the column."
x.Q0688:
Force Fight Monitor (in the main rudder PCU): detects OPPOSING pressure between the A and B actuators (one input jammed/disconnected) → automatically turns on the STANDBY pump, opens the standby rudder shutoff valve (standby rudder PCU pressurized) and lights STBY RUD ON + MASTER CAUTION + FLT CONT.
Hook: "A fights B → standby rudder comes to help."
x.Q0689:
Speed Trim System = speed stability augmentation in MANUAL flight (A/P not engaged), most useful at low weight, aft CG and high thrust (takeoff, climb, go-around). It trims the stabilizer opposite to the speed change to return to the trimmed speed. Don't confuse with MACH TRIM (above M.615, adjusts elevator).
Hook: "Speed trim: low speed, hand flying. Mach trim: high Mach."
x.Q0690:
Max SPEED BRAKE lever position in flight = FLIGHT DETENT. Beyond it (towards UP, ground use) causes buffeting and is prohibited in flight.
Hook: "Flight detent max."
x.Q0691:
ALTERNATE FLAPS master ARM: arms the position switch, starts the standby pump, closes the TE flap bypass valve. Nothing moves yet. LE devices are extended HYDRAULICALLY (standby), TE flaps ELECTRICALLY.
Hook: "ARM prepares; DOWN extends."
x.Q0692:
FEEL DIFF PRESS (amber): excessive DIFFERENTIAL pressure in the ELEVATOR FEEL COMPUTER — caused by failure of either HYDRAULIC system (A/B) or either ELEVATOR FEEL PITOT system (or erroneous EFS activation). On RYR aircraft it's armed with flaps UP OR DOWN. Nothing to do with the standby system or the Captain's pitot.
Hook: "Feel computer sees A≠B → FEEL DIFF PRESS."
x.Q0693:
Alternate (electric) flap drive has NO asymmetry or skew protection → watch the flap position indicator (both needles) closely. The switch must be HELD down (it doesn't latch).
Hook: "Alternate flaps: no protection — watch the needles."
x.Q0694:
After the override operates, the columns are SEPARATED; whichever column is free provides elevator control. Forces are HIGHER (not lighter); travel reduced but enough for flare; use stab trim to relieve sustained force.
Hook: "Jam → columns split → free one flies (heavy)."
x.Q0696:
Primary flight controls: hydraulic A and B; backups = STANDBY system for the RUDDER and MANUAL REVERSION for ailerons/elevators. (B forgets the standby rudder; C/D talk about secondary controls wrongly.)
Hook: "Primary A+B → standby rudder, manual rest."
x.Q0698:
Yes: without wheel spin-up, the flight spoilers still deploy when the air/ground system goes to GROUND mode (any strut compressed); ground spoilers also need the right main strut.
Hook: "Any strut → flight spoilers; right main → ground spoilers."
x.Q0790:
AUTO SLAT FAIL: steady = auto slat SYSTEM failure (both SMYDs). If it only shows on MASTER CAUTION RECALL and extinguishes on reset = failure of a SINGLE SMYD computer (redundancy lost, system still works). Same 'recall' logic as SPEED TRIM FAIL / MACH TRIM FAIL (single FCC channel).
Hook: "Recall-only light = one of two computers failed."
x.Q0926:
The rudder has TWO PCUs: the MAIN rudder PCU (systems A and B) and the STANDBY rudder PCU (standby hydraulic system). The standby PCU is the backup.
Hook: "Main PCU on A+B; standby PCU on standby."
x.Q0932:
FEEL DIFF PRESS: flaps up OR down (RYR aircraft), either hydraulic system A/B fails or either elevator feel PITOT system fails → excessive differential pressure in the feel computer.
Hook: "Feel computer sees A≠B → FEEL DIFF PRESS."
x.Q0934:
Autoslats normally use SYSTEM B. Backup: the PTU uses system A PRESSURE to drive a pump that pressurizes system B FLUID (fluids never mix).
Hook: "PTU: A's muscle, B's blood."
x.Q0940:
The PTU kicks in when a loss of pressure is sensed from the system B ENGINE-DRIVEN PUMP (the high-volume pump). (PTU logic also needs flaps not up / airborne — see Hydraulics.)
Hook: "B's engine pump dies → PTU helps."
x.Q0952:
Main yaw damper uses SYSTEM B → lost with B. The standby yaw damper is only available in MANUAL REVERSION (A AND B lost, both FLT CONTROL switches to STBY RUD). With A still working you can't use it → main and standby yaw damper functions are lost.
Hook: "B lost → no yaw damper (standby YD only in manual reversion)."
x.Q0971:
Autoslats: normally SYSTEM B; alternate via the PTU (system A pressure, B fluid).
Hook: "Slats and flaps live on B."
x.Q1037:
In flight the SPEED BRAKE lever limit is the FLIGHT DETENT.
Hook: "Flight detent max."
x.Q1038:
Elevator feel computer inputs: AIRSPEED (from the dedicated elevator pitot probes on the fin) and STABILIZER POSITION. It uses hydraulic A or B, whichever is higher, and the feel & centering unit passes the force to the columns.
Hook: "Feel = airspeed + stab position."
x.Q1039:
Captain's wheel = ailerons; F/O's wheel = spoilers. If the SPOILERS jam, the CAPTAIN's wheel still drives the AILERONS (the F/O's wheel and the spoilers are out).
Hook: "Captain = ailerons, F/O = spoilers."
x.Q1045:
Speed trim operating conditions: between 100 KIAS and M0.60 (fading to zero by M0.68), 10 s after takeoff, 5 s after releasing the trim switches, A/P NOT engaged, trim requirement sensed.
Hook: "Speed trim: 100 kt to M.60, hand flying."
x.Q1101:
The elevator control column override mechanism lets the two columns be PHYSICALLY SEPARATED during a jam. The feel & centering unit is a different component.
Hook: "Jam → columns split."
x.Q0397:
Flight data recorder, switch NORMAL (guarded): IN FLIGHT – runs whenever electrical power is available; ON THE GROUND – power available AND either engine running. TEST lets maintenance run it on the ground without engines. (CVR: AUTO powers it from first engine start to 5 min after last shutdown.)
Hook: "FDR on the ground needs an engine."
x.Q0445:
FCOM 10.41.22 (TCAS symbols): 'The number and associated signs indicate altitude of traffic in hundreds of feet relative to the airplane' → −07 = 700 ft BELOW you. 'The arrow indicates traffic climbing or descending at a rate >= 500 fpm' → down arrow = DESCENDING at 500 fpm or more. So: traffic below, descending ≥ 500 fpm. It is not 'ascending at 700 fpm' — 07 is altitude, not rate.
Hook: "Number = where (hundreds of ft); arrow = moving ≥500 fpm."
x.Q0448:
DSPLY SOURCE 1/2 (amber, on both PFDs) = all six DUs are being driven by a SINGLE DEU, chosen automatically (DEU failure) or manually (SOURCE selector ALL ON 1/2). Remember: one DEU lost also puts both EECs into alternate.
Hook: "DSPLY SOURCE = one DEU drives everything."
x.Q0468:
Outboard DU fails → PFD AUTOMATICALLY moves to the INBOARD DU (the PFD always has priority). Inboard DU fails → PFD stays outboard. Upper DU fails → engines move to the lower DU.
Hook: "The PFD always survives — it jumps inboard."
x.Q0486:
Minimums (DH RADIO or BARO MDA) are set by EACH PILOT on their OWN EFIS control panel (MINS selector). Not on the FMC or MCP. If an EFIS panel fails, CONTROL PANEL BOTH ON 1/2 lets one panel drive both sides.
Hook: "Your mins, your EFIS panel."
x.Q0520:
Displays source panel has TWO selectors: CONTROL PANEL (BOTH ON 1 / NORMAL / BOTH ON 2) chooses which EFIS CONTROL PANEL drives the displays; SOURCE (ALL ON 1 / AUTO / ALL ON 2) chooses the DEU. BOTH ON 2 = the F/O's EFIS panel controls both pilots' displays.
Hook: "BOTH ON = EFIS panel; ALL ON = DEU."
x.Q0523:
Lower-left PFD annunciations: CDS MAINT (white) = DISPATCHABLE fault; CDS FAULT (amber) = NON-DISPATCHABLE fault. Both only shown on the GROUND, before the SECOND engine is started.
Hook: "White MAINT go; amber FAULT no-go."
x.Q0589:
Radio altitude on the PFD appears below 2,500 ft AGL: between 2,500 and 1,000 ft as a DIGITAL readout only; below 1,000 ft with the ROUND DIAL around it. Turns amber below the RA minimums.
Hook: "2500 digits appear; 1000 the dial closes in."
x.Q0699:
ND orientation: MAP, VOR and APP modes are HEADING (or track) UP, with a compass rose. PLAN mode is TRUE NORTH UP (true-north arrow, used to step through the route on the LEGS page; no WXR/TCAS/TERR shown).
Hook: "Plan = paper map: north up."
x.Q0700:
IAS DISAGREE (amber, under the speed tape): Captain's and F/O's airspeeds differ by more than 5 KT for 5 continuous SECONDS. Compare: ALT DISAGREE = 200 ft for 5 s; AOA DISAGREE = 10° for 10 s (above 400 ft RA).
Hook: "IAS 5/5, ALT 200/5, AOA 10/10."
x.Q0701:
Top of the lower amber bar = MINIMUM MANEUVER SPEED, giving 1.3 g capability (= 40° bank level) to: STICK SHAKER below ~20,000 ft, LOW-SPEED BUFFET above ~20,000 ft. (Upper amber bar with flaps up = max maneuver speed, 1.3 g to high-speed buffet.) Below the amber is the red/black stick-shaker bar.
Hook: "1.3 g: shaker below FL200, buffet above."
x.Q0703:
BARO minimums (green) turn AMBER and FLASH for 3 s when the airplane descends below the selected minimum altitude (DA/MDA). It goes back to green passing mins + 75 ft in a go-around, or reset with RST.
Hook: "Amber flash = you're at minimums."
x.Q0704:
DISPLAYS CONTROL PANEL (amber, lower right of the PFD) = the EFIS CONTROL PANEL on that side has failed (altitude info removed). Fix: CONTROL PANEL select switch to BOTH ON 1 or 2 so the other EFIS panel drives both sides.
Hook: "DISPLAYS CONTROL PANEL = your EFIS panel died."
x.Q0705:
The V2+15 bug is shown for TAKEOFF (target initial climb speed) and is removed at the FIRST FLAP RETRACTION or when VREF is entered in the CDU.
Hook: "V2+15 lives until the first flap comes in."
x.Q0706:
CDS MAINT (white) = DISPATCHABLE CDS fault; ground only, before SECOND engine start. CDS FAULT (amber) = non-dispatchable.
Hook: "White MAINT go; amber FAULT no-go."
x.Q0707:
Magenta readout above the speed tape = TARGET speed: the speed in the MCP IAS/MACH window, or the FMC speed when the window is blank (VNAV). Magenta = selected/target throughout the PFD.
Hook: "Magenta = what you asked for."
x.Q0708:
INSTR SWITCH (amber) = both pilots' displays use the SAME IRU source, because the IRS TRANSFER switch (forward overhead panel, NAVIGATION/DISPLAYS area) is not in NORMAL (BOTH ON L or BOTH ON R). Independent sources lost → warns the crew.
Hook: "INSTR SWITCH = both on one IRS."
x.Q0709:
IAS DISAGREE = Captain and F/O airspeeds differ > 5 kt for 5 s. (Unreliable airspeed NNC.)
Hook: "IAS 5/5, ALT 200/5, AOA 10/10."
x.Q0710:
Two DEUs (Display Electronic Units): DEU 1 drives Capt outboard, Capt inboard and upper DU; DEU 2 drives F/O outboard, F/O inboard and lower DU. Either can drive all six. Each receives both ADIRUs.
Hook: "Two DEUs, six screens."
x.Q0711:
Failure flags REPLACE the failed display: airspeed failed → amber SPD flag on the speed tape. Similar: ALT, ATT, HDG, VERT, FD, LOC, G/S flags.
Hook: "Failed tape → amber flag with its name."
x.Q0714:
V/S digits (white) appear when vertical speed is MORE THAN 400 FPM — above the scale when climbing, below when descending.
Hook: "Digits after 400 fpm."
x.Q0715:
Magenta V/S bug = vertical speed SELECTED in the MCP V/S window, shown only with V/S pitch mode ENGAGED. The white pointer is actual V/S.
Hook: "Magenta bug = MCP V/S target."
x.Q0716:
MAP RANGE DISAGREE (amber) = range selected on the EFIS panel ≠ MAP display range. Similar: WXR RANGE DISAGREE (weather radar), TERR RANGE DISAGREE (terrain).
Hook: "___ RANGE DISAGREE = that layer isn't at your selected range."
x.Q0717:
FPV = FLIGHT PATH VECTOR: shows flight path angle (vertically) and drift (laterally) on the attitude indicator, selected with the FPV switch on the EFIS panel.
Hook: "FPV = where the airplane is actually going."
x.Q0718:
Picture: INSTR SWITCH (amber) → IRS transfer switch on the overhead panel not in NORMAL; both displays on the same IRU.
Hook: "INSTR SWITCH = both on one IRS."
x.Q0719:
ISFD attitude messages: ATT:RST → push the ATT RST switch to reset attitude (hold level/unaccelerated); ATT 10s → 10-second realignment in progress; WAIT ATT → temporary self-correcting loss. INIT 90s = initial alignment after power-up (don't move the airplane).
Hook: "RST says: push reset."
x.Q0720:
Pitch Limit Indication (amber 'eyebrows' on the ADI) = the pitch attitude at which the STICK SHAKER activates for the current conditions. Shown with flaps not up (and at slow speed flaps up on YF501+).
Hook: "PLI = shaker attitude."
x.Q0721:
Digital RA only (no dial): from 2,500 down to 1,000 ft AGL. Below 1,000 ft the round dial appears.
Hook: "2500 digits; 1000 dial."
x.Q0722:
RA is shown below 2,500 ft (digital); the round dial depicting height above ground appears below 1,000 ft RA — that's the intended answer.
Hook: "2500 digits; 1000 dial."
x.Q0723:
Current Mach appears under the speed tape at M0.40 and above; blanks below M0.40 (on some aircraft groundspeed shows instead). M.615 is the Mach trim threshold — don't mix them.
Hook: "Mach shows from .40."
x.Q0724:
Below RADIO minimums: the remaining dial perimeter and pointer turn AMBER and FLASH for 3 SECONDS; the numeric readout does NOT flash.
Hook: "Amber, 3 seconds, dial only."
x.Q0726:
Position trend vector (dashed, MAP modes): predicts position at 30, 60 and 90 s; each segment = 30 s; based on bank angle and groundspeed. With range > 20 NM, 3 segments → second line = 60 s.
Hook: "Each dash = 30 seconds."
x.Q0752:
ADIRS = air data (altitude, airspeed, temperature, V/S) + inertial (attitude, heading, position, groundspeed, track) → position, attitude, altitude and speed for displays, FMCs, flight controls, engines. Components: 2 ADIRUs, 4 ADMs, ISDU, MSU; sensors: 3 pitots, 6 static ports, 2 alpha vanes, 1 TAT probe.
Hook: "ADIRS = everything about where and how you fly."
x.Q0754:
Position trend vector: 30, 60 and 90 s intervals (3 segments with range > 20 NM).
Hook: "Each dash = 30 seconds."
x.Q0796:
Both GPS failed → amber GPS light (and GPS L/R INVALID). The EGPWS look-ahead terrain uses GPS position; with position uncertainty it shows TERR POS (amber) on the ND — terrain display/alerting unavailable. (The link is logical, the FCOM doesn't state it in one place.)
Hook: "No GPS → TERR POS."
x.Q0818:
ANP bars (on the NPS deviation scales) grow inward from the outer edge as ANP increases relative to RNP; they TOUCH AT THE CENTRE when ANP = RNP; they turn AMBER if the deviation pointer is within the ANP bars for 5 continuous seconds.
Hook: "Bars meet = ANP equals RNP."
x.Q1033:
ALT DISAGREE = Captain and F/O altitudes differ by more than 200 FT for more than 5 SECONDS.
Hook: "IAS 5/5, ALT 200/5, AOA 10/10."
x.Q1034:
Amber ROLL (or PITCH) on the PFD = attitude COMPARATOR: Captain's and F/O's roll (pitch) displays differ by MORE THAN 5°. Flashes 10 s then steady. It says nothing about which side is wrong — cross-check with the standby (ISFD).
Hook: "PITCH/ROLL amber = the two attitudes disagree by 5°."
x.Q1046:
Amber ROLL = Captain and F/O roll displays differ by more than 5° (comparator). Use the ISFD to find the bad one.
Hook: "PITCH/ROLL amber = 5° disagreement."
x.Q1051:
Amber PITCH = Captain and F/O pitch displays differ by more than 5°.
Hook: "PITCH/ROLL amber = 5° disagreement."
x.Q1064:
Below RA minimums: dial perimeter + pointer turn AMBER and FLASH 3 s; the numbers don't flash.
Hook: "Amber, 3 seconds, dial only."
x.Q1077:
Amber flashing RA dial for 3 s = descended below the SELECTED RADIO minimums (DH).
Hook: "Amber, 3 seconds = minimums."
x.Q1079:
RVSM limits: on the ground the max Capt–F/O altitude difference depends on field elevation — at SEA LEVEL it is 50 FT (table in L.10.3, larger at higher fields). In flight the max Capt–F/O difference is 200 ft. Standby altimeter is NOT RVSM-accurate.
Hook: "RVSM: 50 ft on the ground at sea level, 200 ft in the air."
x.Q1092:
The TRAFFIC message (amber TA / red RA) shows on the ND in ALL modes during a TA or RA, even if TFC isn't selected. The traffic SYMBOLS themselves need TFC (or the auto pop-up in MAP/VOR/APP).
Hook: "TRAFFIC text appears everywhere."
x.Q1118:
Reaching the PLI = STICK SHAKER for current conditions (both from the SMYD computers). No 'stick nudger' on the 737.
Hook: "PLI = shaker attitude."
x.Q0487:
ISDU DSPL SEL HDG/STS: left window = TRUE HEADING; right window = maintenance status codes, and DURING ALIGNMENT the MINUTES REMAINING (shows 15 until 14 remain, then counts down). Other positions: TK/GS (track, groundspeed), PPOS (lat/long), WIND (true wind dir/speed in flight).
Hook: "HDG/STS: heading left, minutes-to-go right."
x.Q0499:
Assumed temperature (SEL TEMP) reduced thrust: max reduction 25% below any certified rating (the FMC limits N1 accordingly). Not allowed with slush/snow/ice or possible windshear (and per limitations, not with anti-skid inop).
Hook: "Assumed temp: max 25% off."
x.Q0547:
ENG OUT CLB / ENG OUT CRZ pages are ADVISORY only (max altitude, con N1, speed). Once selected they CANNOT BE EXECUTED; VNAV is not changed by them.
Hook: "ENG OUT pages: read, don't execute."
x.Q0727:
True. Present position is normally entered on the FMC CDU (POS INIT → SET IRS POS). Backup: the ISDU keyboard on the aft overhead panel. Airplane must stay still during alignment.
Hook: "CDU first, ISDU keyboard backup."
x.Q0728:
IRS alignment lost in flight → NAV mode (position, groundspeed) dead for the rest of the flight. Select ATT: after ~30 s of straight, level, unaccelerated flight it relevels and gives ATTITUDE (and heading once you enter magnetic heading on POS INIT). ALIGN can't be used in flight.
Hook: "Lost NAV in flight → ATT, fly level 30 s, enter heading."
x.Q0729:
The DEP/ARR INDEX has ARR prompts for RTE 1 and RTE 2 (destination, and origin for a turn-back), so arrivals can be set up for each route — the bank says True. Within one route you select one arrival/approach.
Hook: "Two routes → two arrivals."
x.Q0730:
ADF mode selector: ADF → audio + bearing to DUs and standby RMI; ANT → AUDIO OPTIMIZED, NO BEARING; TONE → BFO for keyed stations; OFF.
Hook: "ANT = listen only, no needle."
x.Q0731:
False. Beyond 99 numbered (created) waypoints the FMC uses the first two characters + a 3-digit number from 100 (e.g. SEA104/74 → SE100).
Hook: "After 99: two letters + 100."
x.Q0732:
Changing the active NAV DATA (only possible on the GROUND) ERASES all previously entered route data → RTE page blank, re-enter the route. If the database expires in flight, it keeps being used until changed after landing.
Hook: "New database = blank route."
x.Q0733:
IntuVue PWS: detection works automatically below 1,800 ft AGL, but ALERTS are available at 1,200 FT and below (same 1,200 ft as the older radar). Warning gives 10–60 s.
Hook: "Detect from 1800, alert from 1200."
x.Q0734:
OVERSPEED DISCONNECT (VNAV PATH descent): airspeed exceeds the FMC speed restriction by MORE THAN 15 KT → VNAV disengages. Action: reduce speed manually (speedbrakes) and re-engage VNAV.
Hook: "15 kt over the restriction → VNAV quits."
x.Q0735:
Two navigation databases, each valid 28 DAYS (AIRAC cycle). You select the active one on the IDENT page.
Hook: "AIRAC = 28 days."
x.Q0736:
False. DC FAIL (amber) = the IRS's DC (backup) power is not normal; if no other lights, the IRS is running NORMALLY on AC. Alignment is lost only if the IRS loses BOTH AC and DC (or the MSU switch leaves NAV).
Hook: "DC FAIL = backup gone, IRS fine on AC."
x.Q0737:
IRS position is set on the POS INIT page (INIT REF → POS), line SET IRS POS. If not entered before initial alignment ends → ENTER IRS POS scratchpad message.
Hook: "POS INIT → SET IRS POS."
x.Q0739:
Marker beacons appear at the UPPER RIGHT of the attitude display: OM = CYAN, MM = AMBER, IM = WHITE.
Hook: "Outer cyan, Middle amber, Inner white."
x.Q0740:
Route colours on the ND: inactive = cyan dashed; ACTIVATED (R6) but not executed = CYAN DASHED; active (executed) = MAGENTA solid; modification to active = WHITE dashed.
Hook: "Cyan = not yet; magenta = flying it; white dashed = mod."
x.Q0741:
Fuel on PERF INIT comes AUTOMATICALLY from the fuel quantity indicating system — you don't type it. Manual entry is only used when the data is invalid (VERIFY GW AND FUEL, FUEL line dashes).
Hook: "Fuel on PERF INIT is automatic."
x.Q0742:
FQIS failure → VERIFY GW AND FUEL, PERF INIT fuel dashes; FMC uses last valid fuel. Crew must ENTER estimated fuel and UPDATE it periodically (reminder every 30 min) to keep gross weight and VNAV performance correct. VNAV doesn't disengage.
Hook: "FQIS dead → you are the fuel gauge, every 30 min."
x.Q0743:
IntuVue windshear mode auto-activates: IN THE AIR below 1,800 ft AGL, or ON THE GROUND with thrust levers at takeoff setting. (Alerts: 1,200 ft and below.)
Hook: "1800 air, takeoff thrust ground."
x.Q0744:
⚠️ NOT IN THE FCOM – airmanship/bank answer. Turbulence associated with a storm can extend well beyond the visible echo — standard airmanship: avoid cells by at least 20 NM (more downwind / at altitude). The FCOM only says turbulence (magenta, needs precipitation) is detected within 40 NM; clear-air turbulence isn't detected.
Hook: "Give storms 20 NM or more."
x.Q0745:
True. In-flight loss of alignment = no NAV mode for the rest of the flight (ATT mode only).
Hook: "Lost NAV in flight stays lost."
x.Q0746:
FMC position = combination of IRS, radio and GPS. If the GPS update is excessive (too far from the others), GPS UPDATING IS SUSPENDED until the GPS position looks reasonable again — not removed permanently, not averaged.
Hook: "Crazy GPS is paused, not deleted."
x.Q0747:
Manual IRS entries (present position, or magnetic heading in ATT mode) are normally made on the FMC POS INIT page; the ISDU keyboard is the alternative. POS SHIFT 3/3 is for FMC position shift in flight, not IRS entries.
Hook: "IRS inputs: POS INIT (or ISDU)."
x.Q0748:
VHF NAV transfer switch (BOTH ON 1 / NORMAL / BOTH ON 2) chooses which Multimode Receiver feeds the NDs. It transfers DME, ILS (ILS/GLS on YW130–YW164), VOR and MCP COURSE. Not autothrottle.
Hook: "VHF NAV = DME, ILS/GLS, VOR, course."
x.Q0749:
FIX INFO page RAD/DIS FR = radial and distance FROM THE FIX TO THE AIRPLANE, continually UPDATED. Lines 2L–4L let you draw radials/distances from the fix on the ND.
Hook: "FR = from the fix to you, live."
x.Q0750:
On the ground, FMC position = GPS (if not available, IRS). In flight it blends IRS + GPS + radio.
Hook: "On the ground, GPS first."
x.Q0751:
POS REF page 2/3 shows lat/long for FMC, IRS L/R, GPS L/R and radio, plus GROUND SPEED for the FMC and each IRS (the classic answer for 'where is groundspeed on the CDU').
Hook: "POS REF 2/3 = positions + GS."
x.Q0755:
DRAG REQUIRED: airspeed 10 KT or more ABOVE FMC target, OR within 5 KT of Vmo/Mmo. Action: speedbrakes / reduce thrust to get within 5 kt of target.
Hook: "+10 or Vmo−5 → DRAG REQUIRED."
x.Q0756:
BUFFET ALERT (flaps up only): current conditions give a MANEUVER MARGIN LESS THAN SPECIFIED (normally 1.3 g to buffet). Get back into the envelope (speed/altitude).
Hook: "BUFFET ALERT = not enough g margin."
x.Q0757:
INSUFFICIENT FUEL: predicted fuel at destination < 2,000 lb / 900 KG (FMC alert light too). Compare USING RSV FUEL: predicted below the RESERVES entered on PERF INIT.
Hook: "<900 kg = INSUFFICIENT; <reserves = USING RSV."
x.Q0758:
RESET MCP ALT: in cruise with VNAV, within 5 NM of TOP OF DESCENT and the MCP altitude hasn't been lowered — VNAV won't descend through the MCP altitude.
Hook: "5 NM to T/D, set a lower MCP altitude."
x.Q0759:
IntuVue (RDR-4000): automatic multi-scan, ground clutter removed → clutter-free weather out to 320 NM; no tilt/gain needed in auto.
Hook: "IntuVue sees 320."
x.Q0760:
VERIFY GW AND FUEL = fuel quantity data INVALID → enter fuel manually on PERF INIT and update it (reminder every 30 min). VNAV does NOT disengage.
Hook: "FQIS dead → you are the fuel gauge."
x.Q0761:
Supplemental (kept until deleted) + temporary (erased at flight completion) databases share 40 NAVAIDS and 6 AIRPORTS; waypoints: 20 reserved in temporary + 20 more in either (max 40).
Hook: "40 navaids, 6 airports."
x.Q0762:
GPS displays: POS REF 2/3 → L and R GPS LAT/LONG; POS SHIFT 3/3 → GPS position RELATIVE to FMC (bearing/distance); NAV STATUS 1/2 → GPS in use.
Hook: "REF = lat/long; SHIFT = relative."
x.Q0763:
POS SHIFT 3/3 = each system's position (GPS, IRS, radio) RELATIVE to the FMC position (bearing/distance), also used to shift FMC position in flight.
Hook: "REF = lat/long; SHIFT = relative."
x.Q0764:
FMC databases: PERFORMANCE (drag, engines, max/opt altitudes, speeds — so you don't need the performance manual in flight) and NAVIGATION (two 28-day sets).
Hook: "FMC = Perf + Nav."
x.Q0765:
LNAV engagement: within 3 NM of the active leg → ANY heading. Outside 3 NM → must be on an intercept of 90° or less that intercepts BEFORE the active waypoint. Otherwise NOT ON INTERCEPT HEADING.
Hook: "3 NM: any heading; beyond: intercept before the waypoint."
x.Q0766:
FMS = FMCS + AFDS + A/T + IRS + GPS (five independent systems working together). MCP/EFIS/ADIRS are not on the list.
Hook: "FMS = FMC, AFDS, A/T, IRS, GPS."
x.Q0767:
LRC = LONG RANGE CRUISE. Cruise modes: ECON (cost index), LRC, manual speed. CI 0 = max range cruise.
Hook: "LRC = Long Range Cruise."
x.Q0768:
Weather radar normal sweep = 180° forward. With PWS enabled on the ground / below 2,300 ft RA it narrows to 120°.
Hook: "180 normally, 120 for windshear."
x.Q0769:
IRS in ATT: ATTITUDE, and HEADING once you enter the initial magnetic heading (it drifts up to 15°/h — cross-check with the compass and update). No position or groundspeed.
Hook: "ATT = attitude + heading (if you give it one)."
x.Q0770:
In VNAV PATH descent the A/T is at idle and pitch holds the path. An unexpected TAILWIND makes speed rise to stay on path → DRAG REQUIRED (use speedbrakes). If a limit speed would be exceeded, VNAV reverts to VNAV SPD.
Hook: "Tailwind on the path → DRAG REQUIRED."
x.Q0771:
FMC preflight REQUIRED: initial position, performance data, route, takeoff data. OPTIONAL: navigation database, RTA data, SID, cruise wind. (Order: IDENT → POS INIT → RTE → PERF INIT → N1 LIMIT → TAKEOFF REF.)
Hook: "Required: Position, Perf, Route, Takeoff."
x.Q0772:
ENG OUT CRZ is INFORMATION ONLY — no EXEC light. You fly the driftdown yourself: A/T off, MCT on the live engine, MCP speed = ENG OUT SPD, MCP altitude = MAX ALT (or lower), LVL CHG.
Hook: "ENG OUT pages: read, don't execute."
x.Q0774:
⚠️ The FCOM doesn't state this sentence – bank answer (it follows from how SET IRS POS works: it's only needed while the IRS is aligning). SET IRS POS box prompts only show while an IRS is in ALIGN waiting for position. Once both IRSs reach NAV the line BLANKS — completely normal.
Hook: "SET IRS POS gone = alignment done."
x.Q0775:
DEP/ARR INDEX: origin has DEP and ARR prompts (ARR for a turn-back), destination has ARR only → arrivals available for BOTH origin and destination, no distance restriction.
Hook: "Origin can have an arrival — for turn-backs."
x.Q0776:
VERIFY POSITION = FMC position sources are CONTRADICTORY (IRS vs radio vs GPS). Do the FMC Navigation Check supplementary procedure.
Hook: "VERIFY POSITION = sources disagree."
x.Q0777:
ATT selected by mistake on the ground: IRS selectors OFF → wait for ALIGN lights to EXTINGUISH (IRS stays powered ~30 s) → do a FULL alignment (to NAV).
Hook: "Wrong ATT → OFF, wait, full align."
x.Q0778:
Preliminary cockpit prep: IRS MODE SELECTORS → NAV directly (passes through ALIGN automatically). Airplane parked, not moved until ALIGN lights go out. ON DC momentarily then ALIGN steady. RYR: full alignment only on the first flight of the duty period.
Hook: "Straight to NAV, don't move."
x.Q0779:
If LNAV can't capture, the CDU shows NOT ON INTERCEPT HEADING. Turn to a proper intercept heading (≤90°, intercept before the active waypoint) and re-engage LNAV.
Hook: "Bad intercept → NOT ON INTERCEPT HEADING."
x.Q0780:
FAST REALIGNMENT: select ALIGN while parked → 30 SECONDS, zeroes groundspeed error; enter present position before going back to NAV. Moving the airplane restarts a full alignment. Full alignment: 5–17 min depending on latitude.
Hook: "Fast align = 30 s in ALIGN."
x.Q0781:
TWO ILS receivers (inside the Multimode Receivers), tuned MANUALLY on the VHF NAV control panels. LOC updating of the FMC only after manual tuning. ILS can also be shown on the ISFD.
Hook: "Two ILS, tuned by hand."
x.Q0783:
APPROACH REF GROSS WT: normally FMC weight; BOX PROMPTS when the FMC has no gross weight → you must enter it to get VREFs. Manual entry is overwritten if you leave and return.
Hook: "Boxes = FMC needs your input."
x.Q0784:
FMC power loss > 10 s in flight: LNAV and VNAV disengage, but ALL DATA IS RETAINED. On restoration: RTE LEGS with SELECT ACTIVE WPT/LEG → select the active waypoint (direct/intercept) and re-engage the A/T, roll and pitch modes. (On the ground ≥10 s: redo the whole preflight.)
Hook: "Data kept, modes dropped — tell it where to go."
x.Q0785:
IRS lights: ALIGN (white, steady = aligning / flashing = position problem), ON DC (amber, on battery), DC FAIL (amber, DC backup not normal), FAULT (amber) = system fault affecting ATT and/or NAV modes.
Hook: "FAULT = the IRS itself is sick."
x.Q0786:
FQIS failure in VNAV: VERIFY GW AND FUEL → enter estimated fuel and update it periodically (reminder every 30 min). VNAV keeps working on the last valid value.
Hook: "FQIS dead → you are the fuel gauge."
x.Q0787:
Windshear event while the ND shows terrain (or other non-weather data) → the display AUTOMATICALLY SWITCHES TO WEATHER mode to show the windshear icon.
Hook: "Windshear grabs the screen."
x.Q0788:
IRS backup DC (ON DC light) = SWITCHED HOT BATTERY bus (right IRS cut after 5 min).
Hook: "Switched hot = IRS backup."
x.Q0791:
MAX RATE and MAX ANGLE climb speeds are selected on the CLB page (VNAV key). MAX ANGLE = most altitude per DISTANCE (obstacles); MAX RATE = most altitude per TIME.
Hook: "Angle = distance, rate = time — both on CLB."
x.Q0792:
RYR NPA with VNAV: if you set the missed approach altitude in the MCP when you are within ~300 ft of it, the AFDS may capture it → inadvertent ALT ACQ (levels off). Hence set the MAA 300 ft above MDA/DA (or once 300 ft below the MAA).
Hook: "Too close to the MAA → ALT ACQ."
x.Q0793:
IRS on DC: ON DC light + on the ground the GROUND-CALL HORN in the nose wheel well sounds (warns maintenance the battery is draining).
Hook: "IRS on battery → horn in the nose well."
x.Q0795:
Left IRS ← AC STANDBY bus; right IRS ← AC TRANSFER BUS 2; both backup from the switched hot battery bus.
Hook: "Left = standby; Right = transfer 2."
x.Q0797:
Turbulence mode: precipitation moving horizontally ≥ 5 m/s toward/away from the antenna → MAGENTA (heavy turbulence), limited to 40 NM. Needs precipitation (no clear-air turbulence).
Hook: "5 m/s → magenta."
x.Q0798:
WX/TURB: weather returns + TURBULENCE within 40 NM (requires precipitation). Windshear is a separate PWS function.
Hook: "Turbulence only within 40."
x.Q0799:
YW059–YW164: default VRNP = 400 FT (oceanic, en route, terminal). Can be changed on RNP PROGRESS 4/4.
Hook: "VRNP 400."
x.Q0800:
FIX INFO: enter a fix and radials/distances; the intersection with the active route can be COPIED into the route as a new waypoint (LEGS page). Also draws the radial/circle on the ND.
Hook: "FIX page → new waypoint where the radial crosses your route."
x.Q0801:
PREDICTIVE windshear (PWS, looks ahead) comes from the WEATHER RADAR. REACTIVE windshear (you're in it) comes from the EGPWS. Don't mix them.
Hook: "Predictive = radar; reactive = GPWS."
x.Q0802:
True. Turbulence detection is limited to 40 NM regardless of the selected ND range.
Hook: "Turbulence only within 40."
x.Q0803:
True. FCOM 11.10.34, weather radar panel, item 3 TILT Control: 'Rotate clockwise – radar antenna tilts up to selected degrees above horizon. Rotate counterclockwise – radar antenna tilts down to selected degrees below horizon.'
Hook: "TILT knob: up above, down below the horizon."
x.Q0804:
IntuVue MAN mode: ALT knob selects the weather analysis altitude slice from 0 to 60,000 ft MSL in 1,000 FT steps (defaults to current altitude). Turbulence removed in MAN.
Hook: "MAN slice: 0–60,000 by 1,000."
x.Q0805:
Max flight operating latitude: 82° N / 82° S (limited by the ADIRU magnetic variation tables), with regional exceptions (73° N between 80° W–170° W, 60° S between 120° E–160° E on newer aircraft). Normal IRS alignment only up to 78°15'.
Hook: "82 north, 82 south."
x.Q0807:
FCOM 11.10.20 (YW130–YW164 IRS panel, aft overhead): the IRS mode selector goes OFF → ALIGN → NAV → ATT clockwise. Look at the diagram: OFF at the bottom left, then ALIGN, NAV at the top right, ATT at the bottom right.
Hook: "OFF – ALIGN – NAV – ATT."
x.Q0809:
VHF NAV transfer switch transfers DME, ILS (ILS/GLS on YW130+), VOR and MCP COURSE to the NDs. Bank answer for the general fleet: DME, ILS, VOR, MCP course.
Hook: "VHF NAV = DME, ILS, VOR, course."
x.Q0810:
TAKEOFF SPEEDS DELETED (V speeds removed, NO VSPD returns): runway/thrust/performance data changed after V speeds were selected, OR after FIRST ENGINE START the entered OAT differs from sensed OAT by ±6 °C. Fix: correct OAT on N1 LIMIT and reselect V speeds.
Hook: "OAT off by 6 after start → V speeds gone."
x.Q0811:
Weather radar turbulence detection: 40 NM.
Hook: "Turbulence only within 40."
x.Q0812:
ALIGN flashing = alignment can't complete: entered position very different from the last position / unreasonable, or NO position entered. Re-enter the correct position (two failed identical entries → FAULT).
Hook: "Flashing ALIGN = check your position entry."
x.Q0813:
IRS FAULT (amber) = system fault affecting ATT and/or NAV modes. DC problems have their own lights (DC FAIL, ON DC).
Hook: "FAULT = the IRS itself is sick."
x.Q0814:
GPS light (amber): steady = BOTH GPS failed; only on MASTER CAUTION RECALL (goes out on reset) = SINGLE GPS sensor failed.
Hook: "Recall-only light = one of two failed."
x.Q0817:
APPROACH REF GROSS WT shows BOX PROMPTS when the FMC has no gross weight.
Hook: "Boxes = FMC needs your input."
x.Q0819:
Single FMC failure (left here): FMC alert light, FAIL light on that CDU, LNAV/VNAV disengage, VTK (amber) on that side's ND, later failure info; restore with FMC source select BOTH ON R. The FCOM describes the right-FMC case; left is the mirror. IRS/ADIRU loss would give ATT/HDG flags instead.
Hook: "FAIL on CDU + VTK = that FMC died."
x.Q0820:
Storm avoidance (airmanship/FCTM, not in FCOM): keep at least 20 NM from each cell, so when flying BETWEEN two cells you need at least 40 NM between them. Turbulence/hail extend beyond the echo.
Hook: "20 from each = 40 between."
x.Q0821:
VERIFY GW AND FUEL = fuel quantity data INVALID → enter estimated fuel manually and keep updating it. Don't confuse with CHECK FMC FUEL QUANTITY (unexpected DROP in fuel, i.e. possible leak). VNAV doesn't disengage.
Hook: "VERIFY = data bad; CHECK = fuel disappearing."
x.Q0822:
VERIFY POSITION (exact wording) is the ON-GROUND message: position information contradictory (e.g. entered position not within 4 NM of origin). Check entries, crosscheck IRS/GPS/FMC, realign if needed. In flight the messages are VERIFY POS: IRS-RADIO etc.
Hook: "VERIFY POSITION = ground check of your entry."
x.Q0823:
GPS lat/long: POS REF page 2/3 (relative position on POS SHIFT 3/3).
Hook: "REF = lat/long; SHIFT = relative."
x.Q0824:
Single FMC failure (mirror the FCOM's right-FMC text for the left): FMC alert (P/RST) light, FAIL light on that CDU, SINGLE FMC OPERATION message, VTK on that ND, LNAV/VNAV disengage (if that side's A/P is in use), failure info on that ND after 25–30 s. Restore with FMC source select BOTH ON (good side). The A/P P/RST light isn't involved.
Hook: "FMC dies: alert light, CDU FAIL, VTK, ND fails after ~30 s."
x.Q0826:
PROGRESS page 1 FUEL QTY = present TOTAL fuel REMAINING from the fuel quantity indicating system (not fuel used, not a single tank).
Hook: "PROG fuel = what's in the tanks now."
x.Q0828:
Database expiring in flight: nothing happens — the expired one keeps being used until you change the active date AFTER LANDING (changing it erases the route).
Hook: "Expires in flight? Keep flying, change on the ground."
x.Q0829:
Arrivals can be selected for BOTH origin (turn-back) and destination; no distance limits.
Hook: "Origin can have an arrival — for turn-backs."
x.Q0830:
VNAV SPD climb (pitch holds speed, A/T N1). Reaching an FMC 'at' altitude constraint, VNAV levels off and the pitch FMA changes to VNAV PTH (holding the constrained altitude). If it levels at the MCP altitude instead → ALT HOLD.
Hook: "FMC level-off = VNAV PTH; MCP level-off = ALT HOLD."
x.Q0857:
PROGRESS page fuel = total fuel on board from the FQIS.
Hook: "PROG fuel = what's in the tanks now."
x.Q1050:
FCOM 11.31.28: 'The E/D will be RWXXX or MAXXX, and the E/D altitude will be either threshold crossing height (TCH – typically 50 ft above the touchdown zone) or the altitude specified at MAXXX.' So the E/D altitude is the ALTITUDE RESTRICTION of the end-of-descent waypoint – not simply the field elevation, airport reference point or threshold elevation.
Hook: "E/D altitude = the E/D waypoint's restriction."
x.Q1108:
Shortest DISTANCE → MAX ANGLE on the CLB page (shortest TIME → MAX RATE).
Hook: "Angle = distance, rate = time — both on CLB."
x.Q0831:
Fuel balance limit: lateral imbalance scheduled to be ZERO; random imbalance max 453 KG (1,000 lb) for taxi, takeoff, flight AND landing. Same number: mains must be full if center > 453 kg; IMBAL alert at > 453 kg.
Hook: "453 kg everywhere."
x.Q0832:
Fuel measuring sticks (magnetic dipsticks under the wing): 6 in EACH main tank + 4 in the center = 16.
Hook: "6 + 6 + 4 = 16."
x.Q0833:
Imbalance (QRH FUEL IMBALANCE): CROSSFEED OPEN, fuel pumps of the LOW tank OFF → both engines feed from the HIGH tank until balanced, then pumps ON and crossfeed CLOSED. Fuel isn't transferred between tanks — it's burned from the heavy side. There's no IMBAL 'warning light' (it's a DU alert).
Hook: "Open crossfeed, switch off the light side."
x.Q0834:
Nitrogen Generation System indicator (right main wheel well): GREEN = fully operational; BLUE = DEGRADED (works, but reduced); AMBER = inoperative (no lights = inoperative too).
Hook: "Green good, blue degraded, amber dead."
x.Q0835:
Valve position lights on the fuel panel: ENG VALVE CLOSED (engine fuel shutoff), SPAR VALVE CLOSED, crossfeed VALVE OPEN (all blue: dim = position, bright = transit/disagree). Pumps have only LOW PRESSURE lights — no pump 'valves'.
Hook: "Engine valve, spar valve, crossfeed — the three blue lights."
x.Q0836:
Center pump auto-shutoff (after low output pressure): cycling the pump switch OFF → ON RESETS the logic and the pump runs again (until OFF or shut off again).
Hook: "Off-on resets the center pump."
x.Q0837:
No CDS alert: CONFIG needs > 726 kg in the center AND both center switches OFF (here 320 kg and switches ON); LOW is for main tanks < 453 kg; IMBAL needs a main-tank difference. You only get the LOW PRESSURE lights (+ MASTER CAUTION/FUEL after 10 s continuous).
