Hook: "CONFIG = >726 kg with switches OFF."
x.Q0838:
Each tank has TWO AC pumps (6 total), cooled/lubricated by fuel. A center tank SCAVENGE JET PUMP moves remaining center fuel into MAIN TANK 1 (starts when tank 1 is about half; needs No 1 FWD pump ON). Pump mounting locations (center pumps on the rear spar, main pumps fwd/aft) are bank details, not in the FCOM.
Hook: "2 pumps each + a jet pump to tank 1."
x.Q0839:
Both pumps of a main tank lost → that engine SUCTION FEEDS from its own main tank through a line bypassing the pumps. At high altitude dissolved air may restrict flow → thrust loss or flameout (until the air depletes). Crossfeed is a crew action, not automatic.
Hook: "No pumps → suction feed (careful high up)."
x.Q0841:
False. IMBAL (amber) shows ON THE GROUND OR IN THE AIR when mains differ by > 453 kg; stays until reduced to 91 kg; shown under the LOWER tank; inhibited by LOW.
Hook: "IMBAL: >453 on, <91 off, ground or air."
x.Q0842:
Crossfeed VALVE OPEN light: OUT = closed; DIM blue = open; BRIGHT blue = in TRANSIT or valve DISAGREES with the selector (e.g. selected open but still closed).
Hook: "Bright blue = moving or disagree."
x.Q0843:
Engine fuel shutoff valves: fuel-actuated, solenoid-controlled, powered by the BATTERY BUS. Spar valves: DC motor from the HOT battery bus. Crossfeed: DC motor from the battery bus.
Hook: "Spar = hot bus; engine valve & crossfeed = battery bus."
x.Q0844:
FUEL TEMP sensor: in MAIN TANK No 1 (AC powered), shown on the fuel panel.
Hook: "Fuel temp lives in tank 1."
x.Q0845:
False. Center tank LOW PRESSURE light must be ON CONTINUOUSLY for 10 SECONDS before MASTER CAUTION + FUEL (flickering at low quantity can go on up to 5 min).
Hook: "Center LOW PRESSURE: 10 s before the master caution."
x.Q0846:
False. FCOM 12.10.5 CONFIG alert: either engine running + center tank > 726 kg + both center pump switches OFF → 'The quantity arc and digits on the CENTER tank fuel quantity indicator turn amber.' It's the center gauge, not No 1 and No 2.
Hook: "CONFIG lights the CENTER gauge."
x.Q0847:
3060 − 2500 = 560 kg > 453 → amber IMBAL under the LOWER tank (No 1) and its digits (arc on older displays) turn amber. No MASTER CAUTION for IMBAL. LOW would need < 453 kg in a main tank.
Hook: "IMBAL sits under the light tank."
x.Q0848:
Center fuel is used first because the CENTER PUMPS produce HIGHER PRESSURE than the main pumps — with all pumps on, center pressure wins at the manifold.
Hook: "Center pumps push harder."
x.Q0849:
Start lever to IDLE opens the spar valve: SPAR VALVE CLOSED goes DIM (closed) → BRIGHT (in transit) → OUT (open). At shutdown (CUTOFF) the reverse: out → bright → dim.
Hook: "Opening: dim → bright → out."
x.Q0851:
760 kg > 726 kg with both center pumps OFF (engines running) → amber CONFIG under the CENTER tank gauge. Reminder to switch the center pumps on.
Hook: "CONFIG lives under the center gauge."
x.Q0852:
All generators lost → no AC → fuel pumps stop → engines SUCTION FEED. As altitude increases, dissolved air comes out of the fuel and collects in the suction line, restricting flow → thrust deterioration or flameout at high altitude (improves once the air depletes / descending).
Hook: "No pumps + altitude = air in the suction line."
x.Q0853:
Bypass valves (suction feed around the pumps) are in BOTH MAIN TANKS — that's how engines suction-feed from their own main tank. The center tank has none (center fuel needs its pumps). Also used for suction defueling.
Hook: "Mains can suck, center can't."
x.Q0854:
IMBAL: appears at > 453 kg, disappears at 91 kg.
Hook: "IMBAL: >453 on, <91 off."
x.Q0856:
Engine fuel shutoff valve and spar valve BOTH close with start lever CUTOFF or fire switch pulled. Both DC powered (spar: hot battery bus; engine: battery bus), both have blue CLOSED lights.
Hook: "CUTOFF or fire switch → both valves shut."
x.Q0858:
Main tank pump LOW PRESSURE light = pump OUTPUT pressure low (or switch OFF). Two lights in the same main tank → MASTER CAUTION + FUEL.
Hook: "LOW PRESSURE = the pump's output."
x.Q0859:
Scavenge jet pump: moves the LAST remaining center fuel into MAIN TANK 1 (left), once tank 1 is about half; needs No 1 FWD pump ON; continues rest of flight.
Hook: "Leftover center fuel → tank 1."
x.Q0860:
Spar valve: DC MOTOR from the HOT BATTERY bus (works even with battery switch OFF, like the fire bottles).
Hook: "Spar = hot bus."
x.Q0861:
CUTOFF closes BOTH the spar and the engine fuel shutoff valves (no bypass valve involved).
Hook: "CUTOFF → both valves shut."
x.Q0862:
IMBAL stays until the imbalance is down to 91 kg. Appears at > 453 kg. Correction: crossfeed open, pumps OFF on the LOW side (not the high one).
Hook: "IMBAL: >453 on, <91 off."
x.Q0863:
All tanks full, all pumps ON → BOTH engines fed from the CENTER tank (higher pressure pumps) until near empty, then each engine from its own main tank. Check valves prevent fuel transferring between tanks.
Hook: "Center first, then own wing."
x.Q0864:
Center tank fuel is used first (higher-pressure center pumps).
Hook: "Center pumps push harder."
x.Q0865:
No CDS alert: CONFIG requires switches OFF and > 726 kg; LOW is for main tanks. With failed center pumps (switches ON) you get LOW PRESSURE lights + MASTER CAUTION/FUEL, nothing on the DU.
Hook: "CONFIG = >726 kg with switches OFF."
x.Q0866:
No CDS indication, but MASTER CAUTION + FUEL (after 10 s continuous LOW PRESSURE with switches ON). Remember the limitation: don't dry-run center pumps → switch them OFF.
Hook: "Center LOW PRESSURE: 10 s → master caution; nothing on the DU."
x.Q0867:
No CDS indication; MASTER CAUTION illuminates (after 10 s).
Hook: "Center LOW PRESSURE: master caution, nothing on the DU."
x.Q0868:
Crossfeed left OPEN with all main pumps on: the side with slightly higher pump pressure feeds both engines → PROGRESSIVE IMBALANCE → IMBAL alert eventually. Normally keep crossfeed CLOSED.
Hook: "Crossfeed left open = imbalance."
x.Q0869:
Crossfeed closed: the LEFT center pump feeds the left manifold, the RIGHT center pump the right manifold. Left center pump fails → the left engine is fed by main tank 1 pumps, the right engine still by the center tank → imbalance develops (tank 1 drops). Fix: crossfeed open so the remaining center pump feeds both.
Hook: "Each center pump feeds its own side."
x.Q0870:
⚠️ The FCOM doesn't list a low fuel temperature alert – bank answer (the gauge only shows the temperature). There is NO caution/alert for low fuel temperature — the FUEL TEMP gauge (tank 1 sensor) just shows it and the crew monitors the limit (−43 °C or freezing point +3 °C, whichever higher).
Hook: "Fuel temp: you watch it, nothing warns you."
x.Q0871:
1500 kg > 726 kg with both center pumps OFF (engine running) → amber CONFIG.
Hook: "CONFIG = >726 kg with switches OFF."
x.Q0873:
Minimum fuel tank temp (before takeoff and in flight): −43 °C OR freezing point + 3 °C, WHICHEVER IS HIGHER. FSII doesn't change it. Max: 49 °C.
Hook: "Min −43 or FP+3 (higher); max 49."
x.Q0874:
Shutdown (CUTOFF): SPAR VALVE CLOSED goes OUT (open) → BRIGHT (transit) → DIM (closed). Start is the reverse.
Hook: "Closing: out → bright → dim."
x.Q0875:
Usable fuel (at 0.8029 kg/l): Main tanks 1 and 2: 4,876 l / 3,915 KG each; Center: 16,273 l / 13,066 KG; Total: 26,025 l / ≈20,896 kg.
Hook: "3.9 – 13.1 – 3.9 (≈20.9 t)."
x.Q0876:
⚠️ NOT clearly in the FCOM – bank answer. FCOM: two AC pumps per tank (no 'boost pump' location given). Bank answer: the pumps are physically in the CENTER TANK area (main tank pumps mounted in the center section). Know it as the bank answer.
Hook: "Bank: pumps sit in the center tank."
x.Q0877:
CONFIG appears at > 726 kg (switches OFF, engine running) and remains until: both engines stopped, center < 363 KG, or one center pump switch ON.
Hook: "CONFIG: on above 726, off below 363."
x.Q0878:
⚠️ Operational practice / bank answer – not stated as a limitation in the FCOM. Crossfeed is normally CLOSED (each engine on its own side) for takeoff and landing — open only to balance fuel or in non-normals. (Operational practice; not an FCOM limitation.)
Hook: "Crossfeed closed for takeoff and landing."
x.Q0879:
Mechanism: higher-pressure center pumps (FCOM). Reason (design): keep fuel in the WINGS as long as possible — its weight counters lift and RELIEVES WING ROOT BENDING.
Hook: "Fuel in the wings = less wing bending."
x.Q0880:
Maximum tank fuel temperature: 49 °C (AFM limitation). Minimum: −43 °C or FP+3 °C, whichever higher.
Hook: "Min −43, max 49."
x.Q0881:
Three CDS fuel alerts: LOW (main tank < 453 kg, until 567 kg), CONFIG (center > 726 kg with center pumps not supplying / switches OFF), IMBAL (mains differ > 453 kg). Filter bypass and pump LOW PRESSURE are panel lights, not CDS alerts; there's no fuel-flow-difference alert.
Hook: "DU fuel alerts: LOW, CONFIG, IMBAL."
x.Q0883:
False. Even during takeoff roll, a continuous center LOW PRESSURE light for 10 s brings MASTER CAUTION + FUEL.
Hook: "Center LOW PRESSURE: 10 s → master caution."
x.Q0885:
Scavenge: remaining center fuel → main tank 1, with the No 1 FWD pump ON and tank 1 at about half or less; continues for the rest of the flight.
Hook: "Leftover center fuel → tank 1 (FWD pump on, tank half)."
x.Q0886:
Start lever to IDLE: SPAR VALVE CLOSED DIM → BRIGHT → OUT.
Hook: "Opening: dim → bright → out."
x.Q0887:
Minimum tank fuel temp: −43 °C OR freezing point + 3 °C, WHICHEVER IS HIGHER (before takeoff and in flight). Max 49 °C.
Hook: "Min −43 or FP+3 (higher); max 49."
x.Q0888:
Fuel leak clues (QRH FUEL LEAK): an IMBAL alert, unusually high fuel flow on one engine, or TOTAL fuel noticeably less than planned (fuel used + remaining ≠ departure fuel), plus CHECK FMC FUEL QUANTITY. CONFIG/LOW PRESSURE are pump/config issues, not leak signs.
Hook: "Leak = numbers don't add up."
x.Q0889:
One center pump fails (crossfeed closed): its side's engine now feeds from its own MAIN tank while the other engine still uses center fuel → main tanks become unequal → IMBAL.
Hook: "Each center pump feeds its own side."
x.Q0890:
APU feeds from the LEFT manifold; with all pumps on and fuel in the center, center pumps dominate → APU burns CENTER tank fuel.
Hook: "All pumps on = center pumps push hardest."
x.Q0891:
Fuel LOW (amber): a MAIN tank below 453 KG; stays until 567 kg.
Hook: "LOW: <453 on, 567 off."
x.Q0892:
CONFIG: engine running + center > 726 KG + both center pumps OFF. Clears below 363 kg or with a center pump ON.
Hook: "CONFIG: on above 726, off below 363."
x.Q0893:
LOW has priority — IMBAL is INHIBITED when LOW is displayed (low fuel matters more than balance).
Hook: "LOW beats IMBAL."
x.Q0894:
560 kg difference → IMBAL under tank 1 (the lower) and its digits amber; no MASTER CAUTION.
Hook: "IMBAL sits under the light tank."
x.Q0895:
Selector closed + valve closed → VALVE OPEN light EXTINGUISHED. Dim = open, bright = transit/disagree.
Hook: "Dark = closed."
x.Q0897:
False. CONFIG requires BOTH center pump switches OFF; with them ON there's no CONFIG regardless of quantity.
Hook: "CONFIG = >726 kg with switches OFF."
x.Q0603:
MFD SYS on the -800 = HYDRAULIC QUANTITY and PRESSURE (A and B) only, on the lower DU (or inboard DU with INBD MFD). No doors, brakes or surface positions.
Hook: "SYS = hydraulics."
x.Q0899:
System A: ailerons, rudder, elevator & feel, flight spoilers 2-4-9-11, ALL ground spoilers, ALTERNATE brakes, No 1 reverser, A/P A, NORMAL nose wheel steering, LANDING GEAR, gear transfer valve, PTU. System B: TE flaps/LE devices, NORMAL brakes, ALTERNATE NWS, No 2 reverser, A/P B, yaw damper, autoslats, gear transfer backup.
Hook: "A = gear, steering, ground spoilers, PTU. B = flaps, brakes."
x.Q0900:
Standby AUTO-ON needs: loss of A OR B + FLAPS EXTENDED + (airborne or wheel speed > 60 kt) + that FLT CONTROL switch ON — OR the Force Fight Monitor trips. With flaps UP in cruise a single system loss does NOT start it (switch STBY RUD manually if needed).
Hook: "Auto standby = one system lost + flaps out + flying/fast."
x.Q0901:
One pump's LOW PRESSURE light = only THAT pump's output is low → MASTER CAUTION + HYD. System B pressure is still held by its engine pump, so no flight control LOW PRESSURE light and no pressure drop.
Hook: "One pump down ≠ system down."
x.Q0902:
Landing gear transfer valve (system B EDP raises the gear) ALL of: airborne, No 1 ENGINE RPM below a limit (not the EDP), gear lever UP, EITHER MAIN gear not up and locked. Typical case: engine 1 fails on takeoff.
Hook: "Engine 1 slow + gear up selected + main not locked → B raises the gear."
x.Q0903:
RF (white) next to hydraulic quantity = below 76%. Valid only on the ground with both engines shut down, or after landing with flaps up during taxi-in.
Hook: "RF = refill, below 76."
x.Q0904:
ENGINE HYD PUMP switch OFF ENERGIZES a BLOCKING VALVE in the pump that blocks its output (the pump keeps turning with the engine — no clutch). ON de-energizes it. Leave ON at shutdown to save the solenoid. Fire switch also shuts off the EDP's fluid supply.
Hook: "OFF = energize the block."
x.Q0905:
System B raises the gear after FAILURE OF No 1 ENGINE (RPM below limit), gear still down, lever UP. Triggered by engine RPM, not by the EDP or system A pressure.
Hook: "Engine 1 lost on takeoff → B raises the gear."
x.Q0906:
PTU (system A pressure → pump → system B fluid) supplies volume for the AUTOSLATS and LE FLAPS & SLATS at normal rate when the system B EDP is lost (airborne, flaps not up — < 15 on older aircraft). Not the TE flaps or gear.
Hook: "PTU = leading edge only."
x.Q0907:
PTU = backup for AUTOSLATS (and LE devices).
Hook: "PTU = leading edge only."
x.Q0908:
Landing gear transfer unit: uses system B to raise the gear at normal rate if No 1 ENGINE is lost (RPM below limit) with gear lever UP and a main gear not locked.
Hook: "Engine 1 lost → B raises the gear."
x.Q0909:
System B leak → quantity to ~0 and pressure lost (one standpipe for both pumps). But the fluid BELOW the standpipe stays in the reservoir and is enough for the PTU. (System A: standpipe saves ~20% for the electric pump.)
Hook: "B leak: pumps starve, PTU still has its reserve."
x.Q0910:
Hydraulic pressure: normal 3000 psi, MAX 3500 psi; both pumps off may show reservoir pressure (< 100 psi).
Hook: "3000 normal, 3500 max."
x.Q0911:
System A lost:
• FCOM 9.20.16: system 'A powers all four ground spoilers' → ground spoilers INOPERATIVE → longer landing distance.
• FCOM 9.20.4: four flight spoilers per wing, each hydraulic system powers a pair on each wing → HALF the flight spoilers on each wing are lost → reduced roll rate / speedbrake.
• FCOM 7.20.13: the No 1 thrust reverser can still work through the STANDBY system (slower).
Hook: "Lose A: no ground spoilers, half flight spoilers."
x.Q0913:
Standby leak: standby reservoir → 0 (LOW QUANTITY at half). System B (which refills the standby reservoir) keeps working but its quantity drops and stabilizes at ≈70% (bank answer 72%).
Hook: "Standby leak → B shows ~70%."
x.Q0914:
Yes: a leak anywhere in system B (EDP line included) → quantity ~0, total B pressure lost, but the PTU still works (reserve below standpipe). Standby system unaffected.
Hook: "B leak: pumps starve, PTU still has its reserve."
x.Q0915:
Brakes: NORMAL = system B; ALTERNATE = system A (automatic switch if B is lost); accumulator backup. Antiskid in both (alternate per wheel pair).
Hook: "Normal brakes B, alternate A."
x.Q0917:
EDP ≈ 6× the volume of the electric pump. A = EDP on engine 1 + ELEC 2; B = EDP on engine 2 + ELEC 1 (crossed for redundancy).
Hook: "EDP = 6 electric pumps."
x.Q0918:
OVERHEAT lights exist only for the ELECTRIC pumps: the fluid cooling/lubricating that electric pump has overheated, or the pump itself. No overheat light for engine pumps. NNC: switch that ELEC pump OFF.
Hook: "OVERHEAT = electric pump only."
x.Q0919:
Automatic standby: (loss of A or B + flaps extended + airborne/wheel speed > 60 kt + FLT CONTROL switch ON) OR FFM trips. Only option B fits; STBY RUD selection is manual activation; the speed is 60 kt not 50.
Hook: "FFM trips → standby on."
x.Q0920:
No fluid in B: TE flaps → electric alternate drive (not standby); LE flaps & slats → STANDBY hydraulics, FULL EXTEND ONLY (ALTERNATE FLAPS ARM + DOWN); autoslats LOST (the PTU needs system B fluid). Trim systems are electric — unaffected.
Hook: "B empty: standby pushes LE out, motor moves TE, no autoslats."
x.Q0921:
Normal quantity variations: system pressurized after engine start, GEAR or LE DEVICES moving, cold soak in long cruise. Little effect. (Foaming at altitude if not properly pressurized: fluctuating pressure, blinking LOW PRESSURE lights.)
Hook: "Quantity wobbles with start, gear, slats, cold."
x.Q0922:
System A reservoir: the EDP draws from a STANDPIPE, the ELECTRIC pump from the bottom. EDP-side leak → level stops at ~20% and the ELECTRIC pump keeps system A pressure. Leak on the electric pump side/common → quantity to 0, all A lost.
Hook: "A: standpipe saves the electric pump."
x.Q0923:
False. A: yes, the EDP starves first (standpipe), electric keeps going. B: ONE standpipe feeds BOTH pumps → both lose fluid together (only the PTU reserve stays).
Hook: "A protects its electric pump; B protects only the PTU."
x.Q0924:
Both B pump LOW PRESSURE lights (e.g. B leak) don't affect the STANDBY system: it has its own reservoir (linked to B only for pressurization/servicing) and its own electric pump. The FCOM states a B leak doesn't affect standby.
Hook: "B dies, standby lives."
x.Q0927:
Ground operation of the ELECTRIC hydraulic pumps needs 760 KG in the RELATED main tank (their cooling fluid runs through a heat exchanger in main tank 1 (A) / 2 (B)).
Hook: "760 kg to cool the hydraulics."
x.Q0928:
False as worded. The FLT CONTROL switches have STBY RUD / OFF / ON (ON = normal, guarded). It's the STBY RUD position that starts the standby pump and opens the standby rudder shutoff valve (and closes that system's flight control shutoff valve).
Hook: "STBY RUD does it; ON is normal."
x.Q0929:
ENG pump OFF: isolates the fluid flow from the system (blocking valve energized); the pump KEEPS ROTATING with the engine — no clutch/disconnect.
Hook: "OFF blocks the output; pump keeps spinning."
x.Q0930:
No 2 fire switch → shuts off fluid to the ENGINE-DRIVEN pump of SYSTEM B (engine 2 drives B's EDP) and deactivates its LOW PRESSURE light. Electric pumps unaffected.
Hook: "Engine 1 = A EDP, engine 2 = B EDP."
x.Q0931:
RF = quantity below 76%, valid only on the ground with both engines shut down, or after landing with flaps up during taxi-in.
Hook: "RF = refill, below 76."
x.Q0933:
Standby LOW PRESSURE: armed ONLY when standby pump operation is selected (STBY RUD / ALT FLAPS ARM) or auto standby is active. Standby LOW QUANTITY: always armed.
Hook: "Standby pressure light only when the pump should be running."
x.Q0935:
760 KG in each related main tank for ground operation of the electric pumps (heat exchangers in main tanks 1 and 2).
Hook: "760 kg to cool the hydraulics."
x.Q0936:
ENG pump switch ON = DE-ENERGIZES the blocking valve (pressure enters system). Leave ON at shutdown → solenoid de-energized → longer life.
Hook: "ON = de-energized = happy solenoid."
x.Q0938:
False: hydraulic quantity reads 0% to 106% (can exceed 100%, e.g. after overservicing or temperature).
Hook: "Hydraulics can read 106%."
x.Q0939:
Hydraulic pressure indication is WHITE; max 3500 psi (normal 3000). No colour change listed.
Hook: "3500 max, white."
x.Q0941:
False — that sentence describes the LANDING GEAR TRANSFER VALVE (B helps A raise the gear). The PTU is the opposite direction: A's pressure helps B for AUTOSLATS / LE devices.
Hook: "Gear transfer: B helps A. PTU: A helps B."
x.Q0942:
PTU auto: system B EDP pressure below limits + AIRBORNE + flaps < 15 but not up (YA573–YW097; 'flaps not up' on YW098+). Engine RPM conditions belong to the gear transfer valve.
Hook: "PTU: B EDP low, airborne, flaps out (<15)."
x.Q0943:
Standby leak → system B QUANTITY decreases (stabilizes ~70%) because the standby reservoir is fed from B; standby LOW QUANTITY at half empty. No pressure lights on A or B.
Hook: "Standby leak → B shows ~70%."
x.Q0944:
B leak → NO effect on the standby system (own reservoir/pump; B link only for pressurization/servicing). Bank wording 'own accumulator' is loose but 'no effect' is the key.
Hook: "B dies, standby lives."
x.Q0947:
System A pump cooling fluid heat exchanger → MAIN FUEL TANK 1; system B → main tank 2.
Hook: "A in tank 1, B in tank 2."
x.Q0951:
Hydraulics power: flight controls, wheel brakes, LE flaps & slats, TE flaps, nose wheel steering, landing gear, thrust reversers, autopilots. NOT autothrottle, NOT antiskid (electric), NOT the tiller as a 'system'.
Hook: "Hydraulics move surfaces, wheels, gear, reversers — and the A/P servos."
x.Q0953:
False. System A EDP-side leak → EDP starves at the standpipe (~20%), electric pump continues. Only an electric-side/common leak kills both.
Hook: "A: standpipe saves the electric pump."
x.Q0956:
ENG hydraulic pump switches are ON before start (they're left ON at shutdown for solenoid life). The ELECTRIC pumps are switched ON in the before-start flow.
Hook: "ENG pumps always ON."
x.Q0958:
QRH HYDRAULIC PUMP LOW PRESSURE: the affected PUMP switch → OFF (system pressure is held by the other pump). Not standby/STBY RUD.
Hook: "Pump LOW PRESSURE → that pump OFF."
x.Q0960:
False — up to 106%.
Hook: "Hydraulics can read 106%."
x.Q0961:
Standby system (one electric pump): THRUST REVERSERS, RUDDER, LE FLAPS & SLATS (extend only), STANDBY YAW DAMPER. No spoilers, no brakes.
Hook: "Standby = Reversers, Rudder, LE devices, standby YD."
x.Q0964:
-800 MFD SYS → hydraulic PRESSURE and QUANTITY only.
Hook: "SYS = hydraulics."
x.Q0966:
760 kg in each main tank for ground operation of the electric hydraulic pumps.
Hook: "760 kg to cool the hydraulics."
x.Q0967:
Leak on the system A ELECTRIC pump side (or common parts) → no standpipe protection → quantity to ZERO, ALL system A pressure lost.
Hook: "Electric-side leak = A empties."
x.Q0968:
Auto standby activation → STBY RUD ON + MASTER CAUTION + FLT CONT.
Hook: "Standby on → STBY RUD ON + master caution."
x.Q0969:
Standby LOW QUANTITY: ALWAYS armed. Standby LOW PRESSURE: armed only when the standby pump should be running.
Hook: "Quantity always watched; pressure only when used."
x.Q0970:
EDP LOW PRESSURE light = that pump's output low → on before start, goes OUT when the engine starts and the pump makes pressure. (Also deactivated by pulling the fire switch.) Switching the pump OFF does NOT put it out — it would show low output.
Hook: "EDP light goes out when its engine runs."
x.Q0972:
Standby: LE devices (extend only), rudder, thrust reversers, standby yaw damper.
Hook: "Standby = Reversers, Rudder, LE devices, standby YD."
x.Q0973:
Standby supplies rudder, thrust reversers, LE flaps & slats (+ standby yaw damper). Not gear, brakes, ailerons or TE flaps.
Hook: "Standby = Reversers, Rudder, LE devices."
x.Q0975:
False: standby can only EXTEND the LE devices; they can't be retracted with it.
Hook: "Standby LE: one-way trip."
x.Q0976:
False — the statement says standby extends the TE devices. Standby hydraulics only extend the LE devices (no retraction). TE flaps in alternate are driven by an ELECTRIC motor (up and down), with no asymmetry/skew protection.
Hook: "Standby = LE out; motor = TE up/down."
x.Q0977:
ENG 1 pump OFF with engine running: the pump keeps turning, its output is isolated from system A (blocking valve).
Hook: "OFF blocks the output; pump keeps spinning."
x.Q0470:
Impact fittings at the wheel well opening: a spinning tire with LOOSE TREAD hits the fitting → that gear STOPS retracting and FREE-FALLS back down, protecting the wheel well (hydraulic lines etc.). It stays down until maintenance replaces the fitting.
Hook: "Shredded tire → gear drops back down."
x.Q0491:
Steering LOCKOUT PIN (towing lever) depressurizes NOSE WHEEL STEERING only → pushback/towing possible with hydraulic systems still pressurized. Without it, system A must be depressurized (RYR procedure).
Hook: "Pin in = tug steers, hydraulics stay on."
x.Q0519:
RTO autobrake: MAX brake pressure when thrust levers are retarded to IDLE at or above 88 KT wheel speed (bank answer '90 kt' is the closest option). Below 88 kt, no automatic braking — brake manually.
Hook: "RTO: idle above 88 kt → max braking."
x.Q0533:
Both normal AND alternate brakes: skid, locked wheel, touchdown and hydroplane protection. Difference: normal = per wheel; alternate = per wheel PAIR. Antiskid works even with both hydraulic systems lost (accumulator).
Hook: "Antiskid: 4 protections, both systems."
x.Q0916:
False — reversed. NORMAL NWS = system A; ALTERNATE NWS = system B (switch ALT, needs normal B quantity, on ground).
Hook: "Steering: A normal, B alternate (brakes are the opposite)."
x.Q0925:
No steering lockout pin → steering would be powered by system A while the tug pushes. RYR procedure: before connecting the tug/towbar, SYSTEM A HYDRAULIC PUMPS (both) OFF (system B stays for brakes).
Hook: "No pin → system A pumps OFF."
x.Q0937:
HYD BRAKE PRESS shows ACCUMULATOR pressure: 1000 psi = nitrogen precharge (no hydraulic pressure); above that it reflects SYSTEM B pressure (B charges the accumulator). Normal 2900–3600, max 3600–4000 psi.
Hook: "Brake gauge = accumulator, charged by B."
x.Q0945:
Normal nose wheel steering = SYSTEM A (B alternate).
Hook: "Steering: A normal, B alternate."
x.Q0948:
Nose wheel steering: TILLER (up to 78°, overrides pedals) and RUDDER PEDALS (up to 7°; deactivated as the nose strut extends).
Hook: "Tiller 78°, pedals 7°."
x.Q0950:
Poorly written bank question: the answer '3500 psi in white' is the maximum HYDRAULIC SYSTEM pressure (lower DU). The real HYD BRAKE PRESS gauge: precharge 1000, normal 2900–3600, max 3600–4000 psi.
Hook: "System 3000/3500; brake accumulator up to 4000."
x.Q0954:
Loss of system A → NORMAL nose wheel steering lost (select ALT for system B steering). A/P B and autoslats are system B — still there.
Hook: "A lost → steering via ALT (B)."
x.Q0974:
Normal NWS = SYSTEM A (NORM guarded); ALT = system B.
Hook: "Steering: A normal, B alternate."
x.Q0978:
Manual extension access door OPEN: manual extension possible with the lever in ANY position; NORMAL extension still possible with system A; RETRACTION DISABLED. → all true. To retract after a manual extension: close door, lever DOWN with A pressure, then UP.
Hook: "Door open: can drop, can't raise."
x.Q0979:
False — it's 88 KT, not 90. (Some banks mark True; FCOM says 88.)
Hook: "RTO: 88 kt."
x.Q0980:
Autobrake disarm (DISARM light) after braking started: SPEED BRAKE lever to DOWN, advancing thrust lever(s) EXCEPT in the first 3 s after touchdown, or MANUAL BRAKES. Selector OFF disarms without the light. So 'advancing immediately after touchdown' does NOT disarm → D.
Hook: "Speedbrake down, manual brakes, throttles (after 3 s)."
x.Q0981:
NWS: system A normally; available only with nose gear DOWN and COMPRESSED (weight on wheels). Alternate = SYSTEM B (not standby) — and lost if B fluid is lost downstream of the gear transfer unit.
Hook: "Steering needs weight on the nose; ALT is B."
x.Q0982:
Manual gear extension handles (right main, nose, left main): pull each to its LIMIT — about 24 in / 61 CM — to release the uplock; gear free-falls (gravity + air loads).
Hook: "Pull 61 cm."
x.Q0983:
The FALSE statement: 'each wheel individual antiskid in normal AND alternate'. Alternate antiskid works on wheel PAIRS. The other statements are true.
Hook: "Alternate antiskid = pairs."
x.Q0984:
True: with normal (B) and alternate (A) brake pressure lost, the BRAKE ACCUMULATOR (charged by B) still gives SEVERAL braking applications or a parking brake application. Don't pump the brakes.
Hook: "Accumulator = last few brake applications."
x.Q0985:
Yes — parking brake pressure is held by the BRAKE ACCUMULATOR (and the pedals are mechanically latched) when A and B are depressurized. Check HYD BRAKE PRESS; chocks as required.
Hook: "Parking brake lives on the accumulator."
x.Q0986:
Yes: a gear is down and locked if ONE green light for it (centre panel OR aft overhead) is illuminated. Two independent indication sets.
Hook: "One green per gear is enough."
x.Q0987:
Brake accumulator → brakes and the PARKING BRAKE.
Hook: "Accumulator = brakes + parking brake."
x.Q0988:
True: centre panel green for the left gear is enough even if the overhead set doesn't show it.
Hook: "One green per gear is enough."
x.Q0989:
Red gear lights (centre panel only): (1) gear not down and locked with a thrust lever at idle below 800 ft AGL, AND (2) gear disagreeing with the lever (in transit/unsafe). Out when gear up & lever UP/OFF, or down & lever DN.
Hook: "Red = disagree, or not down when landing."
x.Q0990:
Door open: manual extension possible with the lever in ANY position (UP included), normal extension still possible with A, retraction disabled. Opening the door doesn't release uplocks — the handles do (pulled ~61 cm).
Hook: "Door open: can drop, can't raise."
x.Q0991:
Parking brake: A OR B (normal B / alternate A brakes) or, if neither, the ACCUMULATOR → 'all of the above'.
Hook: "Parking brake: A, B or accumulator."
x.Q0992:
Antiskid works in normal AND alternate (alternate per wheel pair); all four protections in both; it does NOT disengage with manual braking.
Hook: "Antiskid: both systems."
x.Q0993:
RTO selected on the ground → DISARM light 1–2 s then OUT = SELF-TEST PASSED. No fault. (Stays on = fault / not armed.)
Hook: "Blink 2 s = test passed."
x.Q0994:
Autobrake = NORMAL brake system only (system B). Not on alternate (A) or accumulator. Antiskid works on both.
Hook: "Autobrake needs normal brakes (B)."
x.Q0995:
True — brake accumulator: several braking applications.
Hook: "Accumulator = last few brake applications."
x.Q0996:
No fault: DISARM light for ~2 s after selecting RTO = self-test passed.
Hook: "Blink 2 s = test passed."
x.Q0997:
True: one green per gear (either panel) = down and locked.
Hook: "One green per gear is enough."
x.Q0998:
True — accumulator.
Hook: "Accumulator = last few brake applications."
x.Q0999:
ANTISKID INOP (amber) = fault detected by antiskid monitoring — and a PARKING BRAKE system fault can also trigger it (FCOM 14.20.6).
Hook: "Parking brake fault can show ANTISKID INOP."
x.Q1000:
Lockout (bypass) pin: depressurizes NOSE WHEEL STEERING → pushback/towing without depressurizing hydraulics.
Hook: "Pin in = tug steers, hydraulics stay on."
x.Q1002:
Selector OFF disarms autobrake WITHOUT the DISARM light. Speedbrake down, manual brakes, thrust levers (after 3 s) → light ON.
Hook: "OFF = silent disarm."
x.Q1003:
RTO arming: on ground, antiskid + autobrake OK, selector RTO, wheel speed < 60 kt, thrust levers IDLE. Activation: rejected above 88 kt + levers to idle → max braking; below 88 kt nothing (stays armed).
Hook: "Arm below 60; acts above 88."
x.Q1004:
Forgot autobrake? A landing setting can be selected AFTER touchdown, before decelerating through 30 KT groundspeed; braking starts immediately if thrust levers idle and wheels spun up.
Hook: "Late autobrake OK until 30 kt."
x.Q1005:
True statement: pedal steering deactivates as the nose strut extends (e.g. lift-off). Pedals give 7°, tiller 78° and overrides pedals; the lockout pin depressurizes steering (system A).
Hook: "Strut extends → pedal steering off."
x.Q1006:
Pedal steering deactivated as the nose strut extends. (7° pedals, 78° tiller, tiller overrides.)
Hook: "Strut extends → pedal steering off."
x.Q1007:
NWS switch ALT → SYSTEM B.
Hook: "Steering: A normal, B alternate."
x.Q1008:
No fault — passed self-test.
Hook: "Blink 2 s = test passed."
x.Q1044:
Air/ground system: SIX sensors, TWO on EACH landing gear → configures systems for air or ground (pressurization, speedbrakes, warnings, etc.).
Hook: "6 sensors, 2 per leg."
x.Q1053:
Red goes out only when gear position MATCHES the lever: up with UP/OFF, down with DN. Gear DOWN with lever OFF = disagreement → RED. (Gear up with OFF is fine.)
Hook: "Down gear wants the lever DN."
x.Q1063:
Aft overhead gear lights = REDUNDANT, SEPARATE circuits and GREEN lights only (no red).
Hook: "Overhead = backup greens."
x.Q0379:
Stall warning test (preflight) needs the AC TRANSFER busses powered for up to 4 MINUTES (SMYD warm-up). With hydraulics off, drooping LE flaps can make the test fail — pressurize B and retract.
Hook: "Stall test: 4 minutes of AC."
x.Q0702:
Terrain display: DOTTED RED = terrain > 2,000 ft ABOVE you; dotted amber = 500 ft (250 gear down) below → 2,000 ft above; dotted green = 2,000 ft below → 500/250 below; solid red/amber = look-ahead WARNING/CAUTION; magenta = no data. Relative to airplane ALTITUDE, not radio altitude.
Hook: "Dotted red = mountain well above you."
x.Q0808:
FCOM 15.20.31: 'If altitude data from the traffic aircraft's transponder is not available, no RA can be provided' and altitude is included 'if the other airplane is using transponder mode S or C'. So the MINIMUM for an RA is a Mode C (altitude-reporting) transponder. Mode S also works, but it isn't the minimum. ADS-B or primary radar alone are not enough.
Hook: "No altitude, no RA → minimum Mode C."
x.Q1009:
Stall warning test: AC TRANSFER busses powered for up to 4 MINUTES (not DC).
Hook: "Stall test: 4 minutes of AC."
x.Q1010:
Altitude alerting INHIBITED with TE FLAPS ≥ 25 or G/S CAPTURED (it would be a nuisance on approach). Alert window: 900 ft (white box, tone) to 300 ft; deviation > 300 ft → amber flashing.
Hook: "Flaps 25 or G/S → no altitude alerts."
x.Q1011:
TCAS inhibits (radio altitude): INCREASE DESCENT < 1,500 ft RA; DESCEND < 1,100 ft RA; all RAs and voice < 1,000 ft (automatically TA ONLY). GPWS/windshear inhibit all TCAS alerts.
Hook: "1500 increase-descent, 1100 descend, 1000 no RAs."
x.Q1012:
Silence the fire bell from the flight deck: master FIRE WARN light OR BELL CUTOUT switch. The APU horn cutout on the ground panel only silences the remote horn (and the bell) from outside.
Hook: "Bell off: FIRE WARN light or BELL CUTOUT."
x.Q1013:
NEVER: the landing gear warning is a STEADY horn. INTERMITTENT horn = takeoff configuration and cabin altitude. Clacker = overspeed, bell = fire, tone = A/P disconnect, voice = GPWS/windshear.
Hook: "Gear = steady; takeoff config & cabin alt = intermittent."
x.Q1014:
Altitude acquisition alert (RYR fleet YF501+): at 900 ft to go → white box around selected altitude, current altitude box bold, momentary tone; at 300 ft to go → box disappears. (YA573: 200 ft.)
Hook: "900 box on, 300 box off."
x.Q1015:
Vmo/Mmo exceeded: CLACKER (silenced only by slowing below Vmo/Mmo) + the RED/BLACK band on the speed tape. Amber bands = maneuver margins; stick shaker = stall.
Hook: "Overspeed = clacker + red/black barber pole."
x.Q1016:
Deviation alert: 300 FT away from the selected altitude → tone + current altitude box AMBER FLASHING.
Hook: "Off by 300 → amber flash."
x.Q1017:
Look-ahead terrain: CAUTION TERRAIN (amber) at 40–60 s to impact; TERRAIN TERRAIN PULL UP (red) at 20–30 s. Time-based, not distance.
Hook: "Caution 40–60 s, pull up 20–30 s."
x.Q1018:
Amber flashing deviation alert stops when: back within 300 ft, more than 900 ft away, or a NEW altitude is selected.
Hook: "Fix it, leave it (900), or change it."
x.Q1020:
With TA/RA selected, below 1,000 ft RA TCAS automatically goes TA ONLY (message on ND).
Hook: "Below 1000 → TA only."
x.Q1021:
BANK ANGLE, BANK ANGLE at 35°, 40° and 45°; each once, reset when bank ≤ 30°. (PFD bank pointer turns amber at 35°.)
Hook: "35-40-45, reset at 30."
x.Q1022:
PWS symbol = red/black arcs; its RADIALS = AMBER (help locate it). WINDSHEAR text amber (caution) / red (warning).
Hook: "Symbol red/black, radials amber."
x.Q1023:
False — the PSEU light is on the AFT overhead panel. Conditions correct: on the ground, PSEU fault or overwing exit flight lock failing to disengage; inhibited from takeoff thrust until 30 s after landing.
Hook: "PSEU lives aft."
x.Q1024:
Stall warning comes from the two SMYD computers (stick shakers, PLI, airspeed bars, GPWS windshear).
Hook: "SMYD = stall brain."
x.Q1025:
TCAS symbols: PROXIMATE = SOLID WHITE diamond (within 6 NM and 1,200 ft, no threat); OTHER = hollow white diamond; TA = amber filled circle; RA = red filled square.
Hook: "Solid white = close but harmless."
x.Q1026:
TA ≈ 40 s from closest point of approach; RA ≈ 25 s. No RA without the intruder's altitude.
Hook: "TA 40, RA 25."
x.Q1027:
System annunciator panels (glareshield) cover only systems on the forward overhead, aft overhead and fire panels, arranged to mirror where those panels are (left items on left etc.), so you know where to look. Not by priority.
Hook: "Annunciator = map of the overhead."
x.Q1028:
First RA callout: 2,500 FT 'TWENTY FIVE HUNDRED'; then 1000, 500 (smart), 50-40-30-20-10 (some aircraft 100).
Hook: "Callouts start at 2500."
x.Q1029:
CABIN ALTITUDE: cabin > 10,000 ft → INTERMITTENT horn + RED CABIN ALTITUDE lights. Horn silenced by ALT HORN CUTOUT; light stays until below 10,000. Same intermittent horn as TAKEOFF CONFIG — on the ground it's config, in the air it's cabin altitude!
Hook: "Intermittent horn in the air = masks on."
x.Q1030:
TERRAIN and WEATHER cannot be shown together on one ND. If one pilot has each, displays update on alternate sweeps. Everything else (TCAS, route, data) can overlay terrain.
Hook: "Terrain or weather, never both."
x.Q1031:
Gear horn (thrust lever < ~20°, below 800 ft RA): can be silenced with HORN CUTOUT only at flaps UP–10 and ABOVE 200 FT RA. Flaps 15–25 or below 200 ft: cannot be silenced. Flaps > 25: horn regardless of thrust, no silencing.
Hook: "Cutout works only flaps ≤10 and above 200 ft."
x.Q1035:
True: SMYDs drive stall warning AND the GPWS (reactive) windshear detection and alert.
Hook: "SMYD = stall + reactive windshear."
x.Q1036:
RA callouts begin at TWENTY FIVE HUNDRED.
Hook: "Callouts start at 2500."
x.Q1040:
False. IntuVue in flight: WARNING region 0.5–1.5 NM ahead (±25°); CAUTION region out to 3 NM. (From the diagram on 15.20.28.)
Hook: "Warning 0.5–1.5, caution to 3."
x.Q1042:
True: pushing the BELOW G/S P-INHIBIT light cancels/inhibits the GLIDESLOPE alert below 1,000 ft RA (e.g. intentionally below G/S on a visual).
Hook: "Push BELOW G/S → glideslope alert off (below 1000)."
x.Q1048:
Man-made obstructions are NOT accounted for in all EGPWS databases (FCOM note for some effectivities) → don't rely on EGPWS for towers/buildings.
Hook: "EGPWS may not know the tower."
x.Q1049:
False: terrain within 2,000 FT of barometric altitude is displayed (not 2,500).
Hook: "Terrain shown within 2,000 ft."
x.Q1052:
Note (audit): option C is also arguably true – at flaps 15 ANY thrust lever below ~20° triggers the horn. D is the bank answer. Flaps 15–25 + gear not down: horn when EITHER thrust lever < ~20° (or one engine out and the other < 34°); cannot be silenced. Flaps > 25: horn regardless of thrust. Bank answer D (flaps 15, one lever idle, other < 34°).
Hook: "Flaps 15: low thrust + gear up = steady horn."
x.Q1054:
Terrain shown within 2,000 ft of BAROMETRIC altitude (not RA).
Hook: "Terrain shown within 2,000 ft (baro)."
x.Q1055:
Yes — MACH AIRSPEED WARNING TEST is inhibited airborne → ground only (clacker sounds).
Hook: "Clacker test on the ground."
x.Q1057:
Overwing exit flight lock failed locked (or PSEU fault) → PSEU + OVERHEAD + MASTER CAUTION, but INHIBITED from takeoff until 30 s after ground mode → appears 30 s after landing.
Hook: "PSEU waits 30 s after landing."
x.Q1059:
SMYD inputs: ALPHA VANES, ADIRUs, ANTI-ICE controls, WING configuration, AIR/GROUND, THRUST and FMC outputs.
Hook: "SMYD reads everything that changes stall speed."
x.Q1060:
False: the stall test checks the STICK SHAKERS (No 1 → Captain's, No 2 → F/O's, both columns vibrate). The CLACKER is the Mach/airspeed test.
Hook: "Stall test = shaker; overspeed test = clacker."
x.Q1061:
TAKEOFF CONFIG (intermittent horn) on thrust advance if: flaps not in takeoff range (1–25) or asymmetry/skew, LE devices not right, speed brake lever not DOWN, spoiler valve open, PARKING BRAKE SET, STAB TRIM outside the green band. Flaps 5 is valid.
Hook: "Flaps, slats, speedbrake, park brake, trim."
x.Q1065:
True: pressing an annunciator panel (recall) lights all twelve system lights on both panels while held (bulb test), then shows existing faults, including stored 'simple faults'. A bulb that doesn't light → DDG.
Hook: "Recall = 12 lights test + replay faults."
x.Q1066:
Corrected after the independent audit: False. The EGPWS 'TOO LOW, TERRAIN' alert (FCOM 15.20.13): 'Descent below unsafe altitude while too far from any airport in the terrain database' – this uses the airport database, not the gear/flap configuration, so an off-airport landing in landing configuration WILL still get an alert. (Some banks say True, thinking only of the basic 'too low gear/flaps' mode.)
Hook: "No airport there → EGPWS still shouts."
x.Q1068:
First RA callout descending: TWENTY FIVE HUNDRED (2,500 ft). Then 1000, 500, 100, 50-40-30-20-10.
Hook: "Callouts start at 2500."
x.Q1069:
GLIDESLOPE alert: louder/faster with more deviation. Cancel = push either pilot's BELOW G/S P-INHIBIT light (below 1,000 ft RA) or fly back to the glideslope. RECALL does nothing to aurals.
Hook: "Push BELOW G/S or fix the path."
x.Q1070:
The PSEU light is inhibited IN FLIGHT. If it shows on recall during the approach checklist, the inhibit isn't working → a PSEU problem. The normal PSEU check is on the ground, more than 30 s after landing.
Hook: "PSEU in flight = PSEU is sick."
x.Q1072:
RA ≈ 25 s from the point of closest approach (TA ≈ 40 s). It's time-based, not a fixed distance or a fixed 1,000 ft.
Hook: "TA 40, RA 25."
x.Q1074:
Predictive windshear: the radar scans with takeoff thrust set or in flight below 1,800 ft RA (2,300 ft on YA573/older), but ALERTS are only issued below 1,200 FT RA. Trap: 2,300 is the scan height on some aircraft.
Hook: "Scan at 1800, alert at 1200."
x.Q1075:
TCAS inhibits (descending): INCREASE DESCENT < 1,500 ft → DESCEND < 1,100 ft → ALL RAs and voice < 1,000 ft RA (TA ONLY shown). GPWS and windshear warnings inhibit all TCAS alerts.
Hook: "1500 – 1100 – 1000: the ground is closer, fewer RAs."
x.Q1078:
An RA needs the intruder's ALTITUDE → it must have a Mode C or S transponder. Mode A = no altitude → TA only (no RA). The intruder doesn't need TCAS itself.
Hook: "No altitude, no RA → needs C or S."
x.Q1081:
The clacker can ONLY be silenced by slowing below Vmo/Mmo. HORN CUTOUT = landing gear horn; ALT HORN CUTOUT = cabin altitude horn; nothing for the clacker.
Hook: "Only slowing stops the clacker."
x.Q1082:
Cabin altitude horn: silenced with ALT HORN CUTOUT on the Cabin Altitude Panel (next to pressurisation). The RED light stays until cabin < 10,000 ft.
Hook: "ALT HORN CUTOUT kills the noise, not the light."
x.Q1083:
Same rule: only by slowing below Vmo/Mmo. The test switch is ground-only; there is no reset switch.
Hook: "Clacker: slow down."
x.Q1084:
Terrain colours: dotted GREEN = 2,000 ft below to 500 ft (250 ft gear down) below you; dotted AMBER = 500/250 ft below to 2,000 ft above; dotted RED = more than 2,000 ft above; SOLID amber/red = look-ahead caution/warning; magenta = no data; black = nothing significant. Terrain more than 2,000 ft below = not shown.
Hook: "Green 2000 below, red 2000 above."
x.Q1085:
No: the crew can't reset a real PSEU fault. Only a maintenance BITE check or fixing the fault clears it. (Exception on some aircraft: a 'simple fault' seen only on recall goes out when MASTER CAUTION is reset.) No CB pulling, no thrust lever tricks.
Hook: "PSEU = engineers' light."
x.Q1086:
No 1 test → only the CAPTAIN's shaker motor runs, but the columns are mechanically interconnected, so both shake. No 2 → F/O's motor.
Hook: "One motor, two columns shake."
x.Q1087:
PSEU light (amber, aft overhead), ON THE GROUND: PSEU fault OR overwing exit flight lock fails to disengage. In flight it's inhibited. Doors = DOOR lights, not PSEU.
Hook: "PSEU = overwing lock stuck (on ground)."
x.Q1089:
Look at the diagram 'Predictive Windshear Alert Area' (FCOM 15.20.28): IN FLIGHT the WARNING area goes from 0.5 to 1.5 NM ahead (±25°); the CAUTION area goes out to 3 NM. On the ground the warning area is 0.5–3 NM. The system is the weather radar (RDR-4000 IntuVue), not the EGPWS, and alerts are issued below 1,200 ft RA (not 1,500).
Hook: "Radar windshear: warning ≤1.5 NM in the air."
x.Q1091:
TCAS pops up automatically on a TA/RA (TFC not selected) in MAP, CENTER MAP, VOR or APP modes. Not in PLN.
Hook: "Pops up everywhere except PLAN."
x.Q1095:
Config warning causes include TE flaps SKEW/ASYMMETRY/uncommanded motion. Wrong answers: thrust not set (warning arms when you ADVANCE thrust), stab IN the range is fine, 'flaps 2' doesn't exist.
Hook: "Skewed flaps = config horn."
x.Q1096:
PSEU monitors: takeoff config warnings, landing config warnings, landing gear, air/ground sensing (and controls the overwing exit flight locks). Pick the fullest answer.
Hook: "PSEU = gear, air/ground and config warnings."
x.Q1100:
Aural: 'BANK ANGLE, BANK ANGLE' (said twice) at 35°, 40°, 45°.
Hook: "Bank angle, said twice."
x.Q1102:
The full GPWS SYS TEST runs on the ground (lights, TERR TEST, PULL UP/WINDSHEAR, aurals). Answer: only on the ground.
Hook: "GPWS test on the ground."
x.Q1103:
Predictive windshear works AUTOMATICALLY (no switch needed in flight); alerts are issued below 1,200 ft RA. (WXR can be pushed before takeoff to enable it early.)
Hook: "Automatic, alerts below 1200."
x.Q1104:
CLIMB – CLIMB NOW = REVERSAL from an initial DESCEND RA (the intruder changed path). DESCEND – DESCEND NOW = reversal from an initial climb. 'NOW' always means reversal: act fast.
Hook: "'NOW' = reverse what you were doing."
x.Q1105:
Two independent identical SMYD computers decide when stall warning is needed (from alpha vanes, ADIRUs, anti-ice, configuration, air/ground...). The vanes and ADIRUs are INPUTS, not the decision maker.
Hook: "Two SMYDs decide."
x.Q1106:
False: the first part is right, but each test vibrates BOTH columns (interconnected), not only the one with the motor.
Hook: "One test, both columns shake."
x.Q1109:
True: the SMYDs also provide outputs for GPWS windshear detection and alert.
Hook: "SMYD = stall + windshear."
x.Q1110:
FCOM 15.20.28 diagram 'Predictive Windshear Alert Area': ON GROUND the warning area is 0.5–3 NM; IN FLIGHT it's 0.5–1.5 NM (cautions out to 3 NM); ±25° each side.
Hook: "Air 1.5, ground 3."
x.Q1111:
Picture = solid AMBER circle = TA → traffic about 40 s from closest approach, 'TRAFFIC, TRAFFIC'. Red square = RA (25 s). Solid white diamond = proximate (6 NM/1,200 ft, no alert).
Hook: "Amber circle = TA = 40 s."
x.Q1112:
Solid amber circle = TA ≈ 40 s. 'Within 6 NM and 1,200 ft' describes PROXIMATE traffic (white diamond), not a TA.
Hook: "Amber circle = 40 s."
x.Q1113:
BELOW G/S P-INHIBIT: cancels/inhibits the GLIDESLOPE alert only, and only below 1,000 ft RA. It does NOT inhibit other GPWS warnings.
Hook: "Push BELOW G/S → glideslope alert off (below 1000)."
x.Q1114:
DH/MDA callouts from the CAPTAIN's MINS selector (RADIO → RA, BARO → baro): 'PLUS HUNDRED' at minimums +100 ft, 'MINIMUMS' at minimums.
Hook: "Plus hundred, then minimums."
x.Q1119:
ALL TCAS alerts are inhibited by GPWS and WINDSHEAR warnings (the ground is the bigger threat). The height inhibits only remove some RAs/voice: DESCEND < 1,100 ft, RAs < 1,000 ft, voice < 500 ft (RYR table).
Hook: "Ground beats traffic."
x.Q1120:
RA ≈ 25 s to closest approach; TA ≈ 40 s. 6 NM / 1,200 ft = proximate traffic definition.
Hook: "TA 40, RA 25."
x.Q1121:
PSEU light inhibited: IN FLIGHT + when thrust levers advanced for takeoff + for 30 s after landing (all three). It goes out when parking brake set or both engines off.
Hook: "Air, takeoff thrust, 30 s after landing."
x.Q1122:
False: the Mach/airspeed warning test is INHIBITED while airborne. It is done on the GROUND, each system separately.
Hook: "Clacker test = ground only."
x.Q1123:
Bank answer: at battery power-up, many systems are still off (packs, pumps, generators...), so their amber lights come on → MASTER CAUTION + several system annunciators. No 4-minute suppression; no fire bell unless there's a fire (or a test).
Hook: "Cold aircraft = lots of amber."
x.Q1124:
TA = SOLID AMBER CIRCLE. RA = solid red square. Proximate = solid white diamond. Other = hollow white diamond. No blue symbols.
Hook: "Circle amber TA, square red RA, diamonds white."
x.Q1125:
Spoilers partially extended (speed brake lever not DOWN / spoilers not stowed) → config warning. Speed brake DOWN, slats extended with flaps 5 or 15 = normal takeoff configs.
Hook: "Spoilers up on takeoff = horn."
x.Q1126:
Proximate = within 6 NM and 1,200 ft, no TA/RA expected, shown as a solid white diamond. OFFSCALE appears when a TA/RA is outside the ND range.
Hook: "Proximate = 6 and 1200."
x.Q1128:
Mach/airspeed test: on the GROUND, push No 1 and No 2 separately → clacker for each, proving both systems. It is inhibited airborne, so it's no help for unreliable airspeed.
Hook: "Two buttons, two clackers, on the ground."
x.Q1129:
PSEU monitors takeoff/landing config warnings, landing gear and air/ground sensing. Anti-skid is NOT PSEU (it's the antiskid system).
Hook: "PSEU: no anti-skid."
x.Q1130:
Proximate traffic: within 6 NM horizontally and 1,200 ft vertically (white solid diamond).
Hook: "6 and 1200."
x.S001:
Takeoff: thrust levers to ~40% N1, engines stable → 'STABILIZED' → PF pushes TO/GA, calls 'SET TAKEOFF THRUST'. Captain's hand guards the thrust levers.
Hook: "40%, stabilized, TOGA."
x.S002:
After TOGA: PF 'SET TAKEOFF THRUST'. PM then: 'TAKEOFF THRUST SET', 'INDICATIONS NORMAL'.
Hook: "PF asks SET, PM answers SET."
x.S003:
FCOM NP.40.2 callout table, row '80 knots': PM column "80 KNOTS", PF column C "CHECK" (* Note 1 = incapacitation check / instrument crosscheck). C = calls, R = responds.
Hook: "80 knots – check."
x.S004:
FCOM NP.40.2 table, row 'Positive climb': PM "POSITIVE RATE" → PF "GEAR UP". The PM sees it, only the PF orders the gear.
Hook: "PM sees it, PF orders it."
x.S005:
Above 400 ft RADIO altitude: roll mode 'LNAV' or 'HDG SEL'. Then 1,000 ft AAL CMD A/B; 1,500 ft AAL N1 climb thrust; 1,000 (NADP 2) / 3,000 (NADP 1) BUG UP.
Hook: "400 roll mode."
x.S006:
1,000 ft AAL: autopilot CMD A or B, PF 'COMMAND A or B', PM 'CHECKED'.
Hook: "1000 = autopilot in."
x.S007:
FCOM NP.40.2 table, 'BUG UP' row: 1000 ft AAL (NADP 2) or 3000 feet AAL (NADP 1). So NADP 1 → 3,000 ft AAL.
Hook: "NADP 1 = 3000, NADP 2 = 1000."
x.S008:
NADP 1 initial climb: minimum V2 + 15 (up to V2 + 25 at light weight to match F/D pitch), max 20° nose up.
Hook: "V2+15, max 20°."
x.S009:
Do not exceed 20° nose up.
Hook: "20 up max."
x.S010:
1,500 ft AAL: FMA 'N1' and automatic thrust reduction to climb thrust.
Hook: "1500 = climb thrust."
x.S011:
FCOM NP.40.3 table, row 'Flaps up': PM "FLAPS UP – NO LIGHTS" → PF "AFTER TAKEOFF CHECKLIST" (then "VNAV").
Hook: "Flaps up, no lights, checklist."
x.S012:
FCOM NP.40.3 table, row '1,000 ft to cleared altitude': PM "ONE TO GO" → PF "CHECK".
Hook: "One to go."
x.S013:
FCOM NP.40.3 table, climb row 'FL100': PM "ALTIMETERS" → PF "PASSING FL ___ CLIMBING ___, TEN CHECKS" (Note 2 = altimeter crosscheck).
Hook: "FL100 = ten checks."
x.S014:
FCOM NP.40.3 table, 'When cleared to final cruising level': PF "FL ___ SET, THREE TIMES" (check CRZ page, MCP and FLT ALT on the pressurisation panel); PM "CHECK".
Hook: "Three places: CRZ, MCP, FLT ALT."
x.S015:
FCOM NP.40.3 descent part of the table: 'FL150 / 15 mins to landing' → "SEAT BELT SIGN ON".
Hook: "150 / 15 min: belts on."
x.S016:
RYR sterile cockpit: no unnecessary conversation from ENGINE START to TOP OF CLIMB and from TOP OF DESCENT to ENGINE SHUTDOWN.
Hook: "Start→TOC, TOD→shutdown."
x.S017:
If the PM misses a callout, the PF makes it. A missing callout can mean incapacitation or a malfunction.
Hook: "Missing call → PF calls it."
x.S018:
EGPWS 'TWENTY FIVE HUNDRED' → PF 'TERRAIN NOTED' (approach, and in climb/cruise). In climb/cruise the PF checks TERRAIN is on the F/O's ND and that the route clears terrain; any doubt → turn away from high ground.
Hook: "2500 → terrain noted."
x.S019:
Gear down + flaps 15 at 5 NM IMC / 4 NM VMC (V/S NPAs: 5 NM always). Then landing config to be stable by 1,000 ft (IMC) / 500 ft (VMC).
Hook: "5 IMC, 4 VMC."
x.S020:
Stable in landing configuration: 1,000 ft AAL in IMC (white bar), 500 ft AAL in VMC (amber bar).
Hook: "IMC 1000 white, VMC 500 amber."
x.S021:
500 CONTINUE speed: target VREF+5 to VREF+15; limits min VREF, max VREF+20.
Hook: "+5 to +15, never below Vref or above +20."
x.S022:
ILS: G/S ±1 dot (or 3 reds/3 whites PAPI) and LOC ±1 dot. LNAV/VNAV: ±75 ft vertical, RNAV ½ RNP lateral.
Hook: "One dot each way."
x.S023:
Vertical speed proportional to approach design and groundspeed, not more than 1,000 fpm unless briefed.
Hook: "Max 1000 fpm."
x.S024:
Any criterion not confirmed → '500 GO-AROUND'. No 'unstable – continue'.
Hook: "Not stable = go around."
x.S025:
Circling/side-step: aligned with the centreline by 300 ft AAL (exceptions in OMC AFB).
Hook: "Wings level on centreline by 300."
x.S026:
500 CONTINUE criteria include the landing checklist COMPLETED (except landing lights) and appropriate thrust set.
Hook: "Checklist done, lights aside."
x.S027:
NPA: set missed approach altitude at 1,000 ft AAL. If MDA/DA ≥ 900 ft AAL → set it at 300 ft above MDA/DA (avoid ALT ACQ). If MAA is lower than 1,300 ft AAL → set it after descending 300 ft below MAA. Agree the point before the approach.
Hook: "MAA at 1000 (or 300 above high minima)."
x.S028:
Go-around initiated BY DA, without delay at the minimums call. PF doesn't search for cues — the PM calls them. No cue calls heard = no visual = go around.
Hook: "Minimums, no call → go."
x.S029:
FCOM NP.40.5, GO-AROUND part, row '400 ft radio': PM "LNAV or HDG SEL, SPEED CHECKS, FLAPS 5" → PF "LNAV or HDG SEL, FLAPS 5". Gear up was already called at positive climb.
Hook: "400 = roll mode + flaps 5."
x.S030:
RIBETS = Route check, Instrument crosscheck, takeoff Briefing, Emergency briefing (initial), Taxi routing, SID briefing. If done before ATC clearance, confirm the cleared SID = loaded and briefed.
Hook: "R-I-B-E-T-S: Route, Instruments, Briefing, Emergency, Taxi, SID."
x.S031:
SID change: STOP the aircraft; don't taxi or accept line-up/takeoff until re-briefed and FMC entries (performance, NAVAIDs, MCP) re-confirmed; redo RIBETS.
Hook: "New SID = stop and brief."
x.S032:
RYR max taxi speeds: contaminated 5, turns 10, aprons 15, TAXIWAY 30, runway backtrack 50.
Hook: "5-10-15-30-50."
x.S035:
Before crossing or entering ANY runway (active or not): the 'Two Phase Call'.
Hook: "Any runway = two phase call."
x.S036:
Marshalled off stand: taxi light ON only once the nose wheels are turned away from the marshaller (don't dazzle them).
Hook: "Don't blind the marshaller."
x.S037:
Crosswind > 10 kt → NO assumed temperature (full rated, or the next derate without assumed temp). Reason: rudder/VMCG margins.
Hook: "Xwind over 10 = no assumed temp."
x.S038:
Flaps 1 takeoff: only for performance; flown by the CAPTAIN.
Hook: "Flaps 1 = Captain's."
x.S039:
Slight forward pressure to 80 kt, then relax to neutral. At VR rotate 2–2.5°/s towards 15° (beware the 10° dead band), limit 20°.
Hook: "Forward to 80, rotate 2–2.5°/s to 15."
x.S040:
Single-engine taxi: max 40% N1; it takes about twice as long to accelerate.
Hook: "EOT ≤ 40% N1."
x.S041:
EOT after landing: actual GW ≤ 63,000 kg, plus no LVP, no freezing, no contamination, braking action good, ≤ 40% N1, after landing procedure done.
Hook: "EOT ≤ 63 t."
x.S042:
EOT NOT allowed with LVPs (also freezing conditions, contamination, GW > 63 t, conflicting NNC/MEL).
Hook: "No LVP, no ice, no slush, ≤63 t."
x.S043:
After autoland the F/O stays on instruments until TAXI SPEED (monitors rollout guidance).
Hook: "F/O head down to taxi speed."
x.S044:
FCOM NP.40.6, Additional Autoland Callouts, row '500ft RA': First Officer "PASSING ___ RADIO, FLARE ARMED" → Captain "500 RADIO FLARE ARMED".
Hook: "500: flare armed."
x.S045:
FCOM NP.40.6, LANDING, 'Landing roll' (PM): "SPEEDBRAKES UP/NOT UP", then "REVERSERS NORMAL" or "NO REVERSER ENGINE NUMBER 1/2" or "NO REVERSERS", then ___%, 100, 80, 60, "AUTOBRAKE DISARM".
Hook: "Speedbrakes, reversers, speeds."
x.S046:
Visual with FMC: pick a point not less than 4 NM from the runway; be there with gear down, flaps 15. Don't turn final unless on path ±400 ft.
Hook: "4 NM point, gear + 15."
x.S047:
Any doubt about terrain clearance → REFUSE the visual approach. Offset approaches often exist because of terrain.
Hook: "Doubt = refuse."
x.S048:
EGPWS 2500 in climb/cruise: PF 'TERRAIN NOTED', confirm TERRAIN on the F/O's ND, check route vs terrain (MSA / plog safety height). Doubt → turn away from high ground.
Hook: "2500 → terrain noted, F/O ND on TERR."
x.S049:
APU: run TWO full minutes before using it as a bleed air source (thermal stabilisation).
Hook: "APU 2 minutes before bleed."
x.S050:
Transponder ALT OFF before requesting push/start → ground radar/ATC can see the aircraft's position. TA/RA only before takeoff.
Hook: "ALT OFF = ATC sees you on stand."
x.S051:
TA/RA selected BEFORE TAKEOFF (with LNAV/HDG SEL armed, TERR on F/O's ND).
Hook: "Line-up: TA/RA."
x.S052:
Weather radar ON for takeoff: the Captain includes it in the scan on the 'MCP' response of BEFORE TAKEOFF BELOW THE LINE.
Hook: "MCP check includes the radar."
x.S053:
Cool down: at least 3 min at taxi thrust before shutdown; less than 3 min routinely not recommended.
Hook: "3 minutes cool-down."
x.S054:
FCOM NP.21.144 (shutdown procedure): 'After placing the start lever(s) to cutoff, both pilots must verify a reduction in N2 indication(s).' Confirms the correct engine has been shut down.
Hook: "Cutoff → watch N2 drop."
x.S055:
Before start below the line: PF actions items and calls for it; PM reads/completes the checklist.
Hook: "PF does, PM reads."
x.S056:
Before takeoff below the line: the F/O actions the items, then reads the checklist aloud.
Hook: "F/O does, then reads."
x.S057:
F/O 'CLEAR RIGHT' (his side), Captain 'CLEAR LEFT' and taxi/turnoff lights on.
Hook: "Each pilot clears his own side."
x.S058:
F/O types taxi instructions in the FMC CDU scratchpad and displays the taxi chart on the EFB.
Hook: "Taxi route in the scratchpad."
x.S059:
Progressive Taxi = the PM (right seat) does ACTIVE monitoring of the taxi (route, speed, runways).
Hook: "Right seat actively monitors."
x.S060:
No checklist challenge/response approaching or during turns; only when safety/TEM permit.
Hook: "No checklists in turns."
x.S061:
Squawk: PM writes in scratchpad → PF crosschecks → PM sets transponder → PF verifies.
Hook: "Write, check, set, verify."
x.S064:
Prior to spool-up: RAAS 'On runway __' (or 'XXX/XXX' ND track/runway heading without RAAS) → PF 'TIMING', start CHR and ET.
Hook: "On runway → timing."
x.S065:
The Captain's hand guards the thrust levers during takeoff (he's the one who rejects).
Hook: "Captain's hand on the levers."
x.S066:
FCOM NP.40.3, descent, 'Transition level or when cleared to an altitude': PM "CHECK" → PF "SET QNH ___, PASSING ___, DESCENDING ___FT, ___FLAGS, STANDBY ALTIMETER SET".
Hook: "QNH, passing, descending, flags, standby."
x.S067:
FCOM NP.40.4, row 'When cleared to intercept VOR/LOC': PM "CHECK" → PF "VOR/LOC ARMED". Then 'VOR or LOC alive' and 'capture' rows follow.
Hook: "Cleared → armed."
x.S068:
FCOM NP.40.4, row 'VOR or LOC capture': PM "VOR or LOC CAPTURE" → PF "CHECK, RUNWAY HEADING ___ SET" (or "SET RUNWAY HEADING ___").
Hook: "Captured → runway heading."
x.S069:
FCOM NP.40.5, row 'Glideslope capture': PM "GLIDESLOPE CAPTURE" → PF "CHECK, ___ FEET SET" (the missed approach altitude is set in the MCP).
Hook: "G/S capture → set go-around altitude."
x.S070:
FCOM NP.40.4, row '4/5NM from runway': PF "GEAR DOWN, FLAPS 15, LANDING CHECKLIST TO FLAPS"; PM "SPEED CHECKS, GEAR DOWN, FLAPS 15".
Hook: "Gear, 15, checklist to flaps."
x.S071:
FCOM NP.40.5, row 'Outer marker': PM "ALTITUDE CHECKS, FLAGS / NO FLAGS" → PF "OUTER MARKER ___ FEET, FLAGS / NO FLAGS".
Hook: "FAF: altitude and flags."
x.S072:
FCOM NP.40.5, row 'EGPWS "1000"': PF "CHECK".
Hook: "1000 – check."
x.S073:
FCOM NP.40.5, row 'EGPWS MINIMUMS': PM "GO-AROUND" or "LIGHTS / RWY IN SIGHT" → PF "GO-AROUND, FLAPS__" or "CONTINUE".
Hook: "Runway in sight → continue."
x.S074:
FCOM NP.40.5, GO-AROUND, row 'Positive climb': PM "POSITIVE RATE" → PF "GEAR UP" — same as on takeoff.
Hook: "Same as takeoff: positive rate, gear up."
x.S075:
FCOM NP.40.6, 'Landing roll' (PM): after speedbrakes and reversers: "___%, 100, 80, 60 (IAS)" then "AUTOBRAKE DISARM".
Hook: "100-80-60, autobrake disarm."
x.S076:
Autobrake disarmed before taxi speed by manual braking (the only approved way in a normal rollout); call 'MANUAL BRAKING' / 'AUTOBRAKE DISARM'.
Hook: "Brake pedals kill the autobrake."
x.S077:
From 60 kt (stopping assured) start reducing reverse; reverse IDLE by taxi speed; full down after engines spool down; check REV out. Reason: avoid exhaust re-ingestion/FOD.
Hook: "60 start reducing, idle by taxi speed."
x.S078:
FCOM NP.40.7, Additional VNAV Callouts: '2nm before ND descent point': PM "APPROACHING DESCENT" → PF "XXX FEET SET".
Hook: "2 NM: approaching descent, set altitude."
x.S079:
FCOM NP.40.12 (CPDLC): 'PM will read the message out loud' → PF calls WILCO/UNABLE/STBY → PM presses it; when closed PM calls "CLOSED".
Hook: "PM reads, PF decides, PM presses."
x.S080:
FCOM NP.40.14: "VERTICAL SPEED" (Less than 300 fpm or greater than 1000 fpm in the last 1000 feet AGL).
Hook: "Below 300 or above 1000."
x.S081:
FCOM NP.40.14: "SPEED" whenever IAS is less than Vref or greater than Vfly + 10 kt, or the trend shows a significant tendency to exceed either (and thrust is inappropriate).
Hook: "Below Vref or above +10."
x.S082:
FCOM NP.40.14 note: 'verify' = visually confirm correct operation of a system; no verbal response from either crewmember.
Hook: "Verify = eyes, not voice."
x.S083:
Expected EGPWS callout missing → the PM makes it; the PF acknowledges EGPWS callouts.
Hook: "Box silent → PM speaks."
x.U001:
True. The RYR Initial Emergency Briefing (FCOM NP.21.38) sets 80 kt as the dividing line: 'Above 80 knots I will only reject the takeoff for: fire or fire warning, engine failure, predictive windshear warning, airplane unsafe or unable to fly.' So BELOW 80 kt (low speed, low risk) you reject for any significant problem – a flight deck window opening is one of them. Above 80 kt a window opening alone is NOT a reject reason (the airplane can still fly) unless it makes the airplane unsafe.
Hook: "Below 80: stop for anything significant. Above 80: only fire, engine, windshear, unsafe."
x.U002:
Deviation alert: 300 FT away from the selected altitude → tone + current altitude box AMBER FLASHING.
Hook: "Off by 300 → amber flash."
x.U003:
INSTR SWITCH (amber) = the IRS transfer switch on the forward overhead panel is NOT in NORMAL (BOTH ON L or BOTH ON R), so both pilots' displays use the SAME IRU. Not OFF (the switch has no OFF), not the aft overhead.
Hook: "INSTR SWITCH = IRS switch not NORMAL."
x.U004:
In the climb (nose-up) the centre pump LOW PRESSURE lights can illuminate with fuel still in the centre tank, the pumps are switched OFF and the CONFIG alert appears. RYR SOP: only when established in a LEVEL FLIGHT ATTITUDE do you switch the centre pumps back ON. So: don't action the CONFIG checklist until in level flight.
Hook: "CONFIG? Level off first."
x.Q0765v1:
LNAV engagement: within 3 NM of the active leg → ANY heading. Outside 3 NM → must be on an intercept of 90° or less that intercepts BEFORE the active waypoint. Otherwise NOT ON INTERCEPT HEADING.
Hook: "3 NM: any heading; beyond: intercept before the waypoint."
x.Q0851v1:
760 kg > 726 kg with both center pumps OFF (engines running) → amber CONFIG under the CENTER tank gauge. Reminder to switch the center pumps on.
Hook: "CONFIG lives under the center gauge."
x.Q0030v1:
Crew oxygen pressure is read on the CREW OXYGEN pressure indicator on the AFT OVERHEAD panel. It shows the pressure in the crew oxygen cylinder (in the forward cargo area), but you don't go to the cylinder – you check the gauge during the preflight against the dispatch figures. Each crew station has a flow indicator (yellow cross), not a pressure gauge.
Hook: "Crew O2 pressure = aft overhead gauge."
x.Q0062v1:
FCOM list of bleed air users: air conditioning/pressurisation, wing and engine thermal anti-ice, engine starting, hydraulic reservoir pressurisation, and water tank pressurisation (plus the Nitrogen Generation System on later aircraft). The only option with ALL of them, including water, is the correct one – the others each miss one item. Trace them on the bleed schematic: every 'TO …' arrow is a user.
Hook: "PAWS-H: Packs, Anti-ice, Water, Starters, Hydraulics."
x.Q0062v2:
FCOM list of bleed air users: air conditioning/pressurisation, wing and engine thermal anti-ice, engine starting, hydraulic reservoir pressurisation, and water tank pressurisation (plus the Nitrogen Generation System on later aircraft). The only option with ALL of them, including water, is the correct one – the others each miss one item. Trace them on the bleed schematic: every 'TO …' arrow is a user.
Hook: "PAWS-H: Packs, Anti-ice, Water, Starters, Hydraulics."
x.Q0063v1:
All three temperature selectors OFF = Fixed Cabin Temperature mode: the LEFT pack holds 24 °C (75 °F) and the RIGHT pack 18 °C (65 °F), measured at the pack sensor. Option A has the sides swapped. 'Average of all zones' is what a single pack does with TRIM AIR OFF, not this case.
Hook: "Left is warm (24), right is cool (18)."
x.Q0063v2:
All three temperature selectors OFF = Fixed Cabin Temperature mode: the LEFT pack holds 24 °C (75 °F) and the RIGHT pack 18 °C (65 °F), measured at the pack sensor. Option A has the sides swapped. 'Average of all zones' is what a single pack does with TRIM AIR OFF, not this case.
Hook: "Left is warm (24), right is cool (18)."
x.Q0063v3:
All three temperature selectors OFF = Fixed Cabin Temperature mode: the LEFT pack holds 24 °C (75 °F) and the RIGHT pack 18 °C (65 °F), measured at the pack sensor. Option A has the sides swapped. 'Average of all zones' is what a single pack does with TRIM AIR OFF, not this case.
Hook: "Left is warm (24), right is cool (18)."
x.Q0067v1:
If you descend before reaching the FLT ALT (e.g. returning after a malfunction), the controller shows OFF SCHED DESCENT and automatically programs the cabin to land at the TAKEOFF field elevation – no pilot input needed. If you reset the FLT ALT, that automatic abort capability to the departure field is LOST and you must set LAND ALT yourself. Nothing dramatic like a rapid depressurisation happens.
Hook: "Touch FLT ALT = lose the auto return."
x.Q0071v1:
OFF SCHED DESCENT (amber) = the airplane started descending before reaching the cruise altitude set in the FLT ALT window – typically a return to the departure airport. It is not a failure: the controller automatically programs the cabin to land at the takeoff field elevation. Controller failures show as AUTO FAIL (with ALTN = single, alone = dual).
Hook: "Off schedule = descending early, not broken."
x.Q0076v1:
All bleed and air-conditioning lights on the forward overhead panel report to the AIR COND system annunciator on the glareshield: DUAL BLEED, WING-BODY OVERHEAT, BLEED TRIP OFF, PACK, ZONE TEMP, AUTO FAIL, OFF SCHED DESCENT. OVHT/DET is for engine/APU fire detection, OVERHEAD is for things like EMER EXIT NOT ARMED and PASS OXY ON.
Hook: "Anything on the air panel → AIR COND."
x.Q0077v1:
Pressing the WING-BODY OVHT TEST switch (hold at least 5 s) tests the overheat detection circuits: both amber WING-BODY OVERHEAT lights illuminate, plus MASTER CAUTION and the AIR COND annunciator. It doesn't test the duct overheat, bleed trip or pack trip circuits.
Hook: "OVHT TEST → both WING-BODY lights."
x.Q0078v1:
DUAL BLEED (amber) means the valve positions would let ENGINE bleed air back-pressure the APU: APU bleed valve open AND engine 1 BLEED switch ON, or engine 2 BLEED ON with the APU bleed valve and isolation valve open. It comes on normally during engine start (APU bleed still on) – just keep thrust low until the APU bleed is OFF. It's about valve positions, not measured pressure.
Hook: "DUAL BLEED = engine could blow back into the APU."
x.Q0099v1:
One pack (in HIGH flow) can maintain pressurisation AND acceptable temperatures throughout the airplane up to the maximum certified ceiling (41,000 ft). With TRIM AIR ON, zone temperature control works the same as with two packs; only with TRIM AIR OFF does the pack aim for the average of all zones – so D is not the general answer.
Hook: "One pack is enough – all the way to FL410."
x.Q0156v1:
The amber COWL ANTI-ICE light = OVERPRESSURE in the duct downstream of the cowl anti-ice valve (between valve and cowl lip). It is not an over-temperature warning. Valve position is shown by the blue COWL VALVE OPEN light (bright = in transit/disagree, dim = open).
Hook: "Amber COWL = too much pressure."
x.Q0162v1:
WINDOW HEAT test switch: OVHT simulates an OVERHEAT so you can check the warning: amber OVERHEAT lights on, green ON lights out, MASTER CAUTION + ANTI-ICE. The other position, PWR TEST, forces the controller to full power to check the heating works. It isn't a voltage check and isn't limited to flight.
Hook: "OVHT = fake overheat; PWR TEST = full power."
x.Q0183v1:
With both F/Ds ON, both pilots' F/D modes come from the MASTER FCC. If an autopilot is engaged, the master is the FCC of the first A/P engaged in CMD – regardless of which F/D was switched on first. CMD B → FCC B is master → it drives the Captain's F/D too (MA light on the F/O side). Without A/P, the first F/D switched on decides.
Hook: "A/P in CMD wins the master battle."
x.Q0189v1:
The AFDS is a dual system: TWO flight control computers (FCC A and FCC B) and ONE mode control panel. Each FCC drives its own pitch/roll hydraulic servos (through separate hydraulic systems) and its own pilot's F/D bars.
Hook: "Two FCCs (A & B), one MCP."
x.Q0196v1:
Besides pushing the N1 switch, N1 mode engages AUTOMATICALLY when you engage VNAV in a climb, or LVL CHG in a climb – except during the 2½-minute inhibit period after lift-off (to protect a reduced-thrust/ engine-out takeoff from an automatic thrust increase).
Hook: "Auto N1: VNAV climb, LVL CHG climb after 2½ min."
x.Q0198v1:
Each FCC uses its own radio altimeter. With one radio altimeter inoperative, the autopilot disengages TWO SECONDS after LOC and G/S capture – so no autopilot ILS to minimums. Also: dual-channel A/P needs two generators powering the busses.
Hook: "One RA dead → A/P off 2 s after capture."
x.Q0203v1:
Two A/T modes let you move the thrust levers without the A/T fighting: THR HLD (servos inhibited during takeoff) and ARM (no mode engaged, servos inhibited – but minimum speed protection is still provided). In N1, GA, MCP SPD or FMC SPD the A/T drives the levers.
Hook: "Hands-free for you: THR HLD and ARM."
x.Q0207v1:
After lift-off the A/T stays in THR HLD until 800 ft above field elevation (the bank says 800 ft RA), then changes to ARM and you can push N1 for climb thrust. There's no 18-second rule.
Hook: "THR HLD until 800."
x.Q0187v1:
The FMC provides the N1 limits and target N1 to the autothrottle (and command speeds to A/T and AFDS). The A/T uses FMC N1 limits whether the EECs are ON or in ALTN. There is no separate 'autothrottle computer' feeding limits; the EECs control the engine, not the A/T limits.
Hook: "N1 limits come from the FMC."
x.Q0186v1:
AFS = AFDS (autopilot flight director system) + A/T (autothrottle). The MCP and FMC are what CONTROL them, not parts of the AFS. The FMC feeds N1 limits, target N1 and command speeds.
Hook: "AFS = AFDS + A/T."
x.Q0222v1:
SPD INTV during VNAV: the IAS/MACH window opens showing the current FMC TARGET SPEED, which you can then change. Not dashes, not 100 kt (100 kt is only what it shows on first power-up).
Hook: "SPD INTV shows the FMC target."
x.Q0311v1:
STANDBY POWER switch in AUTO: the standby busses switch from normal to battery (alternate) power if power is lost from EITHER AC transfer bus 1 OR DC bus 1 – the '1' side feeds the standby system. Losing DC bus 2 alone doesn't trigger it.
Hook: "Standby watches the No. 1 side: XFR 1 or DC 1."
x.Q0312v1:
Normal: DC STANDBY bus ← TR1, TR2 and TR3; AC STANDBY bus ← AC transfer bus 1; battery bus ← TR3; hot battery buses ← battery/charger. With all AC lost, the battery powers DC standby and (via the static inverter) AC standby.
Hook: "DC standby has all three TRs."
x.Q0313v1:
After loss of all engine/APU AC power, the standby system gives 115 V AC (from the battery through the static inverter, on the AC standby bus) and 24 V DC (battery: DC standby bus, battery bus, hot battery buses). 22–30 V is just the battery's voltage range.
Hook: "Standby = 115 AC + 24 DC."
x.Q0315v1:
DC bus 1 and DC bus 2 are isolated when the cross bus tie relay opens, which happens automatically at G/S capture on an F/D or A/P ILS approach (so one failure can't take out both nav receivers/FCCs) and when the BUS TRANSFER switch is OFF. So all answers are true.
Hook: "GS capture or BUS TRANSFER OFF → DC busses split."
x.Q0316v1:
Generator DISCONNECT (guarded): disconnects the IDG from the engine (needs electrical power and start lever at IDLE) and the amber DRIVE light comes on (IDG low oil pressure). It can only be reconnected on the ground by maintenance. The transfer bus then gets power via the BTBs from another source.
Hook: "DISCONNECT = DRIVE light, no way back in flight."
x.Q0318v1:
With all AC lost, the AC standby bus is fed by the STATIC INVERTER, which converts 24 V DC from the battery into 115 V AC. TRs do the opposite (AC → DC).
Hook: "Inverter: battery DC → standby AC."
x.Q0320v1:
Red guards mark switches whose action can't be undone in flight – the IDG DISCONNECT can only be reset on the ground by maintenance. So: red guard = irreversible.
Hook: "Red guard = no undo."
x.Q0328v1:
IRS power: LEFT IRS ← AC standby bus; RIGHT IRS ← AC transfer bus 2. Both switch automatically to DC from the SWITCHED HOT BATTERY bus if AC fails (ON DC light) – but the RIGHT IRS backup is cut after 5 minutes to save the battery. So on standby power you keep the left IRS.
Hook: "Right IRS: XFR 2, battery 5 min only."
x.Q0342v1:
Batteries are 24 V Ni-Cd (range 22–30 V). When AC is available, the battery charger/TRs hold the DC system at about 28 V. With NO AC power, nothing charges the battery, so the DC voltmeter on BAT shows the battery's own voltage — LESS than 28 V (around 24 V, decreasing as it discharges).
Hook: "No AC = no charger = below 28."
x.Q0343v1:
The SWITCHED hot battery bus is fed from the battery THROUGH the BATTERY switch (look at the schematic on 6.20.10: the battery switch sits between the battery and the switched hot bat bus). STANDBY POWER to BAT puts the AC standby, DC standby and battery bus on the battery even with the battery switch OFF — but the switched hot battery bus is NOT powered if the battery switch is OFF. (The plain hot battery bus is always powered.)
Hook: "'Switched' = needs the battery switch ON."
x.Q0364v1:
DC busses run at 28 V DC (TR output). AC is 115 V (400 Hz). Batteries are 24 V nominal (22–30 V).
Hook: "AC 115, DC 28, battery 24."
x.Q0414v1:
APU fuel feed: with AC fuel pumps running → from the LEFT side of the fuel manifold (so any running pump that feeds the left side, incl. center tank pumps / crossfeed). With no AC pumps → suction fed from MAIN TANK No 1. That's why, for an APU start without AC, a main tank 1 pump isn't needed.
Hook: "APU drinks from the left."
x.Q0426v1:
Abnormal start protection (hot start, stall, EGT exceedance, wet start → auto cutoff) works on GROUND STARTS ONLY. In flight there is NO automatic protection — the crew monitors and moves the lever to CUTOFF if needed.
Hook: "EEC babysits ground starts only."
x.Q0431v1:
Wet start = no EGT rise after the start lever goes to IDLE (fuel in, no light-off). On a GROUND start the EEC turns off ignition and fuel 15 SECONDS after the START LEVER (not the thrust lever) is moved to IDLE. In flight: no protection.
Hook: "Wet start: 15 seconds, then EEC cuts it."
x.Q0454v1:
Yes — a BATTERY START is possible: the start switch uses BATTERY power to open the start valve; you only need an AIR source (ground cart, APU bleed, other engine). The EEC powers up from its own alternator at 15% N2. Battery switch must be ON (start switch circuit needs it).
Hook: "No AC? Air + battery is enough."
x.Q0468v1:
Outboard DU fails → PFD AUTOMATICALLY moves to the INBOARD DU (the PFD always has priority). Inboard DU fails → PFD stays outboard. Upper DU fails → engines move to the lower DU.
Hook: "The PFD always survives — it jumps inboard."
x.Q0487v1:
ISDU DSPL SEL HDG/STS: left window = TRUE HEADING; right window = maintenance status codes, and DURING ALIGNMENT the MINUTES REMAINING (shows 15 until 14 remain, then counts down). Other positions: TK/GS (track, groundspeed), PPOS (lat/long), WIND (true wind dir/speed in flight).
Hook: "HDG/STS: heading left, minutes-to-go right."
x.Q0512v1:
FWD WINDOW HEAT switch → window No 1 only (L1/R1, the windshield). SIDE → window No 2. Window No 3 is acrylic and not electrically heated (it gets warm air). So LEFT FWD = L1 only.
Hook: "FWD = 1, SIDE = 2, 3 = none."
x.Q0518v1:
APU switch OFF = 60 s delay, not immediate. Battery switch OFF → ECU loses power → APU stops at once (bank answer B). The FCOM's own 'immediate shutdown' method is PULLING the APU fire switch (option A says ROTATE, which fires the bottle — wrong wording).
Hook: "Immediate APU stop: pull fire switch / battery OFF — not the APU switch."
x.Q0649v1:
Don't extend flaps above 20,000 ft — at high altitude the same IAS means higher Mach → excessive structural loads. (Also a limitation: max flap extension altitude 20,000 ft.)
Hook: "Flaps: below FL200."
x.Q0652v1:
FCOM 9.10.11 uses "OR": the light comes on for EITHER condition (not both at the same time). The correct option is the one that lists both possible meanings. SPEED BRAKE DO NOT ARM (amber) has two meanings: (1) abnormal condition or test input in the auto speedbrake system; (2) after landing, wheel speed below 60 kt and the speedbrake lever NOT yet DOWN (reminder to stow). Deactivated with the lever DOWN.
Hook: "DO NOT ARM = fault, or 'stow the lever' below 60 kt."
x.Q0653v1:
Lever left DOWN (forgot to arm) on landing/RTO: the auto speedbrake still works when wheels spin up > 60 kt, both thrust levers at IDLE, AND the REVERSE THRUST levers are raised. Then the SPEED BRAKE lever moves UP automatically and all spoilers deploy. Advancing a thrust lever afterwards retracts them.
Hook: "Forgot to arm? Pull reverse — spoilers follow."
x.Q0654v1:
ALTERNATE FLAPS master switch ARM: closes the TE flap BYPASS valve (prevents hydraulic lock of the flap drive), activates the STANDBY PUMP and arms the ALTERNATE FLAPS position switch. The red guard warns: once you push DOWN, the LE devices go to FULL EXTEND on standby pressure and CANNOT BE RETRACTED by the standby system. (TE flaps can still be moved up and down electrically.)
Hook: "Red guard: LE devices out for good."
x.Q0707v1:
Magenta readout above the speed tape = TARGET speed: the speed in the MCP IAS/MACH window, or the FMC speed when the window is blank (VNAV). Magenta = selected/target throughout the PFD.
Hook: "Magenta = what you asked for."
x.Q0707v2:
Magenta readout above the speed tape = TARGET speed: the speed in the MCP IAS/MACH window, or the FMC speed when the window is blank (VNAV). Magenta = selected/target throughout the PFD.
Hook: "Magenta = what you asked for."
x.Q0728v1:
