IRS alignment lost in flight → NAV mode (position, groundspeed) dead for the rest of the flight. Select ATT: after ~30 s of straight, level, unaccelerated flight it relevels and gives ATTITUDE (and heading once you enter magnetic heading on POS INIT). ALIGN can't be used in flight.
Hook: "Lost NAV in flight → ATT, fly level 30 s, enter heading."
x.Q0728v2:
IRS alignment lost in flight → NAV mode (position, groundspeed) dead for the rest of the flight. Select ATT: after ~30 s of straight, level, unaccelerated flight it relevels and gives ATTITUDE (and heading once you enter magnetic heading on POS INIT). ALIGN can't be used in flight.
Hook: "Lost NAV in flight → ATT, fly level 30 s, enter heading."
x.Q0732v1:
Changing the active NAV DATA (only possible on the GROUND) ERASES all previously entered route data → RTE page blank, re-enter the route. If the database expires in flight, it keeps being used until changed after landing.
Hook: "New database = blank route."
x.Q0733v1:
IntuVue PWS: detection works automatically below 1,800 ft AGL, but ALERTS are available at 1,200 FT and below (same 1,200 ft as the older radar). Warning gives 10–60 s.
Hook: "Detect from 1800, alert from 1200."
x.Q0742v1:
FQIS failure → VERIFY GW AND FUEL, PERF INIT fuel dashes; FMC uses last valid fuel. Crew must ENTER estimated fuel and UPDATE it periodically (reminder every 30 min) to keep gross weight and VNAV performance correct. VNAV doesn't disengage.
Hook: "FQIS dead → you are the fuel gauge, every 30 min."
x.Q0743v1:
IntuVue windshear mode auto-activates: IN THE AIR below 1,800 ft AGL, or ON THE GROUND with thrust levers at takeoff setting. (Alerts: 1,200 ft and below.)
Hook: "1800 air, takeoff thrust ground."
x.Q0753v1:
The CVR ERASE switch (red, on the forward overhead CVR panel) erases all four channels when pushed for 2 seconds, BUT only works with the airplane ON THE GROUND AND THE PARKING BRAKE SET. Never in flight — this protects the recording for accident investigation.
Hook: "Erase = 2 sec + ground + parking brake."
x.Q0756v1:
BUFFET ALERT (flaps up only): current conditions give a MANEUVER MARGIN LESS THAN SPECIFIED (normally 1.3 g to buffet). Get back into the envelope (speed/altitude).
Hook: "BUFFET ALERT = not enough g margin."
x.Q0769v1:
IRS in ATT: ATTITUDE, and HEADING once you enter the initial magnetic heading (it drifts up to 15°/h — cross-check with the compass and update). No position or groundspeed.
Hook: "ATT = attitude + heading (if you give it one)."
x.Q0832v1:
Fuel measuring sticks (magnetic dipsticks under the wing): 6 in EACH main tank + 4 in the center = 16.
Hook: "6 + 6 + 4 = 16."
x.Q0833v1:
Imbalance (QRH FUEL IMBALANCE): CROSSFEED OPEN, fuel pumps of the LOW tank OFF → both engines feed from the HIGH tank until balanced, then pumps ON and crossfeed CLOSED. Fuel isn't transferred between tanks — it's burned from the heavy side. There's no IMBAL 'warning light' (it's a DU alert).
Hook: "Open crossfeed, switch off the light side."
x.Q0838v1:
Each tank has TWO AC pumps (6 total), cooled/lubricated by fuel. A center tank SCAVENGE JET PUMP moves remaining center fuel into MAIN TANK 1 (starts when tank 1 is about half; needs No 1 FWD pump ON). Pump mounting locations (center pumps on the rear spar, main pumps fwd/aft) are bank details, not in the FCOM.
Hook: "2 pumps each + a jet pump to tank 1."
x.Q0002v1:
FCOM 12.20.2 'Suction Feed': 'When main tank fuel pump pressure is low, each engine can draw fuel from its corresponding main tank through a suction feed line that bypasses the pumps.' On the schematic (12.20.5) this is the ENGINE BYPASS VALVE in each main tank. So No 1 engine keeps running on fuel from the No 1 tank, sucked by its engine-driven pump through the bypass. It does NOT flame out. At high altitude suction feed may not be able to give full thrust (air comes out of the fuel).
Hook: "Both pumps dead → engine sucks through the bypass."
x.Q0840v1:
Pulling the engine fire switch closes BOTH the ENGINE fuel shutoff valve AND the SPAR fuel shutoff valve (exactly like the start lever to CUTOFF). It never discharges automatically — you must ROTATE. (Power: spar valve DC motor from hot battery bus; engine valve solenoid from battery bus.)
Hook: "Pull = both fuel valves shut; rotate = bottle."
x.Q0003v1:
FCOM 12.20.3: the centre tank scavenge jet pump (with No 1 FWD pump switch ON) moves the last centre-tank fuel into main tank No 1, and 'Fuel transfer begins when main tank No. 1 quantity is about one-half.' Once started, it continues for the rest of the flight.
Hook: "Tank 1 half empty → scavenge starts."
x.Q0863v1:
All tanks full, all pumps ON → BOTH engines fed from the CENTER tank (higher pressure pumps) until near empty, then each engine from its own main tank. Check valves prevent fuel transferring between tanks.
Hook: "Center first, then own wing."
x.Q0899v1:
System A: ailerons, rudder, elevator & feel, flight spoilers 2-4-9-11, ALL ground spoilers, ALTERNATE brakes, No 1 reverser, A/P A, NORMAL nose wheel steering, LANDING GEAR, gear transfer valve, PTU. System B: TE flaps/LE devices, NORMAL brakes, ALTERNATE NWS, No 2 reverser, A/P B, yaw damper, autoslats, gear transfer backup.
Hook: "A = gear, steering, ground spoilers, PTU. B = flaps, brakes."
x.Q0899v2:
System A: ailerons, rudder, elevator & feel, flight spoilers 2-4-9-11, ALL ground spoilers, ALTERNATE brakes, No 1 reverser, A/P A, NORMAL nose wheel steering, LANDING GEAR, gear transfer valve, PTU. System B: TE flaps/LE devices, NORMAL brakes, ALTERNATE NWS, No 2 reverser, A/P B, yaw damper, autoslats, gear transfer backup.
Hook: "A = gear, steering, ground spoilers, PTU. B = flaps, brakes."
x.Q0902v1:
Landing gear transfer valve (system B EDP raises the gear) ALL of: airborne, No 1 ENGINE RPM below a limit (not the EDP), gear lever UP, EITHER MAIN gear not up and locked. Typical case: engine 1 fails on takeoff.
Hook: "Engine 1 slow + gear up selected + main not locked → B raises the gear."
x.Q0903v1:
RF (white) next to hydraulic quantity = below 76%. Valid only on the ground with both engines shut down, or after landing with flaps up during taxi-in.
Hook: "RF = refill, below 76."
x.Q0905v1:
System B raises the gear after FAILURE OF No 1 ENGINE (RPM below limit), gear still down, lever UP. Triggered by engine RPM, not by the EDP or system A pressure.
Hook: "Engine 1 lost on takeoff → B raises the gear."
x.Q0908v1:
Landing gear transfer unit: uses system B to raise the gear at normal rate if No 1 ENGINE is lost (RPM below limit) with gear lever UP and a main gear not locked.
Hook: "Engine 1 lost → B raises the gear."
x.Q0909v1:
System B leak → quantity to ~0 and pressure lost (one standpipe for both pumps). But the fluid BELOW the standpipe stays in the reservoir and is enough for the PTU. (System A: standpipe saves ~20% for the electric pump.)
Hook: "B leak: pumps starve, PTU still has its reserve."
x.Q0913v1:
Standby leak: standby reservoir → 0 (LOW QUANTITY at half). System B (which refills the standby reservoir) keeps working but its quantity drops and stabilizes at ≈70% (bank answer 72%).
Hook: "Standby leak → B shows ~70%."
x.Q0917v1:
EDP ≈ 6× the volume of the electric pump. A = EDP on engine 1 + ELEC 2; B = EDP on engine 2 + ELEC 1 (crossed for redundancy).
Hook: "EDP = 6 electric pumps."
x.Q0929v1:
ENG pump OFF: isolates the fluid flow from the system (blocking valve energized); the pump KEEPS ROTATING with the engine — no clutch/disconnect.
Hook: "OFF blocks the output; pump keeps spinning."
x.Q0944v1:
B leak → NO effect on the standby system (own reservoir/pump; B link only for pressurization/servicing). Bank wording 'own accumulator' is loose but 'no effect' is the key.
Hook: "B dies, standby lives."
x.Q0950v1:
Poorly written bank question: the answer '3500 psi in white' is the maximum HYDRAULIC SYSTEM pressure (lower DU). The real HYD BRAKE PRESS gauge: precharge 1000, normal 2900–3600, max 3600–4000 psi.
Hook: "System 3000/3500; brake accumulator up to 4000."
x.Q0978v1:
Manual extension access door OPEN: manual extension possible with the lever in ANY position; NORMAL extension still possible with system A; RETRACTION DISABLED. → all true. To retract after a manual extension: close door, lever DOWN with A pressure, then UP.
Hook: "Door open: can drop, can't raise."
x.Q0978v2:
Manual extension access door OPEN: manual extension possible with the lever in ANY position; NORMAL extension still possible with system A; RETRACTION DISABLED. → all true. To retract after a manual extension: close door, lever DOWN with A pressure, then UP.
Hook: "Door open: can drop, can't raise."
x.Q0980v1:
Autobrake disarm (DISARM light) after braking started: SPEED BRAKE lever to DOWN, advancing thrust lever(s) EXCEPT in the first 3 s after touchdown, or MANUAL BRAKES. Selector OFF disarms without the light. So 'advancing immediately after touchdown' does NOT disarm → D.
Hook: "Speedbrake down, manual brakes, throttles (after 3 s)."
x.Q0981v1:
NWS: system A normally; available only with nose gear DOWN and COMPRESSED (weight on wheels). Alternate = SYSTEM B (not standby) — and lost if B fluid is lost downstream of the gear transfer unit.
Hook: "Steering needs weight on the nose; ALT is B."
x.Q0981v2:
NWS: system A normally; available only with nose gear DOWN and COMPRESSED (weight on wheels). Alternate = SYSTEM B (not standby) — and lost if B fluid is lost downstream of the gear transfer unit.
Hook: "Steering needs weight on the nose; ALT is B."
x.Q0982v1:
Manual gear extension handles (right main, nose, left main): pull each to its LIMIT — about 24 in / 61 CM — to release the uplock; gear free-falls (gravity + air loads).
Hook: "Pull 61 cm."
x.Q0986v1:
Yes: a gear is down and locked if ONE green light for it (centre panel OR aft overhead) is illuminated. Two independent indication sets.
Hook: "One green per gear is enough."
x.Q1010v1:
Altitude alerting INHIBITED with TE FLAPS ≥ 25 or G/S CAPTURED (it would be a nuisance on approach). Alert window: 900 ft (white box, tone) to 300 ft; deviation > 300 ft → amber flashing.
Hook: "Flaps 25 or G/S → no altitude alerts."
x.Q1020v1:
With TA/RA selected, below 1,000 ft RA TCAS automatically goes TA ONLY (message on ND).
Hook: "Below 1000 → TA only."
x.Q1025v1:
TCAS symbols: PROXIMATE = SOLID WHITE diamond (within 6 NM and 1,200 ft, no threat); OTHER = hollow white diamond; TA = amber filled circle; RA = red filled square.
Hook: "Solid white = close but harmless."
x.Q1026v1:
TA ≈ 40 s from closest point of approach; RA ≈ 25 s. No RA without the intruder's altitude.
Hook: "TA 40, RA 25."
x.Q1033v1:
ALT DISAGREE = Captain and F/O altitudes differ by more than 200 FT for more than 5 SECONDS.
Hook: "IAS 5/5, ALT 200/5, AOA 10/10."
x.Q1034v1:
Amber ROLL (or PITCH) on the PFD = attitude COMPARATOR: Captain's and F/O's roll (pitch) displays differ by MORE THAN 5°. Flashes 10 s then steady. It says nothing about which side is wrong — cross-check with the standby (ISFD).
Hook: "PITCH/ROLL amber = the two attitudes disagree by 5°."
x.Q1041v1:
Limitations (L.10.6), Non-AFM operational info: on the ground use the VHF radio connected to the TOP-of-fuselage antenna for primary ATC. On the 737 that is VHF-1 (VHF-2 uses the bottom antenna, which can be shielded by the fuselage/terminal buildings on the ground).
Hook: "On the ground, talk through the top: VHF 1."
x.Q1051v1:
Amber PITCH = Captain and F/O pitch displays differ by more than 5°.
Hook: "PITCH/ROLL amber = 5° disagreement."
x.Q1057v1:
Overwing exit flight lock failed locked (or PSEU fault) → PSEU + OVERHEAD + MASTER CAUTION, but INHIBITED from takeoff until 30 s after ground mode → appears 30 s after landing.
Hook: "PSEU waits 30 s after landing."
x.Q1061v1:
TAKEOFF CONFIG (intermittent horn) on thrust advance if: flaps not in takeoff range (1–25) or asymmetry/skew, LE devices not right, speed brake lever not DOWN, spoiler valve open, PARKING BRAKE SET, STAB TRIM outside the green band. Flaps 5 is valid.
Hook: "Flaps, slats, speedbrake, park brake, trim."
x.Q1069v1:
GLIDESLOPE alert: louder/faster with more deviation. Cancel = push either pilot's BELOW G/S P-INHIBIT light (below 1,000 ft RA) or fly back to the glideslope. RECALL does nothing to aurals.
Hook: "Push BELOW G/S or fix the path."
